content.rendered:
India’s beer market spans legacy lagers, high-ABV strong beers, and a rapidly growing craft beer segment. From mass-market Indian brands to premium international labels, Indian consumers today enjoy a wide spectrum of beer styles.

The table below compares 25 popular beer brands in India (both Indian and international) based on style, alcohol content (ABV), and typical price range in Delhi. Detailed brand profiles follow after the table.

1. Kingfisher (India)

Buy Beer Glass

India’s best-known beer brand, Kingfisher, is a range of pale lagers brewed by United Breweries. Its flagship Kingfisher Premium, a light lager, is prized for its crisp, refreshing taste and mild hop character. For consumers who prefer higher alcohol strength, Kingfisher Strong and Kingfisher Ultra variants offer increased ABV levels.

Kingfisher Premium contains approximately 4.8% ABV, while Kingfisher Strong goes up to around 8% ABV. The brand is widely appreciated for its easy drinkability and its ability to pair exceptionally well with spicy Indian cuisine.

Kingfisher has also earned international recognition, with Kingfisher Ultra winning Gold at the World Beer Awards 2025 (India country winner, international lager category), while Kingfisher Premium and Strong secured Silver medals.

Top 26 Best Whiskey Brands in India (Updated-List)

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Lager (Premium, Strong, Ultra)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~4.8%–8%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Light and malt-forward with gentle hop bitterness
    • Ultra and Strong variants are smoother, richer, and more malty
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold in a chilled glass
    • Pairs especially well with spicy Indian dishes
  • Awards:
    • Multiple World Beer Awards 2025 medals
    • Ultra – Gold
    • Premium and Strong – Silver
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹110 (500 ml Premium can)
    • Up to ₹145 (650 ml Strong)
  • Other Variants:
    • Kingfisher Premium – 4.8% ABV, ₹140 (650 ml)
    • Kingfisher Strong – 8% ABV, ₹145 (650 ml)
    • Kingfisher Ultra – 5% ABV, ~₹160 (650 ml)
    • Kingfisher Ultra Max – 7% ABV, ~₹160 (650 ml)

2. Budweiser (International – AB InBev)

Buy Beer Glass

Budweiser is a globally popular American-style pale lager widely sold in India by AB InBev. The classic Budweiser Premium is a smooth, medium-bodied lager with 5% ABV, offering mild toasted malt notes and subtle hop bitterness.

For consumers who prefer a stronger taste, Budweiser Magnum delivers 6.5% ABV with a bolder flavor profile. Budweiser Premium pairs especially well with grilled foods, pizzas, and classic bar snacks.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • American Pale Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 5.0% (Premium)
    • 6.5% (Magnum)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Clean malt base
    • Slightly grainy texture
    • Well-balanced hop bitterness
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled, preferably in a glass bottle
    • Complements kebabs, pizzas, and bar snacks
  • Awards:
    • Globally acclaimed brand (no specific India awards noted)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹170 (Premium 650 ml)
    • ₹195 (Magnum 650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Budweiser Premium – 650 ml
    • Budweiser Magnum – Strong lager, 650 ml

3. Corona Extra (Mexico)

Buy Beer Glass

Corona Extra is a light Mexican pale lager with 4.6% ABV, known for its extremely crisp and refreshing character. It has low bitterness and a slightly sweet, easy finish that appeals to casual and premium beer drinkers alike.

Traditionally served ice-cold with a wedge of lime, Corona enhances its subtle citrus notes and is widely popular in India’s bars, lounges, and resorts as a “beach-style” beer.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Pale Lager (Light Import)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 4.6%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Very light-bodied
    • Low hop bitterness
    • Clean, mildly sweet malty finish
  • Best Served:
    • Extremely cold, often with lime
    • Excellent with seafood and spicy dishes
  • Awards:
    • No major India-specific awards
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹280 (330–355 ml bottle)
  • Other Variants:
    • Corona Light – 4.1% ABV, ~₹280 (355 ml)
    • Corona Sunset – Flavored variant with orange peel

4. Carlsberg Elephant (Denmark / India)

Buy Beer Glass

Carlsberg Elephant is Carlsberg India’s flagship strong lager with 7% ABV and ranks among the highest-selling premium strong beers in India. It pours a bright golden color with a thick foamy head and delivers a rich, malty body balanced by a pleasing dry bitterness.

For drinkers seeking a smoother alternative, Carlsberg All-Malt (5% ABV) offers a cleaner and more refined taste. Elephant’s sweet malt aroma and warmth make it a popular choice for celebrations and festive occasions.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Strong Lager (Super Premium)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 7.0%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Full-bodied malt
    • Subtle piney hop notes
    • Dry, lingering bitterness
  • Best Served:
    • Well chilled
    • Pairs excellently with spicy curries and fried snacks
  • Awards:
    • Known for strong market leadership (no recent awards cited)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹165 (650 ml Elephant Strong)
    • ~₹160 (650 ml All-Malt)
  • Other Variants:
    • Carlsberg Elephant Strong – 7% ABV
    • Carlsberg All-Malt – 5% ABV

5. Foster’s (Australia)

Buy Beer Glass

Foster’s is an Australian lager brewed in India under Carlsberg India. Foster’s Lager is a light golden beer with approximately 6.9–7% ABV, featuring a solid malt backbone and a clean hop finish.

The Foster’s Strong Premium variant offers a slightly bolder taste while remaining smooth and easy-drinking. The beer is known for its mild botanical aroma, moderate bitterness, and refreshing finish.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Pale Lager (Standard and Strong)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~7% (Lager)
    • 6.9–7% (Strong Premium)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Light malt-forward body
    • Balanced hop bitterness
    • Floral and herbal notes
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold
    • Goes well with light snacks and pizzas
  • Awards:
    • No notable awards reported
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹115 (Lager 650 ml)
    • ~₹120 (Strong 650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Foster’s Lager
    • Foster’s Strong Premium

6. Heineken (Netherlands / India)

Buy Beer Glass

Heineken is brewed locally in India and retains its classic Dutch lager character. With 5% ABV, it is a crisp pale lager that is notably hoppier and more bitter than many Indian mass-market beers, giving it a distinct bite.

Its clean, refreshing taste makes it especially popular when served ice-cold. In India, Heineken is often enjoyed straight from the green bottle or occasionally with lime or ice.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Pale Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 5.0%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Light to medium-bodied
    • Pronounced hop bitterness
    • Crisp, refreshing finish
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled (sometimes over ice)
    • Pairs well with seafood, salads, and light curries
  • Awards:
    • No major awards noted
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹200 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Heineken Light – Alcohol-reduced variant

7. Tuborg (Denmark / India)

Buy Beer Glass

Tuborg is another popular brand from Carlsberg India. Tuborg Green (4.6% ABV) is a mild, refreshing lager with delicate floral and grain aromas, light bitterness, and an affordable price point.

For those who prefer stronger beers, Tuborg Strong Premium offers 7–8% ABV, catering to Indian taste preferences. Tuborg is widely positioned as an easy, pocket-friendly everyday beer.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Lager (Green / Strong Premium)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 4.6% (Green)
    • ~7–8% (Strong)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Mild malt sweetness
    • Subtle floral and grain notes
    • Moderate bitterness
  • Best Served:
    • Cold
    • Green variant with light snacks or salads
    • Strong variant with spicy food
  • Awards:
    • No major awards reported
  • Price (Delhi):
    • Tuborg Green – ~₹90 (650 ml)
    • Tuborg Strong – ~₹120 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Tuborg Green Lager
    • Tuborg Strong Premium

8. Stella Artois (Belgium)

Buy Beer Glass

Stella Artois is a premium Belgian pale lager with 5.2% ABV, imported and marketed by AB InBev. It is known for its bright golden color, moderate malt sweetness, soft hop character, and a smooth, slightly bitter finish.

In India, Stella Artois is typically served extremely cold and is sometimes enjoyed with ice, especially in upscale bars and lounges. Its refined profile makes it a popular choice for premium occasions.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Belgian Pale Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 5.2%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Crisp malt backbone
    • Light floral and subtle spice notes
    • Clean, gentle bitterness
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold (often with ice)
    • Ideal with bar snacks, grilled meats, and light appetizers
  • Awards:
    • Classic global brand (no India-specific awards noted)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹280 (330 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Stella Artois Cidre (Apple cider)
    • Stella Midnight Lager (seasonal, higher strength)

9. Hoegaarden (Belgium)

Buy Beer Glass

Hoegaarden is a renowned Belgian wheat beer (witbier) with 4.9% ABV, instantly recognizable for its cloudy appearance and smooth, aromatic profile. Brewed with coriander seeds and orange peel, it delivers a refreshing citrus-spice character with mild sweetness and very low bitterness.

The beer is unfiltered and pours with yeast sediment, making it exceptionally smooth and easy-drinking. It is best enjoyed well chilled, often with a slice of lemon.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Belgian White Wheat Beer (Witbier)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 4.9%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Citrus and spice (orange peel, coriander)
    • Soft wheat sweetness
    • Low bitterness
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold in a glass
    • Pairs well with seafood, salads, and mildly spiced foods
  • Awards:
    • Legendary international classic (no recent India-specific awards)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹280 (330 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Hoegaarden Rosée (strawberry-flavored)
    • Hoegaarden 0.0 (non-alcoholic)

10. Bira 91 (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Bira 91 is one of India’s most successful homegrown craft beer brands, known for innovative and approachable beer styles. Its most popular offerings include Bira Blonde (4.0% lager) and Bira White (4.9% wheat beer).

Bira beers are lightly fruity, mildly spicy, and low in bitterness, making them widely appealing. The brand also produces Boom, a strong lager, along with IPAs, stouts, and fruit-infused variants.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Lager, Witbier, IPA, Stout
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 4.0% (Blonde Lager)
    • 4.9% (White Wheat Beer)
    • ~6–7% (Boom Strong Lager)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Blonde: light, clean malt
    • White: citrusy and spicy (clove, coriander)
    • Boom: toasty malt with higher alcohol warmth
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled
    • Blonde with pizza and snacks
    • White with salads or grilled chicken
    • Boom with hearty curries
  • Awards:
    • 9 medals at the World Beer Awards 2024
    • Including “World’s Best Strong Lager” for Boom
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹355 (Blonde Lager, 650 ml)
    • ~₹220 (White Wheat Beer, 330 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Blonde Lager
    • White Wheat Ale
    • Boom Strong Lager
    • Malabar Stout
    • Rise IPA
    • Fruit-flavored brews (Mango, Berry)

11. Simba (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Simba is a premium Indian craft brewery known for bold, internationally inspired styles. Its flagship Simba Stout, India’s first bottled stout, has 4.5% ABV and features rich notes of coffee, toffee, and dark chocolate with a creamy texture and dry finish.

Simba also produces a Belgian-style Witbier with orange peel and coriander aromas, along with lagers and lighter styles.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Belgian-style Witbier, Lager, Stout
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~4.5% (Stout)
    • ~4.5–5% (Wit and Lager)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Stout: roasted coffee and dark chocolate
    • Wit: bright citrus and spice
    • Lager: light, crisp malt
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled in a pint glass
    • Stout with rich meats or dark gravies
    • Wit with salads or grilled chicken
  • Awards:
    • World Beer Awards 2025 – India category
    • Wit – Silver
    • Stout – Bronze
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹130 (750 ml Stout can)
    • ~₹100 (Wit, 330 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Simba Stout
    • Simba Wit
    • Simba Lager
    • Simba Light

12. White Owl (India)

Buy Beer Glass

White Owl is a New Delhi–based craft beer brand by Globus Spirits, known for experimental flavors and premium brewing. Popular offerings include Spark (citrus wheat ale), Diablo (Irish-style red ale), and Ace (apple cider).

White Owl Diablo (5% ABV) is particularly popular for its roasted caramel notes, smooth body, and low bitterness.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Craft Ales and Ciders
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~5% (most variants)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Diablo: caramel malt, smooth finish
    • Spark: bright citrus wheat
    • Halcyon: fruity and aromatic
  • Best Served:
    • Cold
    • Diablo with BBQ and grilled foods
    • Spark with salads or seafood
  • Awards:
    • Established craft brand (specific awards not cited)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹160 (330 ml Diablo)
    • Spark ~₹160 (330 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Spark Wheat Ale
    • Halcyon Fruit Ale
    • Shadow Imperial Stout
    • Ace Apple Cider

13. White Rhino (India)

Buy Beer Glass

White Rhino is India’s first fully bottled craft brewery, based in Gwalior. Its beers are 100% malted and traditionally brewed, offering clean and balanced profiles across styles such as witbier, lager, pale ale, and IPA.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Craft Wheat Beer, Lager, Pale Ale, IPA
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~5% (most variants)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Wit: soft, fruity, clove-like
    • Lager: crisp malt
    • IPA: citrus-forward hops
    • Pale Ale: balanced malt and hops
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold
    • Wit with light appetizers
    • IPA with spicy foods
  • Awards:
    • No major awards cited
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹170 (330 ml pint)
  • Other Variants:
    • White Rhino Wit
    • White Rhino Lager
    • White Rhino IPA
    • White Rhino Pale Ale

14. Lone Wolf (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Lone Wolf is a rapidly growing Delhi/NCR-based craft beer brand known for premium lagers and ales. Its popular offerings include Lone Wolf Strong, Alpha, and Maverick. Lone Wolf Strong, at around 8% ABV, delivers a smooth yet powerful malt-driven experience.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Craft Lagers and Ales
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 4.5%–8%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Strong: toasty malt, piney hops
    • Alpha: crisp citrus notes
    • Maverick: lightly sweet malt character
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled
    • Strong with hearty meals
    • Lighter variants with salads or seafood
  • Awards:
    • No major awards noted
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹110 (500 ml can)
  • Other Variants:
    • Lone Wolf Strong
    • Alpha
    • Maverick

15. Kati Patang (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Kati Patang is a boutique Delhi brewpub brand known for creative beers infused with Indian ingredients. Signature brews include Zesty Amber Ale, Snappy Wheat, and Saffron Lager, typically ranging between 5–6% ABV.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Craft Ale and Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~5%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Amber Ale: caramel malt, orange-peel hops
    • Spiced Wheat: fruity spice notes
    • Saffron Lager: delicate floral saffron undertones
  • Best Served:
    • Cold
    • Amber Ale with hearty foods
    • Spiced Wheat with tandoori dishes
    • Saffron Lager with mild curries
  • Awards:
    • Regional brewpub acclaim
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹170 per 330 ml pint
  • Other Variants:
    • Zesty Amber Ale
    • Snappy Wheat
    • Saffron Lager

16. Three Cheers (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Three Cheers is a value-focused Indian strong lager brand by United Breweries. It is brewed with high alcohol content and positioned for drinkers seeking strength at an affordable price point.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Ultra Strong Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~7–8% (estimated)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Mild malt sweetness
    • Low hop bitterness
    • Strong alcoholic punch
  • Best Served:
    • Ice cold
    • Pairs well with spicy Indian foods
  • Awards:
    • None noted
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹160 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Three Cheers Ultra Lager

17. Knock Out (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Knock Out is a super-strong lager brewed by United Breweries (Mysore) with a formidable 8% ABV, making it one of India’s strongest packaged beers. It pours a light golden color and delivers a mild bitterness with a noticeable malty aroma, followed by a pronounced alcohol punch.

The brand enjoys strong popularity in South India and neighboring states, particularly among consumers seeking high strength at a competitive price.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Super Strong Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 8.0%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Grainy malt sweetness
    • Gentle hop aroma
    • Strong alcohol warmth
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled
    • Complements spicy snacks such as fried chicken and kebabs
  • Awards:
    • No major awards noted
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹170 (1000 ml bottle)
  • Other Variants:
    • Marketed primarily as a single flagship product

18. Bad Monkey (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Bad Monkey is a Delhi-based super-strong lager brand launched in 2018, known for its bold branding and 8% ABV strength. The beer is golden in appearance, mildly sweet, and surprisingly smooth despite its high alcohol content.

It is positioned for “bold flavor lovers” and has quickly gained popularity among younger, urban consumers.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Super Strong Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 8.0%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Full-bodied and malt-forward
    • Slight sweetness
    • Very low bitterness for its strength
  • Best Served:
    • Cold
    • Works well with barbecue and hearty Indian meals
  • Awards:
    • No awards reported to date
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹180 (500 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Currently sold as a flagship product (flavored variants may be introduced)

19. Maka Di (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Maka Di, meaning “Give me” in Konkani, is a Goa-based craft brewery producing small-batch artisanal beers inspired by European styles and local ingredients. Its range includes Belgian Tripel, Bavarian Keller, Belgian Blanche, and Honey Ale, with alcohol levels varying across styles.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Craft Lagers and Ales (Tripel, Blanche, Keller, Honey Ale)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 5%–8% (varies by variant)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Tripel: spicy fruit and yeast character
    • Honey Ale: sweet malt and floral honey notes
    • Blanche: zesty wheat and citrus
  • Best Served:
    • Cold
    • Tripel with roasted meats
    • Blanche with citrus-forward or light foods
  • Awards:
    • Well-regarded Goa craft brewery (no major national awards cited)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ₹69–₹295 (varies by variant and availability)
  • Other Variants:
    • Belgian Tripel
    • Belgian Blanche
    • Bavarian Keller
    • Honey Ale

20. Thunderbolt (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Thunderbolt is India’s first strong beer, introduced in 1984, and remains a cult favorite, especially in North India. It is a golden strong lager with approximately 7% ABV, known for its fruity-malty character and nostalgic appeal.

Thunderbolt is often consumed as a high-strength everyday beer, particularly at social gatherings and informal parties.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Classic Strong Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • ~7% (legacy formulation)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Fruity malt notes
    • Mild alcohol warmth
    • Clean finish
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold
    • Pairs well with Indian bar snacks and street food
  • Awards:
    • Cult and nostalgic status rather than formal awards
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹140 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Traditionally sold as a single “Strong Beer” product

21. Old Monk 10000 (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Old Monk 10000 is a super-strong American-style malt liquor brewed by Mohan Meakin, the makers of Old Monk Rum. Despite the brand name, it contains no rum flavor and is brewed in Chennai.

With 8% ABV, it pours a deep amber color and delivers a rich, full-bodied malt profile, making it one of the strongest legal beers in India.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Malt Liquor (Strong Lager)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 8.0%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Sweet caramel malt
    • Toasty grain notes
    • Heavy body with a smooth finish
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled
    • Pairs well with rich meat dishes and spicy Indian food
  • Awards:
    • Cult favorite (no major beer awards)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹130–150 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Sold as a single flagship product

22. Haywards 5000 (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Haywards 5000 is one of India’s most iconic strong lagers, brewed by United Breweries and known for its 7.5% ABV strength. It has been marketed for decades as a robust, no-nonsense beer.

The beer pours golden amber and offers a malt-forward flavor with a smooth, clean finish. It is brewed using Indian malts and German hops.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Strong Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 7.5%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Rich malt sweetness
    • Moderate body
    • Clean, smooth finish
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold
    • Pairs excellently with spicy or fatty Indian dishes
  • Awards:
    • Legendary legacy brand (no recent awards noted)
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹140 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Haywards 2000 – 5% ABV, ~₹110 (650 ml)

23. Royal Challenge (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Royal Challenge is a heritage beer brand from United Spirits. It offers both a Premium Lager (5% ABV) and a Strong Lager (~7% ABV). The beers pour a clear straw-yellow color and feature a smooth, malt-driven profile with low bitterness.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Lager (Premium and Strong)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 5.0% (Premium)
    • ~7.0% (Strong)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Light malty sweetness
    • Smooth mouthfeel
    • Low hop bitterness
  • Best Served:
    • Cold
    • Premium with light snacks
    • Strong with spicy meals
  • Awards:
    • No specific awards noted
  • Price (Delhi):
    • Premium – ~₹50 (330 ml)
    • Strong – ~₹180 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Royal Challenge Premium Lager
    • Royal Challenge Strong Lager

24. Godfather (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Godfather is a mass-market strong lager that originated in Jammu & Kashmir and is especially popular across North India. It is an amber-tinged lager with 6.5–7.5% ABV, known for its pronounced maltiness and heavy body.

The beer has a grainy-sweet aroma and a robust, full-bodied mouthfeel, making it a preferred choice for drinkers who enjoy high-strength beers such as Haywards or Thunderbolt.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Strong Lager
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 7.5% (flagship)
    • 6.5% (alternate variant)
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Strong sweet grain and malt notes
    • Full-bodied texture
    • Mild hints of caramel and smoke
    • Moderate bitterness
  • Best Served:
    • Chilled
    • Pairs well with North Indian spicy dishes such as biryani and kebabs
  • Awards:
    • No notable awards
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹180 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Godfather Original Strong
    • Godfather Light – 4.5% ABV

25. Zingaro (India)

Buy Beer Glass

Zingaro is a value-focused strong lager from United Breweries, primarily sold in South India. With 7.5% ABV, it is positioned as an affordable high-strength beer for everyday consumption.

Zingaro pours a clear golden-yellow color and offers a mildly bitter taste with a toasty corn-malt aroma. It delivers a noticeable alcohol kick at a lower price point, making it popular among budget-conscious consumers.

Key Details

  • Type:
    • Strong Lager (Value Segment)
  • Alcohol Content:
    • 7.5%
  • Flavor Profile:
    • Subtle malty sweetness
    • Moderate bitterness
    • Light grainy and corn-malt aroma
  • Best Served:
    • Very cold
    • Pairs well with spicy or fried street food
  • Awards:
    • No awards noted
  • Price (Delhi):
    • ~₹100 (650 ml)
  • Other Variants:
    • Primarily sold as a single flagship product

Beer Brands Comparison Table (Delhi Pricing)

Conclusion: Choosing the Best Beer in India (2025)

India’s beer market in 2025 reflects a perfect balance between legacy strong lagers, premium international imports, and fast-growing craft beers. From iconic brands like Kingfisher, Haywards 5000, and Godfather to premium imports such as Heineken, Corona, and Stella Artois, Indian consumers today enjoy more variety than ever before.

Strong lagers continue to dominate due to value and strength preferences, while wheat beers, IPAs, and Belgian-style ales are steadily gaining popularity among urban drinkers. Pricing varies significantly by state due to excise policies, making local selection an important factor when buying beer in India.

Whether you prefer a light, refreshing lager, a bold strong beer, or a flavorful craft brew, there is a beer in India suited to every taste and budget.

Beer Buying Guide: How to Choose the Right Beer

1. Choose Based on Alcohol Strength

  • Light beers (4–5%) → Hoegaarden, Bira White, Corona
  • Medium strength (5–6%) → Kingfisher Premium, Heineken, Stella Artois
  • Strong beers (7–8%) → Haywards 5000, Godfather, Knock Out, Bad Monkey

2. Choose Based on Taste Preference

  • Smooth & Easy Drinking: Budweiser Premium, Tuborg Green
  • Malty & Strong: Haywards 5000, Godfather, Thunderbolt
  • Citrusy & Spiced: Hoegaarden, Bira White, Simba Wit
  • Bold & Craft: White Owl, White Rhino, Maka Di

3. Pair Beer with Food

  • Spicy Indian food: Strong lagers (Kingfisher Strong, Haywards)
  • Seafood & salads: Wheat beers (Hoegaarden, Simba Wit)
  • BBQ & grilled meats: Budweiser, Stella Artois
  • Desserts or rich gravies: Stouts (Simba Stout, Malabar Stout)

title.rendered: Top 20 Custom Blockchain Development Companies in USA

content.rendered:
The blockchain industry in the USA is evolving rapidly, with companies at the forefront transforming how businesses handle security, transparency, and decentralized operations. As blockchain adoption accelerates across finance, healthcare, logistics, and digital identity sectors, American development firms are pioneering innovative solutions like smart contracts, NFT marketplaces, and DeFi ecosystems.

These organizations not only build custom blockchain platforms but also integrate AI, IoT, and cloud technologies for smarter, scalable systems. From versatile startups to global technology leaders, the top blockchain development companies in the USA stand out for their technical proficiency, industry-specific expertise, and commitment to client success.

They are driving the next generation of decentralized innovation—enabling enterprises to digitize operations, enhance security, and unlock new business models in an increasingly tokenized economy. The following list highlights the top 20 custom blockchain development companies shaping the U.S. Web3 landscape in 2025.

Top 20 Custom Blockchain Development Companies in USA

1. Netset Software

Netset Software stands as a leading blockchain and Web3 software development company based in the USA. The company specializes in comprehensive blockchain development services including DeFi solutions, NFT development, smart contracts, and private blockchain development. Netset Software delivers enterprise-grade blockchain solutions for various industries including real estate, finance, and supply chain management. With expertise across multiple blockchain platforms and a focus on custom blockchain architecture, Netset Software has established itself as a trusted partner for businesses seeking to implement blockchain technology.

Read Also:- Top Web3 Developers in India 2025 (Updated- List)

2. LeewayHertz

LeewayHertz is one of the most established blockchain software firms in the USA, headquartered in San Francisco, CA. The company has extensive experience developing for platforms like Hyperledger and Ethereum, making them a top choice for large corporations looking to integrate blockchain into their operations. LeewayHertz offers enterprise blockchain solutions, smart contract development, NFT marketplace creation, and AI & blockchain integration services. With a 4.9-star rating on Clutch from 80+ reviews, they have established strong partnerships with Fortune 500 companies including Siemens, Disney, and PepsiCo.

3. ConsenSys

ConsenSys is a foundational company in the Ethereum ecosystem, headquartered in New York, NY. The company is known for developing key infrastructure like MetaMask and Infura. ConsenSys offers enterprise-grade software and services for building on Ethereum, including Ethereum development solutions, smart contract auditing, DeFi & staking products, and enterprise consulting. With 500+ employees, ConsenSys is widely recognized as a leader in the Ethereum community and serves major financial institutions, governments, and leading Web3 projects.

4. IBM Blockchain

IBM provides a fully integrated, enterprise-ready blockchain platform based on the open-source Hyperledger Fabric framework. Headquartered in Armonk, NY, IBM has been a pioneer in enterprise blockchain since 2016. The IBM Blockchain Platform offers a complete blockchain-as-a-service (BaaS) solution with management console, SDK, and deployment options across IBM Cloud, AWS, Azure, and on-premises environments. IBM serves various industries with solutions for supply chain, trade finance, and digital identity, providing 24/7 support and industry-leading expertise.

5. Chainalysis

Chainalysis is an American blockchain analysis firm headquartered in New York City. While primarily focused on blockchain analytics rather than development, Chainalysis provides critical blockchain intelligence services to government agencies, cryptocurrency businesses, and financial institutions. The company has helped law enforcement recover over $34 billion in illicit funds and supports investigations across 45+ regulatory agencies worldwide. Chainalysis serves nine of the top ten crypto exchanges and provides essential compliance and investigation tools for the blockchain ecosystem.

6. Altoros

Altoros is a blockchain development and consulting firm based in Pleasanton, CA, with expertise in Web3 integration and enterprise blockchain solutions. The company offers blockchain consulting, development, deployment, and full-cycle custom development services including PoC, MVP, and production-grade solutions. Altoros specializes in Hyperledger Fabric and Ethereum, with a proven track record in tokenization, DeFi, and supply chain blockchain applications. With a 4.8 Clutch rating, Altoros serves enterprises looking to integrate blockchain into existing operations.

7. HashCash Consultants

HashCash Consultants is a blockchain software products company headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company offers comprehensive blockchain consulting services including blockchain application development, marketing, fundraising, and ICO services. HashCash runs the US-based cryptocurrency exchange PayBito and digital asset payment processor BillBitcoins. With 201-500 employees and $6.5 million in revenue, HashCash provides white label cryptocurrency exchange software, payment processor solutions, and customized blockchain use case development.

8. PixelPlex

PixelPlex is a leading blockchain development company headquartered in New York, NY. The company specializes in blockchain-powered dApps, cryptocurrency exchanges, smart contracts, and NFT marketplaces. PixelPlex offers expertise across Ethereum, Solidity, Polkadot, and Solana platforms. With over 300 delivered projects and a 4.9 Clutch rating, PixelPlex serves startups and enterprises in fintech, healthcare, real estate, and cybersecurity.

9. SoluLab

SoluLab is a trusted blockchain development partner offering comprehensive blockchain services. The company, with 201-500 employees, provides blockchain tech consulting, enterprise blockchain development, smart contracts development, and decentralized application services. Founded by ex-Goldman Sachs and Citrix executives, SoluLab has offices in the USA, India, and UAE, serving various industries with blockchain solutions for DeFi, NFTs, and enterprise applications. The company has successfully completed over 1,500 projects worldwide.

10. Accenture

Accenture (NYSE: ACN) has been recognized as a Leader in enterprise blockchain services by Everest Group. The company offers comprehensive blockchain consulting and development services, including work on central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), decentralized finance, digital identity, and supply chain solutions. Accenture developed Blockchain for Contracts, built on R3 Corda technology and hosted through Microsoft Azure. The company serves global clients with blockchain integration, smart contract development, and enterprise transformation services.

11. Unicsoft

Unicsoft is a technology consulting firm based in Miami, FL, with a strong focus on blockchain and AI. The company specializes in DeFi application development, custom blockchain solutions, AI integration, and NFT development. With a team of 50-249 employees and a 5.0-star rating on Clutch from 75+ reviews, Unicsoft serves FinTech startups, investment funds, and companies entering the DeFi market. Their expertise in decentralized finance has made them particularly popular for developing lending protocols and financial products on blockchain.

12. Debut Infotech

Debut Infotech has been a leader in delivering blockchain services since 2012. The company specializes in building secure and scalable blockchain solutions, offering expertise in smart contracts, decentralized applications (dApps), and blockchain integration. Debut Infotech serves startups, SMBs, and Fortune 500 companies with comprehensive blockchain development services. The company focuses on creating production-ready blockchain applications across various industries including finance, supply chain, and healthcare.

13. R3

R3 is an enterprise blockchain firm that developed Corda, one of the world’s leading open, permissioned distributed ledger technology platforms. Founded in 2014, R3 has created the largest permissioned DLT ecosystem with over 400+ CorDapps. The company received $120+ million in Series A funding led by 40 global institutions, the largest ever USD investment for DLT at the time. R3 specializes in RWA tokenization, digital currencies, and interoperability solutions with over $10 billion in on-chain real-world assets.

14. Infosys

Infosys offers comprehensive blockchain solutions and services through its dedicated blockchain practice. The company provides end-to-end blockchain services from advisory, implementation, and change management to operationalization and application maintenance. Infosys has developed blockchain solutions for government services, supply chain, insurance, and financial services. Notable projects include blockchain-based vital records management systems and credentialing solutions for state governments. Founded in 1981, Infosys is a global IT services leader with over 317,000 employees.

15. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)

TCS has been ranked among the top five providers in enterprise blockchain services by HFS Research, ranked number two for delivery footprint and number three for vision and strategy. The company offers Quartz™, a comprehensive blockchain solutions suite that enables institutional-grade secure custody and transaction management for crypto and digital assets. TCS provides integrated blockchain offerings for financial firms with expertise across multiple blockchain platforms and protocols. As one of India’s largest IT companies founded in 1968, TCS employs over 612,000 people globally.

16. Markovate

Markovate is a blockchain development company headquartered in San Francisco, California. The company specializes in AI consulting, Gen AI development, Web3 development, and blockchain development services. Markovate offers comprehensive blockchain services including smart contract development, dApp development, NFT marketplace creation, and DeFi solutions. With a team of 51-200 employees, Markovate has delivered over 300 digital products across various industries including Stellar, Cardano, and other blockchain platforms.

17. Blaize

Blaize is a specialized blockchain development firm focusing on DeFi and blockchain engineering. The company has expertise with both established chains like Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Solana, as well as cutting-edge ones like Aptos, Sui, and StarkNet. Core services include private blockchain development, decentralized applications development, smart contracts development and audits, security assessments, blockchain integration, and crypto wallet infrastructure. Blaize is highly rated on Clutch with 5.0/5.0 and has six-plus years of experience exclusively in blockchain.

18. Wildnet Edge

Wildnet Edge is globally recognized as a premier blockchain development company at the forefront of the decentralized revolution. Founded in 2008, the company has 250-999 employees and maintains a 5.0-star rating on Clutch from 90+ reviews. Wildnet Edge specializes in custom blockchain development, dApp development, smart contract development & auditing, NFT marketplace development, and DeFi solutions. The company has major global offices with a significant hub for blockchain innovation in the USA, serving major corporations in finance, supply chain, gaming, and digital identity.

19. Appinventiv

Appinventiv offers custom blockchain development services with expertise in blockchain application development for various industries. The company provides comprehensive blockchain solutions including smart contract development, cryptocurrency exchange platforms, and decentralized application development. Appinventiv serves clients globally with a focus on creating scalable and secure blockchain implementations for finance, real estate, and supply chain applications. The company has established itself as a prominent player in the blockchain development space with numerous successful projects.

20. Block (formerly Square)

Block, headquartered in San Francisco, is a financial services and mobile payments company founded by Jack Dorsey. The company has rapidly expanded its blockchain and cryptocurrency operations with subsidiaries including Cash App, a popular payments platform, and Bitcoin-focused Spiral. Block collaborates with businesses globally to develop inclusive financial policies and blockchain-based payment solutions. The company focuses on leveraging blockchain technology to provide faster, more transparent, and cost-effective alternatives to traditional financial services.

These 20 companies represent the leading edge of blockchain development in the United States, offering comprehensive services ranging from enterprise blockchain solutions to DeFi platforms, smart contracts, NFT marketplaces, and blockchain consulting. Each company brings unique expertise and capabilities to help businesses leverage blockchain technology for digital transformation and innovation.

title.rendered: Top 50 Most Popular Native American Actresses

content.rendered:
From Lily Gladstone’s history-making awards run to Sacheen Littlefeather’s 1973 Oscar protest, Indigenous actresses have shaped film and television for generations. This guide profiles 50 of them — Oscar nominees, franchise leads, voice artists, playwrights and advocates — with every career checked and updated to November 2026.

A note on scope: inclusion follows documented Indigenous heritage — tribal citizenship, descent or upbringing — as reported by reliable sources. Where a performer’s heritage is mixed, disputed or simply not documented, her profile says so plainly rather than guessing.

Quick answer

  • Fifty actresses are profiled, in the list’s established order, each with her photograph, career summary and sourced key facts.
  • The most decorated recent run belongs to Lily Gladstone, the first Native American to win the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Drama and the first nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress.
  • The newest franchise names include Amber Midthunder, who headlined Prey, and Alyssa Wapanatâhk, who plays White Sun in Netflix’s Little House on the Prairie.
  • The longest career span runs from Geraldine Keams, who debuted in The Outlaw Josey Wales in 1976, to the streaming-era leads of Dark Winds and Reservation Dogs.
  • The list includes citizens of sovereign nations such as the Blackfeet Nation, the Cherokee Nation, the Navajo Nation and the Kahnawà:ke Mohawk community.

Award firsts and milestones

  • 1973: Sacheen Littlefeather declines Marlon Brando’s Oscar on his behalf, protesting Hollywood’s portrayal of Native Americans and the standoff at Wounded Knee; the Academy formally apologised to her in 2022.
  • 1995: Irene Bedard provides the speaking voice and physical model for Disney’s Pocahontas, the studio’s first Native American princess.
  • 2008: Misty Upham wins Best Supporting Actress at the American Indian Film Festival and an Independent Spirit Award nomination for Frozen River.
  • 2020: Nyla Rose becomes the first transgender wrestler to win a world championship in a major United States promotion, alongside her acting work.
  • 2022: Amber Midthunder becomes the first Indigenous actor to headline a major franchise film, leading Prey.
  • 2024: Salli Richardson-Whitfield becomes the first Black woman nominated for the Emmy for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series.
  • 2024: Lily Gladstone becomes the first Native American to win the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Drama and the first nominated for the Best Actress Oscar.

The new generation

A generation of Indigenous-led series has changed who gets cast and who gets to create. Reservation Dogs, Dark Winds and Little Bird all put Native actresses at the centre, several of them writing and directing as well as performing.

  • Devery Jacobs played Elora Danan in Reservation Dogs and also wrote and directed on the series.
  • Jessica Matten leads Dark Winds as Sergeant Bernadette Manuelito; season three premiered in March 2025.
  • Elle-Máijá Tailfeathers directed the first three episodes of Little Bird, winning Directors Guild of Canada and Canadian Screen Award honours.
  • Kaniehtiio Horn wrote, directed and starred in Seeds (2024), which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival.

How this list was researched

  • Every profile was rewritten from fresh research carried out in November 2026, using official biographies, major entertainment press and award bodies.
  • Tribal affiliation or nation is stated only where a reliable source documents it; where none could be found, the profile records that honestly.
  • Earlier versions of this list carried unsourced tables of net worth, zodiac signs and relationship status. Those have been removed in full.
  • Each actress keeps the photograph published with her profile. Where the stored photograph could not be confidently matched to its subject, that is flagged in the pack’s editorial report.

The 50 actresses, profiled

1. Lily Gladstone

Lily Gladstone is of Piegan Blackfeet and Nez Perce descent and was raised on the Blackfeet Reservation in Montana. After years of independent-film work, her performance as Mollie Burkhart in Martin Scorsese’s Killers of the Flower Moon (2023) made awards history on three fronts.

She became the first Native American to win the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Drama, the first to win the Screen Actors Guild Award for a leading film role, and the first nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress. She followed it with an Emmy nomination for Under the Bridge (2024) and a starring role in The Wedding Banquet (2025).

  • Heritage: Piegan Blackfeet and Nez Perce descent; raised on the Blackfeet Reservation
  • Breakthrough role: Mollie Burkhart in Killers of the Flower Moon (2023)
  • Awards firsts: First Native American to win the Golden Globe for Best Actress (Drama) and the first nominated for the Best Actress Oscar
  • Recent work: Under the Bridge (2024); Fancy Dance; The Wedding Banquet (2025)

2. Elle-Máijá Tailfeathers

Elle-Máijá Apiniskim Tailfeathers is a member of the Kainai First Nation (Blood Tribe) of the Blackfoot Confederacy and is also Sámi, from Uŋárga in Norway. She works as an actor, writer and director, and co-wrote, co-directed and starred in The Body Remembers When the World Broke Open, which won Canadian Screen Awards for direction and screenplay.

Her acting credits include Night Raiders and Blood Quantum. Behind the camera she directed the acclaimed documentary Kímmapiiyipitssini: The Meaning of Empathy and the first three episodes of Little Bird, winning a Directors Guild of Canada Award in 2023 and a Canadian Screen Award in 2024. She starred in Sweet Angel Baby (2024).

  • Nation: Member of the Kainai First Nation (Blood Tribe), Blackfoot Confederacy
  • Heritage: Blackfoot and Sámi (from Uŋárga, Norway)
  • Known for: The Body Remembers When the World Broke Open; Night Raiders
  • Directing: First three episodes of Little Bird; DGC Award 2023 and Canadian Screen Award 2024

3. Rosario Dawson

Rosario Dawson was born in New York City on 9 May 1979 and was discovered on a stoop in the East Village, leading to her debut in Kids (1995). Her mother is Afro-Cuban and Puerto Rican. Her biological father has been described as of American Indian and Irish ancestry, and Dawson herself wrote in 2013 that she is “half Puerto Rican/Afro-Cuban & half Irish/Native Indian”; no specific tribal affiliation is documented.

She went on to star in Rent and Sin City, played Claire Temple across Marvel’s Netflix series, and took on the fan-favourite role of Ahsoka Tano in The Mandalorian (2020) and the spin-off Ahsoka (2023).

  • Born: 9 May 1979, New York City
  • Heritage: Afro-Cuban and Puerto Rican mother; father described as of Irish and Native American ancestry (self-described, 2013)

The community said she was not a member, and a genealogical review found only distant Indigenous ancestors from the 17th century. No tribal affiliation is stated for her here.

37. Sacheen Littlefeather

Sacheen Littlefeather (14 November 1946 – 2 October 2022), born Marie Louise Cruz, made history at the 45th Academy Awards on 27 March 1973. Sent by Marlon Brando, she declined his Best Actor Oscar for The Godfather, protesting Hollywood’s portrayal of Native Americans and the federal standoff at Wounded Knee. The Academy sent her a formal apology in June 2022, read aloud at An Evening with Sacheen Littlefeather that September, weeks before her death.

Littlefeather said her father was of White Mountain Apache and Yaqui heritage. After her death, her sisters Rosalind Cruz and Trudy Orlandi told the San Francisco Chronicle that the family was of Spanish-Mexican descent with no tribal ties. Both accounts are recorded here; her place in this list reflects the historic role she played, which is not in dispute.

  • Known for: Declining Marlon Brando’s Oscar at the 1973 Academy Awards

  • Heritage note: Claimed White Mountain Apache and Yaqui parentage; disputed by her sisters after her death — see profile

38. Alyssa Wapanatâhk

Alyssa Wapanatâhk was born on 15 January 1998 in Fort McMurray, Alberta, is a member of the Bigstone Cree Nation, and was raised in Conklin. Her first major role was Tiger Lily in Disney’s Peter Pan & Wendy (2023), in which she speaks Cree and worked with the filmmakers and language consultants to shape the character from her own heritage.

She earned a Leo Award nomination for Bones of Crows and also appeared in Riverdale. She now plays White Sun, an Osage character, in Netflix’s adaptation of Little House on the Prairie, learning Osage for the role with the production’s language consultants.

  • Born: 15 January 1998, Fort McMurray, Alberta
  • Nation: Member of the Bigstone Cree Nation
  • Known for: Tiger Lily in Peter Pan & Wendy (2023)
  • Honours: Leo Award nomination for Bones of Crows
  • Recent work: White Sun in Netflix’s Little House on the Prairie

39. Jenny Gago

Jenny Gago was born on 11 September 1953 in Peru and trained at UCLA, where she earned a BA in Theatre Arts, before winning a scholarship to the Lee Strasberg Institute. She played Maria in Knots Landing (1984–86) and the matriarch Maria Sanchez in Gregory Nava’s My Family (1995).

Her later roles include Anaya in The Agency, President Martinez in Coach Carter (2005) and Detective Josie Ochoa in Southland (2011); she won a Golden Eagle Award for Old Gringo (1989). No Indigenous affiliation is documented for her in reliable sources, and none is claimed here.

  • Born: 11 September 1953, Peru
  • Training: BA in Theatre Arts, UCLA; Lee Strasberg Institute scholarship
  • Known for: Maria in My Family (1995); Knots Landing
  • Honours: Golden Eagle Award for Old Gringo (1989)
  • Affiliation: None documented — see profile

40. Patricia Velásquez

Patricia Velásquez was born on 31 January 1971 in Maracaibo, Venezuela, the fifth of six children of a mestizo father and a mother of Wayuu heritage. A pioneering Latina supermodel, she is best known on screen as Anck-su-namun in The Mummy (1999) and The Mummy Returns (2001).

In 2002 she founded the Wayuu Taya Foundation, which works to improve living conditions for the Wayuu people of Venezuela and Colombia while preserving their culture. She was appointed a UNESCO Artist for Peace in 2003, published her memoir Straight Walk in 2015, and in 2018 became an OAS Goodwill Ambassador for the Rights of Indigenous Peoples of the Americas.

  • Born: 31 January 1971, Maracaibo, Venezuela
  • Heritage: Wayuu heritage through her mother; mestizo father
  • Known for: Anck-su-namun in The Mummy (1999) and The Mummy Returns (2001)
  • Advocacy: Founder of the Wayuu Taya Foundation (2002); UNESCO Artist for Peace (2003)
  • Writing: Memoir, Straight Walk (2015)

41. Taylor Dooley

Taylor Dooley was born on 26 February 1993 in Grosse Pointe, Michigan, and became a child star as Lavagirl in Robert Rodriguez’s The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl (2005). She stepped back from acting to study, graduating in psychology from California State University, Northridge, before returning to the role as an adult in We Can Be Heroes (2020).

Biographies of Dooley list Sioux among her family’s ancestries, although accounts differ on which side of the family it comes from and no tribal affiliation is documented. This profile records the claim with that caution.

  • Born: 26 February 1993, Grosse Pointe, Michigan
  • Known for: Lavagirl in The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl (2005)
  • Recent work: Reprised Lavagirl in We Can Be Heroes (2020)
  • Education: Psychology graduate, California State University, Northridge
  • Heritage: Sioux ancestry listed in biographies; details inconsistent and affiliation not documented

42. Jessica Matten

Jessica Matten is a Canadian Métis actor best known as Sergeant Bernadette Manuelito in AMC’s Dark Winds. Season three, which premiered in March 2025, took Manuelito out of the tribal police and into a Border Patrol storyline, the series’ most prominent arc for the character so far.

Her earlier work includes the series Frontier, Tribal and Burden of Truth, and the 2024 basketball film Rez Ball.

  • Heritage: Métis (Canadian)
  • Known for: Sergeant Bernadette Manuelito in Dark Winds
  • Recent work: Dark Winds season 3 (premiered March 2025); Rez Ball (2024)
  • Television: Frontier; Tribal; Burden of Truth

43. Geraldine Keams

Geraldine Keams was born on 19 August 1951 in Flagstaff, Arizona, is a citizen of the Navajo Nation, and was raised on the Navajo reservation before studying drama and film at the University of Arizona. In New York she wrote and performed with the Native American Theater Ensemble at La MaMa, adapting a Navajo creation story for the stage in 1972.

Her film debut came as Little Moonlight in Clint Eastwood’s The Outlaw Josey Wales (1976). Decades later she returned to screens with a recurring role in the sitcom Rutherford Falls (2021). She is also a storyteller and the author of children’s books including Grandmother Spider Brings the Sun.

  • Born: 19 August 1951, Flagstaff, Arizona
  • Citizenship: Citizen of the Navajo Nation; raised on the Navajo reservation
  • Known for: Little Moonlight in The Outlaw Josey Wales (1976)
  • Recent work: Recurring role in Rutherford Falls (2021)
  • Other work: Storyteller; children’s author (Grandmother Spider Brings the Sun)

44. Shauna Baker

Shauna Baker was born on the Stellat’en First Nation in British Columbia and is Carrier (Dakelh); in keeping with Carrier-Sekani tradition she and her identical twin sister Shannon were raised by their grandmother, Emma Baker. Together the two work as the Baker Twins, models, actors and spokespeople who have spoken publicly about First Nations stereotyping in media, including on The Tyra Banks Show in 2007.

The twins’ screen appearances together include Smallville, CSI: Crime Scene Investigation and Blue Mountain State, and they starred in the music video for Slipknot’s “Killpop”.

  • Nation: Carrier (Dakelh), of the Stellat’en First Nation, British Columbia
  • Family: Identical twin sister Shannon; together they are the Baker Twins
  • Known for: Modelling and media advocacy as the Baker Twins
  • Television: The Tyra Banks Show (2007); Smallville; CSI; Blue Mountain State

45. Yvonne DeLaRosa

Yvonne DeLaRosa was born in Los Angeles in 1978 to a Colombian mother and a Native American father; her IMDb biography describes her as part Cheyenne on her father’s side. A true Los Angeles native, she studied theatre from childhood, graduated from Hollywood High’s performing arts school, and earned a BA in directing and an MFA in screenwriting at UCLA.

Director Betty Thomas cast her as the lead of the Fox pilot Señor White (2003), and she starred as Alma Valenzuela opposite Esai Morales in the Imagen Award-winning series Los Americans (2011). Her many guest roles include NCIS, Weeds, How I Met Your Mother and Longmire. She has since become known as a cannabis-industry entrepreneur in Malibu.

  • Born: 1978, Los Angeles
  • Heritage: Colombian mother; Native American father — part Cheyenne per her IMDb biography
  • Education: BA in directing and MFA in screenwriting, UCLA
  • Known for: Alma Valenzuela in Los Americans (2011)
  • Breakthrough: Series lead in the Fox pilot Señor White (2003)

46. Catherine Bach

Catherine Bach, born Catherine Bachman in Warren, Ohio, became one of the most recognisable television stars of her era as Daisy Duke in The Dukes of Hazzard (1979–85). She later played Margo Dutton in African Skies and joined The Young and the Restless as Anita Lawson in 2012.

Her father was of German ancestry. Her mother was a Verdugo: her grandfather was born in Mexico, and her mother claimed descent from one of the oldest Californio families of California. That Mexican and Californio heritage is documented; a specific Indigenous affiliation is not, and none is claimed here.

  • Born: Warren, Ohio (born Catherine Bachman)
  • Heritage: German father; mother of Mexican and Californio (Verdugo family) descent
  • Known for: Daisy Duke in The Dukes of Hazzard (1979–85)
  • Recent work: Anita Lawson in The Young and the Restless (from 2012)
  • Affiliation: None documented — see profile

47. Nyla Rose

Nyla Rose was born on 3 August 1982 in Washington, D.C., and is of Oneida and African American ancestry. She works in two spotlights at once: as an actor she played the lead in the Canadian comedy series The Switch (2016), and as a professional wrestler she signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019.

That signing made her the first openly transgender wrestler signed by a major American promotion; in February 2020 she defeated Riho to become AEW Women’s World Champion, the first transgender wrestler to win a world title in a major United States promotion. In 2025 she returned to the independent circuit and won the Pro Wrestling EVE championship in August.

  • Born: 3 August 1982, Washington, D.C.
  • Heritage: Oneida and African American ancestry
  • Acting: Lead role in The Switch (2016)
  • Milestone: First openly transgender wrestler signed by a major US promotion (AEW, 2019)
  • Titles: AEW Women’s World Champion (2020); Pro Wrestling EVE champion (2025)

48. Marisa Quintanilla

Marisa Quintanilla, credited on screen as Marisa Quinn, was born in McAllen, Texas, and graduated from Brown University. She is best known as Huilen, the aunt of the hybrid Nahuel, in The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2 (2012).

Her television credits include Sons of Anarchy, Private Practice and Criminal Minds, and she founded Monarch Media Productions, executive producing and starring in Sweet Mary & Jane. A Yaqui affiliation attached to her name in older listicles could not be verified from reliable sources, so none is claimed in this profile.

  • Born: McAllen, Texas
  • Education: Graduate of Brown University
  • Known for: Huilen in The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2 (2012)
  • Television: Sons of Anarchy; Private Practice; Criminal Minds
  • Affiliation: None verified — see profile

49. Ashley Callingbull

Ashley Callingbull is a member of the Enoch Cree Nation in Alberta. In 2015 she won Mrs. Universe, becoming both the first Canadian and the first Indigenous winner of the title. She broke another barrier in 2022 as the first Indigenous woman to appear as a Sports Illustrated swimsuit model.

On 27 July 2024 she was crowned Miss Universe Canada — again the first Indigenous woman to win it — and went on to place in the Top 12 at Miss Universe 2024 in Mexico. Her acting credits include the series Blackstone and Tribal.

  • Nation: Member of the Enoch Cree Nation (Plains Cree), Alberta
  • Titles: Mrs. Universe 2015; Miss Universe Canada 2024
  • Milestones: First Indigenous winner of both titles; first Indigenous Sports Illustrated swimsuit model (2022)
  • Recent result: Top 12 at Miss Universe 2024
  • Acting: Blackstone; Tribal

50. Acquanetta

Acquanetta (17 July 1921 – 16 August 2004) was a B-movie star whom Universal Pictures billed as “the Venezuelan Volcano”. She starred in Captive Wild Woman (1943) and Tarzan and the Leopard Woman (1946), trading on an exotic persona whose origins she kept deliberately mysterious.

She claimed to have been born Burnu Acquanetta in Ozone, Wyoming, orphaned by Arapaho parents. Census-based research instead identifies her as Mildred Davenport, from a Pennsylvania family whose son Horace became the first African American judge in Montgomery County, and the Arapaho story is generally treated as a studio-era invention. She is included here for the identity she publicly claimed, with that dispute recorded in full.

  • Born: 17 July 1921 (birth name and origins disputed — see profile)
  • Died: 16 August 2004
  • Known for: Captive Wild Woman (1943); Tarzan and the Leopard Woman (1946)
  • Persona: Billed by Universal as “the Venezuelan Volcano”
  • Heritage note: Claimed Arapaho birth; census records point to Mildred Davenport of Pennsylvania

Check also: Top 30 Most Beautiful 90s Actresses (Then and Now)

Final word

The through-line of these fifty careers is a shift in who holds the pen. The earliest names here worked inside an industry that cast Indigenous women as atmosphere; the newest write, direct and produce their own stories — and several, like Jennifer Podemski and DeLanna Studi, have built the institutions that train the next generation.

This list is reviewed and refreshed as careers develop. Where a fact could not be verified from a reliable source, it has been left out rather than repeated — that includes several heritage claims carried by older versions of this article.

Frequently asked questions

Who was the first Native American actress nominated for the Best Actress Oscar?

Lily Gladstone, for Killers of the Flower Moon (2023). She was also the first Native American to win the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Drama and the Screen Actors Guild Award for a leading film role.

Who voiced Disney’s Pocahontas?

Irene Bedard, an enrolled citizen of the Native Village of Koyuk. She provided the character’s speaking voice and served as her physical model in the 1995 film, returning for the 1998 sequel and a 2018 cameo.

Who stars in Prey, and what is her tribal background?

Amber Midthunder, a citizen of the Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes, plays the Comanche hunter Naru. Prey (2022) made her the first Indigenous actor to headline a major franchise film.

What happened at the 1973 Academy Awards?

Sacheen Littlefeather declined Marlon Brando’s Best Actor Oscar on his behalf, protesting Hollywood’s portrayal of Native Americans and the standoff at Wounded Knee. The Academy formally apologised to her in 2022. After her death that year, her sisters disputed her claimed Apache and Yaqui heritage; both accounts are set out in her profile above.

Are all fifty women enrolled citizens of tribal nations?

No. The list mixes enrolled citizens, women of documented Indigenous descent, and performers whose claimed or listed affiliation could not be verified from reliable sources. Each profile states exactly what the sources support, and flags the cases — including Vanessa Williams, Raven-Symoné and Andrea Navedo — where no affiliation is documented.

Who plays Bernadette Manuelito in Dark Winds?

Jessica Matten, a Canadian Métis actor. Season three of Dark Winds premiered in March 2025 and moved Manuelito into a Border Patrol storyline.
