title.rendered: Top 22 Whiskey Brands in India (Updated List)

content.rendered:
India is one of the largest markets for whisky in the world, boasting a wide range of local and international brands. Whisky enthusiasts in the country have access to a diverse array of blends, flavors, and price ranges, making it easier for every individual to find a whisky that suits their palate and budget. Below, we explore the best whisky brands in India with their unique features, prices, and characteristics.

Best Whiskey Brands in India

1. Dewar’s 18-Year-Old Blended Scotch Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Dewar’s 18 is an epitome of sophistication, offering a creamy finish and a subtle smokiness. This whisky, renowned among the best in India, is aged to perfection for 18 years. Its 40% alcohol content ensures a smooth and balanced drinking experience.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Delicate and creamy with hints of smoke.
  • Awards: Gold medal at the 2012 International Wine & Spirits Competition.
  • Price Range: Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 9,500 for 750 ml.

Other Dewar’s Varieties

  • Dewar’s 12-Year-Old: Rs. 3,029 (750 ml)
  • Dewar’s 15-Year-Old: Rs. 5,290 (1L)
  • Dewar’s 25-Year-Old: Rs. 22,800 (750 ml)
  • Dewar’s White Label: Rs. 1,800 (750 ml)

2. Jameson Irish Whiskey

Buy Wine Glass

Jameson is a beloved name among whisky lovers, especially for its triple-distilled process, which ensures a smooth and refined taste. Known for its golden honey color and exceptional balance, this Irish whisky remains a top choice for Indian consumers.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Spicy, nutty, and vanilla tones with a mellow finish.
  • Alcohol Content: 40%.
  • Price Range: Rs. 2,500 to Rs. 5,000 for 750 ml.

Popular Jameson Variants

  • Jameson Irish Whiskey Caskmates: Rs. 4,450 (750 ml)
  • Jameson Irish Whiskey: Rs. 3,790 (1L)
  • Smaller Quantities: Rs. 400 for 60 ml, Rs. 970 for 180 ml.

3. Ballantine’s Scotch Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Ballantine’s is a name synonymous with premium whisky, with its 1827 origins lending it a rich legacy. It offers a smooth, balanced taste complemented by notes of honey and vanilla. With a slightly higher alcohol percentage of 42.8%, it appeals to seasoned whisky enthusiasts.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Aromatic honey, vanilla, and a hint of smoke.
  • Price Range: Rs. 3,000 to Rs. 5,000 for 750 ml.

Popular Ballantine’s Options

  • Ballantine’s 17-Year-Old: Rs. 7,590 (750 ml)
  • Ballantine’s 21-Year-Old: Rs. 12,790 (750 ml)
  • Ballantine’s Finest Scotch: Rs. 2,290 (750 ml).

4. Black Dog Reserve Whiskey

Buy Wine Glass

Black Dog Reserve is revered for its premium quality and smooth texture. Crafted in Scotland, this whisky is aged to perfection in oak casks, making it a top-tier choice among Indian whisky brands.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Smooth and rich, with a harmonious blend of malt and grain whiskies.
  • Alcohol Content: 42.8%.
  • Price Range: Rs. 1,600 to Rs. 3,220 depending on the variant.

Notable Black Dog Varieties

  • Black Dog Centenary Aged: Rs. 2,500 (750 ml)
  • Black Dog Triple Gold Reserve: Rs. 2,660 (1L).

5. Johnnie Walker Red Label Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Johnnie Walker is a name that needs no introduction, and its Red Label blend is a testament to the brand’s legacy. Crafted with whiskies from four Scottish regions, it offers a balanced and flavorful experience.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Cedar, butterscotch, and spiced rum.
  • Alcohol Content: 40%.
  • Price Range: Rs. 2,500 to Rs. 4,000 for 750 ml.

Other Johnnie Walker Labels

  • Blue Label: Rs. 14,400 (750 ml)
  • Double Black: Rs. 3,120 (750 ml).

6. Monkey Shoulder Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Monkey Shoulder is a unique blended malt whisky, featuring malts from three renowned Speyside distilleries. This whisky is known for its smooth texture and exceptional affordability in India.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Sweet and malty, with hints of vanilla and oak.
  • Price: Rs. 3,900 for 700 ml.

7. Black & White Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Black & White Whisky is celebrated for its light and smooth profile. As a London-style blend, it combines some of Scotland’s finest malts and grains, making it a popular choice in India.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Subtle and balanced, with a floral and malty aroma.
  • Price: Rs. 1,500 to Rs. 2,930 depending on the variant and size.

9. Teacher’s Highland Cream

Buy Wine Glass

Teacher’s Highland Cream holds a special place in the hearts of Indian whisky lovers, thanks to its smoky undertones and rich texture. Crafted with over 30 whiskies, it is a versatile choice for any occasion.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Smoky, toffee-like sweetness with malt and fruity hints.
  • Alcohol Content: 40%.
  • Price Range: Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 3,235 for 750 ml.

10. Imperial Blue

Buy Wine Glass

Imperial Blue, one of the most popular Indian whisky brands, is a perfect blend of Scotch malts and Indian grain whiskies. It delivers exceptional quality at an affordable price, making it a go-to choice for many.

Key Features

  • Flavor Profile: Smooth, with a balance of sweet and grainy notes.
  • Alcohol Content: 42.8%.
  • Price: Rs. 490 for 750 ml.

11. Royal Challenge

Buy Wine Glass

Royal Challenge, popularly known as RC, is a flagship Indian whisky brand that perfectly fuses Scotch malts, Indian malts, and grain spirits. Originally crafted by Shaw Wallace and now owned by United Spirits Ltd. (part of Diageo), this whisky has maintained its royal reputation for decades.

Achievements and Popularity

RC holds the distinction of being the first whisky in the mid-prestige price segment to cross the threshold of 1 million cases in annual sales. With over 4.5 million cases sold every year, it has cemented itself as a household name for whisky lovers across India.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

Royal Challenge offers a smooth and balanced drinking experience with an alcohol content of 42.8%, adhering to India’s permissible limits for whiskies.

  • 180 ml: ₹140
  • 375 ml: ₹260
  • 750 ml: ₹460

12. The Rockford Reserve

Buy Wine Glass

The Rockford Reserve is a premium whisky brand born from a joint venture between Umesh Modi Group and Saronno Modi Illva India Pvt. Ltd. Its introduction marked the brand’s foray into the premium whisky market with variants like Rockford Reserve and Rockford Classic.

Unique Craftsmanship

This whisky stands out due to its meticulous craftsmanship, including an eight-year aging process in American oak casks. Made using imported grains and infused with natural herbs and Himalayan spring water, it offers a distinctive flavor that combines complexity and smoothness.

Pricing and Alcohol Content

The Rockford Reserve is a preferred choice among connoisseurs for its golden hue, seductive aroma, and 42.8% ABV.

  • 750 ml: ₹850
  • 1000 ml: ₹1150

13. Amrut Indian Single Malt Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Amrut Indian Single Malt Whisky holds the honor of being India’s first single malt whisky, launched in 2004. Produced by the Amrut Distillery, this whisky has gained global acclaim for its remarkable quality and taste. It is now sold in over 20 countries, including Belgium, Denmark, and Singapore, and is regarded as a trailblazer in the Indian whisky landscape.

Flavor Profile

This single malt whisky presents a rich and luscious flavor profile with notes of fruit, honey, and spice. The blend’s impeccable balance ensures every sip is an unforgettable experience.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

Amrut Indian Single Malt Whisky has an alcohol percentage of 46%, offering a premium experience for whisky lovers.

  • 750 ml: ₹3000–₹6000

14. Antiquity Blue Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Antiquity Blue Whisky, launched in 1992 by Shaw Wallace, is known for its seamless blend of Scottish grain whiskies and Indian malts. Its unique combination of tradition and modernity has earned it a loyal fan base.

Tasting Notes and Aroma

Antiquity Blue stands out for its smooth texture, making it suitable for neat drinking or mixing with water, soda, or ice. It offers a delightful aroma of peat smoke, honeycomb, and dark fruits, complemented by flavors of honey, caramel, and cinnamon. The finish leaves subtle hints of vanilla and dark chocolate, making it a luxurious choice.

Price Range and ABV

With an alcohol content of 42.8%, Antiquity Blue is available in an affordable range.

  • 750 ml: ₹1000–₹2000

15. Rampur Single Malt Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Rampur Single Malt Whisky, crafted by Radico Khaitan, made its debut in Las Vegas in April 2016. Despite being a relatively new entrant, it has carved a niche for itself with its distinctive qualities and global appeal.

Distinctive Qualities

This whisky is distilled in copper pot stills using carefully selected Himalayan malted barley. Aged in oak barrels, it boasts a smooth character with rich notes of caramel, vanilla, and dried fruits. The craftsmanship and attention to detail elevate Rampur to a class apart.

Pricing and Alcohol Content

Rampur Single Malt Whisky has a robust alcohol percentage of 63%, reflecting its bold character.

  • 750 ml: ₹3500–₹5500

16. Paul John Brilliance Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Paul John Brilliance Whisky, crafted by John Distilleries, is a shining star in the Indian whisky market. Launched in 2013, this single malt whisky has captured the hearts of whisky enthusiasts worldwide. With its origins in Goa, the tropical climate contributes significantly to its unique maturation process, setting it apart from traditional single malts.

Tasting Experience

Paul John Brilliance is known for its fruity and creamy texture. It combines the sweetness of honey and butterscotch with a hint of cocoa, creating a balanced and luxurious palate. Matured in charred American oak barrels, it delivers a velvety finish that lingers on your taste buds, making every sip a delightful experience.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

With an alcohol content of 46%, this whisky is a premium offering for discerning drinkers.

  • 750 ml: ₹3500–₹5000

17. The Glenlivet 12-Year-Old Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

The Glenlivet 12-Year-Old Whisky is a hallmark of excellence in the single malt whisky category. Produced by the iconic Glenlivet Distillery in Scotland, it has earned its place among the most sought-after whiskies in India. Known for its consistent quality, it appeals to whisky enthusiasts who appreciate heritage and finesse.

Flavor Profile

This whisky is characterized by its fruity and creamy notes. Hints of pineapple, vanilla, honey, and a gentle touch of oak make it a balanced yet complex single malt. The smooth finish leaves a memorable impression, perfect for those who prefer subtlety over intensity.

Pricing and ABV

With an alcohol percentage of 40%, Glenlivet 12-Year-Old Whisky offers an elegant drinking experience.

  • 750 ml: ₹5500–₹7000

18. Chivas Regal 12-Year-Old Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Chivas Regal 12-Year-Old Whisky, a blend crafted by Chivas Brothers, has been a global favorite since its inception in 1909. Known for its rich heritage and premium quality, this whisky represents sophistication in a bottle. It has become a go-to choice for celebratory moments and special occasions.

Taste and Texture

Chivas Regal is celebrated for its smooth, creamy texture with notes of ripe apples, honey, and a gentle hint of spice. Its balanced flavor profile appeals to seasoned whisky drinkers and newcomers alike. The finish, with hints of hazelnut and butterscotch, adds to its charm.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

This whisky has a standard alcohol content of 40%, making it a versatile option for all kinds of whisky drinkers.

  • 750 ml: ₹2500–₹5000

19. McDowell’s No.1 Platinum

Buy Wine Glass

Launched in 2010, McDowell’s No.1 Platinum has become a symbol of premium whisky in India. A blend of Indian spirits and Scotch malts, it combines affordability with quality, catering to a wide range of consumers.

Taste and Aroma

McDowell’s Platinum delivers a smooth, grainy mouthfeel with a subtle hint of oak spice. The aroma is rich with malty notes, balanced by a touch of honey and fruit, making it perfect for both casual and formal occasions.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

This whisky boasts an alcohol content of 42.8%, making it a robust and enjoyable choice.

  • 750 ml: ₹500–₹1200

20. Royal Stag Barrel Select Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Royal Stag Barrel Select, introduced in 2011, is a premium variant of the popular Royal Stag brand. Known for its fine craftsmanship, this whisky is a blend of carefully selected Scotch malts and Indian grain spirits.

Taste and Aroma

Aged in handpicked oak barrels, this whisky reveals a smooth, refined taste with hints of charred coconut and vanilla. The fruity aroma, coupled with subtle peat undertones, makes it a favorite among whisky connoisseurs.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

With an alcohol content of 42.8%, Royal Stag Barrel Select offers an exceptional experience at an affordable price.

  • 750 ml: ₹600–₹1000

21. Seagram’s 100 Pipers Deluxe

Buy Wine Glass

Introduced in India in 1995, Seagram’s 100 Pipers Deluxe is a trusted name among whisky lovers. It is known for its elegant blend of Scotch whiskies, offering a balanced and approachable drinking experience.

Tasting Notes

The whisky delivers a pleasant smokiness with fruity undertones. Its smooth texture and full-flavored palate make it an excellent choice for those who enjoy a mild yet flavorful whisky.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

Seagram’s 100 Pipers Deluxe has an alcohol content of 42.8%, providing an optimal balance of flavor and strength.

  • 750 ml: ₹2000–₹3000

22. Vat 69

Buy Wine Glass

Vat 69, a classic Scotch whisky, was created in 1882 by William Sanderson. Known for its smoothness and rich heritage, this blend continues to charm whisky enthusiasts worldwide, including in India.

Tasting Experience

This whisky offers a distinct sweetness of vanilla, complemented by a smooth and well-balanced character. The subtle complexity makes it a favorite for both solo sipping and cocktails.

Price Range and Alcohol Content

Vat 69 contains an alcohol percentage of 40%, delivering a refined experience at a reasonable price.

  • 750 ml: ₹1500–₹2500

23. Indri-Trini Whisky

Buy Wine Glass

Indri Whisky draws inspiration from the vibrant indri bird and offers an equally colorful drinking experience. Its unique blend and innovative approach make it a standout choice in the Indian whisky market.

Tasting Notes

The whisky features notes of dried fruits, young oak, caramel, vanilla, and a refreshing touch of lemon. Its balanced yet dynamic profile appeals to both novice and experienced drinkers.

Price Range and ABV

Indri Whisky has an alcohol content of 46%, reflecting its robust and full-bodied character.

  • 750 ml: ₹3500–₹5000

Best Whisky Under ₹1500 in India

Cutty Sark Blended Scotch

This light and smooth Scotch whisky offers a delightful mix of barley, custard, and herbs. It’s perfect for those seeking a budget-friendly option.

  • Price: ₹1477

Jim Beam Kentucky Straight Bourbon

A top bourbon worldwide, this whisky combines smokiness from charred oak barrels with the sweetness of corn and rye.

  • Price: ₹1363

Conclusion

Embark on an exciting journey through India’s finest whisky brands, each offering unique flavors and a rich heritage. From the luxurious single malts to budget-friendly gems, these whiskies cater to every palate. Whether you’re savoring a royal experience or indulging in everyday elegance, there’s a bottle for every occasion. Cheers to discovering the best whisky India has to offer!

title.rendered: Top 12 Tiles Brands in India (Strong and Durable)

content.rendered:
Best Tile Brands in India: Your home reflects the story of who you are and describes your attitude toward life. Decorating your home with the best tile brands in India will enhance the overall look of your house. Le Corbusier says that a home should be the treasure chest of living. And for sure, interior decoration is a central part of the building.

Beauty in a home comes from flooring done with decorative tiles. Flooring is the first thing that attracts guests when they enter your home. It used to be that tiles were restricted to the kitchen and bathrooms, but now every free space is filled with tiles to enhance the aesthetics.

Did you know????

“India ranks at number 3 concerning the production of tile in the world”.

Many companies manufacture marble materials for home decor. All these options create confusion and hurdle us a little bit. We have arranged a list of the top 10 best brands of tile companies in India after researching, and analyzing the customer review, and the quality of the material they serve.

Best Tiles Brands in India

Here goes a list of the best tile companies out of dozens of brands prevailing in the market.

1. Kajaria Ceramics Tiles

Kajaria Ceramics Ltd has gained significant expertise and industry experience in home décor products. It is India’s most prominent ceramic/vitrified tile manufacturer and the 8th largest worldwide. They provide tiles of far better quality than other tile companies in India. Therefore, Kajaria Ceramics is ranked 1st among the best tile brands in India.

The company was founded in 1985 and has nine plants in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh. The head office is in New Delhi. The company made a public offering in September 1988 to set up a factory in Sikandrabad, Uttar Pradesh. Commercial production at this unit commenced in August 1988. Over the years, the company expanded its capacity in stages. Starting with just 12,000 TPA in 1988, the total installed capacity (at both the Sikandrabad and Alwar units) increased to 160,000 TPA by 1999.

The company’s annual production capacity is 70.40 million square meters (MSM). It holds around 10-11% of the market share in the entire tile industry. Additionally, the company offers bathroom solutions, including sanitaryware and faucets. It exports to Europe, West Asia, and SAARC countries and plans to tap into the export potential in Australia, South Africa, Vietnam, North America, and Singapore.

Kajaria is a mid-cap company with a market capitalization of ₹14,959.61 Crore. The brand has built public trust and received a green certificate for its commitment to eco-friendly practices.

Today, if you ask anyone in the market about the best ceramic tile brand in India, Kajaria is likely to be mentioned. The company is the best ceramic tile producer and manufacturer in India. The ink used in manufacturing these tiles is specially imported from foreign countries to give the tiles a natural look.

The company employs a unique strategy in organized retailing, such as mock bathrooms, kitchens, and living rooms. It has also invested ₹25 million in Kajaria Plus Limited, making this ceramic product marketing company its subsidiary.

Milestones:

  • Kajaria became India’s first ceramic tile company accredited with ISO 9002.
  • The company won the prestigious Capexil Special Export award (for the highest export made in a year) three times: in 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1997. It also received the award again for 1999-2000.
  • The company has become the world’s most certified ceramic tile company internationally.
  • In the Premium Tiles category, the company won the “Asia’s Most Promising Brand” tag, standing out among thousands of companies in the Indian market.
  • The Indian Green Building Council has awarded the company for manufacturing eco-friendly products.

Specification

Good about Kajaria Ceramics Tiles

  • Long-lasting nature
  • Smooth surface
  • Mesmerizing patterns
  • Supreme material quality

Did You Know?

China is the world’s largest producer, consumer, and exporter of ceramic tiles. As of 2019, China was the largest manufacturer of ceramic tiles globally, producing approximately 5.2 billion square meters. In comparison, India ranked as the second-largest producer, with 1.27 billion square meters produced in 2019, while its consumption stood at 960 million square meters.

2. H & R Johnson

H & R Johnson is a BSE-listed division of Prism Cement Limited. It is India’s number one and the world’s 7th largest tile manufacturer. The public company was founded on January 25, 1958, and its registrar’s office is in Mumbai. Its authorized share capital is ₹40 Crores, while its paid-up capital is ₹12.39 Crores.

H & R Johnson has over 1,000 exclusive dealers, more than 10,000 sub-dealers, 35 branches, and several House of Johnson showrooms to ensure its products are accessible nationwide. Additionally, the brand offers after-sales support through its Pan-India customer service. The company also has franchises in Bangladesh, the UAE, South Africa, Sri Lanka, and Nepal.

Johnson operates the most modern manufacturing units across India, using the highest quality raw materials to deliver a delightful and lasting experience. All their plants are ISO-compliant, with certifications for both ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, as well as OHSAS 18001.

H & R Johnson’s annual production is 70.40 million square meters (MSM). With 13 manufacturing units across India, the company boasts one of the country’s largest manufacturing capabilities. Today, HRJ is the only company in India to offer end-to-end solutions for tiles, sanitaryware, bath fittings, and engineered marble & quartz.

Achievements:

  • H & R Johnson (India) won the “Economic Times Best Brand – 2019” award.
  • The company was awarded the title of Superbrand in India for 2019 and 2021.

Specification

Good about Johnson tiles

  • Germ-free
  • Easy to Clean
  • Admirable looks

3. Simpolo Tiles

Sompolo tiles have developed into one of the world’s finest ceramic and vitrified tiles. It began by producing tile and marble in 1997. Simpolo has a presence in more than 45 countries across the globe. The company has served its customers the finest and highest quality floor tiles. The wide range of products includes decorative roofing tiles and attractive floor tiles.

History

  • In 1991, Simpolo entered the Sanitaryware segment with a 400-unit per day production plant, which grew to 700 by 1993.
  • In 1995, they established a ceramic tiles factory with a 1000 square meter production capacity. 
  • In 1999, they installed a new facility for Sanitaryware with 900 units per day.
  • In 2004 Simpolo’s ceramic venture expanded to a capacity of 5000 meters per day. 
  • In 2008, they became a manufacturer of vitrified tiles and established a double-charge plant that produces 8000 square meters per day.
  • By 2012, it established a new 14000 square meter double-charged vitrified tile factory with an 800 x 800 square meters capacity to protect the Indian market from China.

Achievement

  • Simpolo Tiles introduced the first innovative tabletop in India in 2003.
  • In 2008, the brand developed the first stain-free tiles with Nano Technology.
  • With Alaska Whites, they introduced the white tiles into the world. Moreover, it introduced the color body glazed vitrified tiles in India for the first time.
  • Introducing the Rock deck tiles, India’s most robust outdoor tiles, made way for a new era in tiles.

Is SIMPOLO a foreign brand or product?

No, SIMPOLO is an Indian company, and the product is made in India. The main plant of the company is in Morbi, Gujarat. At present, actor Hrithik Roshan is the brand ambassador 

Awards

  • Rising Star 2012
  • “Power Brand’s Leadership – Rising Entrepreneur of the Year Award 2012”
  • “The Udhyog Patra Award” for Efficient and practical Entrepreneurship
  • “Bhartiya Udhyog Ratna ” Award for Industrial Progress.

Specification

Good about the Simpolo Tiles

  • Long-lasting nature
  • Admirable looks
  • Stain-resistant
  • Smooth surface

4. Somany Ceramics Limited

Somany Ceramics Limited (previously SPL Ltd) is a part of H L Somany Group and is into ceramic tiles manufacturing. Founded in 1968 by the Kolkata-based Somany Group in collaboration with the UK-based Pilkington Tiles. In 1995, Pilkington Tiles divestiture his entire stake in SPL Ltd., and the total control of the company was vested in the hand of Somany Group.

Somany Ceramics operates in the Building Materials sector. It is a Small Cap company(with a market cap of Rs 2,406.59 Crore). The company’s main Products/Revenue Segments include Ceramic Floor & Wall Tiles, Other Operating Revenue, and Scrap for the year ending 31-Mar-2021.

Somany Ceramics is a manufacturer and trader of complete decor solutions. Its extensive range includes:

  • Ceramic walls and Floor Tiles.
  • Polished Vitrified Tiles.
  • Glazed Vitrified Tiles.
  • Sanitary ware Bath Fittings.
  • Allied products.

The corporate head office of Somany ceramics is in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. It has manufacturing plants in Kassar (Haryana), Kadi, and Morbi (Gujarat). The company’s annual production is 60 million square meters (MSM). It is the second-largest ceramic tile manufacturer in India.

The company’s operation is spread across the Middle East, Russia, Africa, India, and the United Kingdom. They stepped into manufacturing Vitrified Tiles in 1999-2000 and put up a Floor Tiles plant at Kadi from 2000-01. In the production of Verified porcelain tiles, the company has a capacity of one million square meters per year.

Milestones

  • The R&D department of the company is the first in this field to be recognized by the Govt of India.
  • The company (Kadi plant) has been awarded OHSAS certification, which shows risks associated with health and safety is very little in manufacturing the material.
  • The brand is awarded Asia’s most promising brand for 2012 and 2013.

Specification

Good about Somany Ceramic Tiles

  • Waterproof
  • Chemical-Resistant
  • Long-lasting nature
  • Smooth surface

5. Orient Bell

Orient Bell Limited was established as a public limited company in 1977. To manufacture ceramic tiles, K C Kejriwal partnered with AGRDB Germany. The former collaborators and the Indian promoters failed to produce any saleable tiles.

Somany-Pilkingtons took it over in 1981 as part of the rehabilitation package from IFCI, and it has since repaid all its debts under the agreement. After Somany-Pilkingtons sold its assets in 1993, Mahendra K Dag was in charge. In 1998-99, the company introduced the largest wall tiles in India, measuring 400mm x 300mm.

It was the first company to hire an in-house European designer and has several manufacturing plants in North West and South India. The head office of the company is in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. It is a Small Cap company (having a market cap of Rs 790.04 Crore) operating in the Building Materials sector. Available sections for tiles are Ceramic, Vitrified, and Digital Tiles that cover the entire range of applications for your living and working spaces.

The main revenue-generating segment of the company includes Tiles Ceramic and Other Operating Revenue for the year ending 31-Mar-2021. Its authorized share capital is Rs. 55 Crores, and its paid-up capital is Rs. 14.4 Crores. It is involved in the Quarrying of stone, sand, and clay.

It is the first company to hire an in-house European designer and has several North West and South India manufacturing plants. The manufacturing plants are at three key locations: Sikandrabad in UP, Hoskote in Karnataka, and Dora in Gujarat.

Awards

  • The company was awarded “Indian Green Building Council (GRIHA)”, because of producing eco-friendly products.
  • Awarded for outstanding sales generation in 2016
  • Awarded for investments and contributions to the world of the Tile industry
  • Awarded as one of the Best Tile Research industries.

Specification

Good About Orient Bell Tiles

  • Tough and strong
  • Smooth surface
  • Scratch resistance
  • Supreme material quality
  • Slip-resistant

6. CERA India Ltd

In terms of quality manufacturing, few companies have a great hand, and Cera ltd is one of those brands. The company was founded in 1980. Since then, they have been producing high-grade products. The company is prevalent in the field of Tile Manufacturers in India. The principal head office of the company is in Ahmedabad, Gujrat.

The company is a pioneer in using natural gas to provide additional sheen to its products. The natural gas component of Cera’s manufacturing process accounts for 18-20% of the total cost basket. The company has long-term contracts with Sabarmati Gas and GAIL (India) to secure gas supplies. Prices and quantities of gas are influenced by availability, international pricing, and contracts.

Cera Ltd is one of the best manufacturers of sanitary ware, faucets, tiles, and allied products. The company offers various good choices, including HD digital wall tiles with matching floor tiles, digital glazed vitrified tiles, and vitrified tiles with nanotechnology.

The tile industry in India has been estimated at Rs 22,000 crore, of which 55 percent of sales come from South India. As of 2014-15, Cera India has a turnover of Rs 822 crore, about 60 percent came from sanitaryware, 16 percent from faucet ware, 12 percent from tiles, and the rest from lifestyle products.

Besides expanding its domestic presence, the company has entered overseas markets. Cera Ltd has already set up a showroom in Dubai and opened a warehousing facility in Sharjah to cater to the UAE market.

Achievements

  • The business was certified by India’s most preferred home solutions provider in 2015-2016 by CREDAI.
  • CERA was also conferred Power Brand for two years, in 2012 and 2013. The award was presented to the top 100 brands in the country.
  • The “Asia’s Most Promising Brand” award for 2012-2013.
  • CERA has won the Readers’ Digest Trusted Brand Survey Gold Award in the bathroom & fittings and sanitaryware category in keeping with its tradition of innovation.
  • CERA received Product of the Year awards for Cerenity in 2014, Sanitaryware & Bathroom Fittings in 2013, Nano Technology in 2012, and Snow White Range in 2011.

Specification

Good about Cera Sanitaryware Ltd

  • Scratch resistance
  • Waterproof
  • Stain-resistant
  • Tough and strong

7. Asian Granito

Build your room as you imagine and create the most fantastic place in the world with Asian Granito tile. The quality of constantly innovating and ‘leading the change’​ has made AGL one of the best ceramic companies in the area of home decoration.

The Company was founded on 8 August 1995 as “Karnavati Fincap Private Limited” to carry on the business of a non-banking financial company. Subsequently, the Company went public on 29 August 1995. After that, the Company’s business line changed from finance to trading in cloth and was accordingly renamed Panchariya Textile Industries Limited on 18 March 1999.

On 28 July 2000, the Company changed its name to Vasudev Textile Industries Limited. In September 2002, the promoters of Asian Tiles Limited acquired the Company’s entire shareholding. After that, the Company’s line of business changed from trading in cloth to Ceramic tiles and was accordingly renamed Asian Granito India Ltd. 

The market cap of the company is around 506 Crores. The main revenue deriving Segments of the company includes Tiles, Export Incentives, and Wind Mills for the year ending 31-Mar-2021. Regarding the quality of the tile, the company serves one of the best durable tiles in the Indian market. Its products include:

  • Vitrified tiles.
  • Ceramic floor tiles.
  • Glazed vitrified tiles.
  • Digital wall tiles.
  • Composite marble tiles.
  • Quartz tiles.

The Company has a global presence in more than 100 countries. The ultra-modern plants of the Company are spread over an area of 3,20,000 sq. mt. The Company has nine manufacturing units spread across Gujarat. Its distribution and marketing network has more than 1,300 direct dealers and 500+ exclusive showrooms across India.

The company is the first to introduce the following products:- 

  • 450×450 outdoor tile with 12 mm thickness, 
  • 9-colour printing technology,
  • Online vitrified technology,
  • Slab vitrified tiles of 905mm x 905mm,
  • Large format wall and vitrified tiles.

Awards

2015:

  • Indian Stonemart Best Overall Display
  • The Economic Times’ Most Promising Brand.

2016:

  • Architecture+ Mega Brand of the Year.

2017:

  • Architecture+ Mega Brand of the Year
  • Fortune India The Next Fortune 500
  • Greentech Foundation Greentech Environment Award
  • Highest Productivity in a Summit of Vibrant Ceramics

2018:

  • Gujarat Brand Leadership Award
  • Fortune India The Next Fortune 500 
  • The Expert’s Choice Award

2019:

  • The Expert’s Choice Award
  • Reader’s Digest Most Trusted Brand 2019

2021

  • ET Industry Leader
  • GRIHA Council Showcasing our Vitrified & Ceramic Tiles in their catalog from 2021-2023

Specification

Good about Asian Granito Tiles

  • Good Quality
  • Durable
  • Tough and strong

8. Bajaj Tiles

Bajaj Tiles is one of the best tile brands in India. The company began its journey with the manufacturing of Ceramics Tiles. The first plant established under the Bajaj group was in 1990 as M/s ALFA CERAMICS. The company captured a huge market base, and due to heavy demand for products, they established 2nd plant and 3rd plant as M/S YASHICA CERAMICS and M/s SIGMA CERAMICS in 1996.

The head office of the company is in Gujrat. The company has numerous manufacturing models in PAN India, which generate tiles of 75,000 sqm per day. The company is currently exporting its products to customers spread across 27 countries.

The company has created high benchmarks in various categories of products: electronics, automobiles, sanitaryware, and floor tiles. It is among the renowned and Leading tiles-making Brands in India. The company’s product portfolio includes digital wall tiles, glazed, polished porcelain, and heavy-duty industry tiles used for walls and floors.

The company uses imported machinery from Europe, employing advanced Italian technology to ensure global quality products. All the company’s products are certified with ISO 9001:2000.

Specification

Good about Bajaj Tiles

  • Easily affordable
  • Admirable looks
  • Tough and strong
  • Scratch resistance

9. NITCO Tiles

NITCO is one of the most widely recognized brands and the only company in the world with a presence on all three surfaces: namely, tiles, marble, and mosaic. In tiles, the company’s main product is flooring tile. Previously known as Nitco Tiles, the company is one of India’s largest flooring tile manufacturers. 

The company began its journey in the year 1953. It was formed as a partnership firm with the purpose of manufacturing mosaic tiles. Today their extended product segment includes ceramic tiles, vitrified tiles, mosaics, marble, cement terrazzo tiles, and cement. Their manufacturing unit is in Alibaug (Maharashtra), with an installed capacity of 0.18 million metric tons per annum.

The head office of the company is in Mumbai. Their pan-India presence is facilitated through 15 offices. It has four factories and various offices in major cities. The company has a distribution network of 18 depots, 750 direct dealers, and over 5000 retail outlets across the country. 

History

  • In 1984, they began processing marble imports in India and distributing it in Kanjur Marg.
  • In March 1995, the company built its Greenfield plant to manufacture ceramic floor tiles in Alibaug, Maharashtra. The plant cost Rs 900 million.
  • On January 25, 1996, Nitco Tiles Ltd. became a public limited company.
  • In the year 1997, they started full-scale commercial production at Alibaug Maharashtra with a capacity of 10000 sq. Mts. Per day.
  • The company merged with Mahalaxmi Tiles & Marble Company Pvt Ltd in 2001, a manufacturer of mosaic tiles with a capacity of 7.4 million square feet per year.
  • In 2002, the company set up a unit in Silvassa to process and sell imported marble. 
  • In 2004, the company started producing paving tiles.
  • In 2005-06, the company increased its production capacity of Mosaic Tiles from 84.86 sq ft to 90.88 sq ft.
  • The company set up six windmills of 7.5 MW at Dhule in Maharashtra in March 2006. They also increased ceramic floor tile capacity by 56% and commissioned it in May 2006.

Achievements

  • “NITCO has won the 20th Rank of “Dream Company To Work For Award” held by World HRD Congress 2013 ”
  • Has been awarded by Capexil awards for innovation and design.
  • The company holds two Construction World Awards.

Highlights

  • The super-gloss scratch-proof tiles resist dirt and bacteria.
  • Tile finishes from glazed to glossy, matte to rustic, and much more.
  • The brand comes from top tier floor tiles manufacturer in India.

Specification

Good about Nitco Tile Ltd

  • Easily affordable
  • Admirable looks
  • Tough and strong
  • Resist dirt and bacteria

10. Swastik Tiles

Another name queued in this list of best tile brands in India is Swastik Tiles. It is a private limited company. The company manufactures and sells digitally printed wall and floor tiles. There are four manufacturing units of the company spread across India. The head of the company is in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India.

The company’s products range from unglazed polished vitrified tiles, digital glazed polished vitrified tiles, unpolished tiles, external tiles, digital double fast-fired, glazed wall tiles, to Gres vitrified wall tiles.

Highlights

  • The company is one of the highest producers of parking and elevation tiles in the industry.

11. Regent Granito (India) Ltd.

The Regent Granito Limited rings a definite bell in India when it comes to sophisticated tile products. Having been established in 2004, it had since ruled the top list of the leading Indian tiles brands.

In a short span of time, it had proven its worth as a popular item in the flooring market. It is an ISOQAR ISO 9001: 2008 / ISO 14001: 2004 awarded company.

The company is also known for preserving unique ingredients for its item quality. Currently, the company projects revenue of 150 Crore and has a manufacturing potential of 18000 Sq.mtrs. Of Vitrified Tiles daily. It is located in Himatnagar, Gujarat.

12. Sonata Ceramics Ltd.

The Sonata Clay Limited Company reigns in the list of the top tiles brands in India. An ISO 9001-2008 certified company; it owns manufacturing models in PAN India.

It produces top-quality products at affordable prices using innovative technology. It has a vast submission system that is integral to its market growth. Its main corporate office is located in Himatnagar, Gujarat.

What are Ceramic Tiles?

Ceramic tiles are made of red or white day. These tiles can be used in several areas of the house.

These tiles are thin and may break at high pressure. Despite these differences, Ceramic tiles are commonly used for floors, countertops, and walls.

A special glaze coat protects improves its look. This feature is the tile does not absorb stains which adds ups to its durability.

Facts about Ceramic Tiles

1. Most common materials used in today’s market.
2. These tiles are called green products because they do not harm the environment in any manner.
3. Since it is made up of clay and glass which can be recycled
3. Morbi, a small city in Gujarat is the hub of manufacturing tiles where 70 percent of ceramic tiles in India are made

Which Types of Tiles are best for the floor?

The best and most commonly used floor tiles are Vitrified tiles. Since they are durable and can withstand heavy traffic.
These tiles are one of the best alternatives to marble and granite flooring. They are easy to maintain in comparison with other types of tiles. These tiles resist scratches and discoloration

Conclusion

We are wrapping up the list of India’s top 10 tile companies. Suggest in the comments to add more to the best tile brands in India. Provide your valuable feedback if you are using any of them. Share this list with your friends.

Lastly

After Exploring these Best Tiles brands in India, bring home an exquisite piece of splendor. Make your home look fantastic by using the superb quality of these branded tiles. I would recommend using these best-branded tiles in your home. So go and get these wonderfully designed products to beautify your home handsomely.

title.rendered: Top 24 Steel Companies and Plants in India (2026)

content.rendered:
India is the world’s second-largest steel producer, and its biggest plants rank among the largest steelworks anywhere. This guide profiles the industry honestly in two parts: first the 10 steel companies that anchor the sector, then the 14 largest individual plants, one by one. Every capacity figure is taken from an official source — a company annual report, an official company statement or a government release — and is dated, because expansions keep changing the order.

Two names in the company list need a health warning. Essar Steel and Tata Steel BSL appear in older rankings, but neither exists as an independent company today: Essar Steel became AM/NS India in December 2019, and Tata Steel BSL was merged into Tata Steel in November 2021. Their plants are still very much running, and both are profiled below under their current owners.

Quick answer

  • India produced 152.18 million tonnes of crude steel in FY2024-25, second only to China (Press Information Bureau).
  • The largest single plant is JSW Steel’s Vijayanagar Works in Karnataka, at 17.5 MTPA crude steel capacity (FY2024-25).
  • The largest company by capacity is JSW Steel, with 35.7 MTPA consolidated crude steel capacity in FY2024-25.
  • India’s installed crude steel capacity reached 200.3 MTPA in 2024-25 (Ministry of Steel), against a policy target of 300 MTPA by 2030-31.
  • This article covers 10 companies and 14 plants. Two listed companies no longer exist independently, and the text says so where it matters.

India’s steel industry in numbers

The sector figures below come from the Ministry of Steel and the Press Information Bureau. They frame the company and plant profiles that follow: a fast-growing industry, still well short of the capacity its own policy targets.

  • Crude steel production, FY2024-25: 152.18 million tonnes (PIB), keeping India second in the world behind China.
  • Installed crude steel capacity: 200.3 MTPA in 2024-25, provisional (Ministry of Steel / Joint Plant Committee).
  • Finished steel consumption, FY2024-25: 152.13 million tonnes, up 11.6% on the previous year (PIB).
  • National Steel Policy 2017 targets for 2030-31: 300 MTPA of crude steel capacity, 255 million tonnes of production and 158 kg per-capita finished steel consumption.
  • Public sector: SAIL (about 20 MTPA) and RINL (7.3 MTPA liquid steel) are the two government-owned steelmakers on this list.
  • Private sector: JSW Steel and Tata Steel together account for the majority of the large integrated capacity profiled here.

Top 10 steel companies in India

The ten companies below are listed in the order the original guide used. Capacities are crude steel capacity for FY2024-25 unless a different measure is named. Two entries, Tata Steel BSL and Essar Steel, are status updates rather than live companies, and are labelled as such.

1. JSW Steel

JSW Steel is India’s largest steelmaker by capacity. Consolidated crude steel capacity stood at 35.7 MTPA in FY2024-25, including 1.5 MTPA in the USA; capacity within India was 34.2 MTPA. Consolidated crude steel production reached 27.79 million tonnes in FY2024-25, the company’s highest ever. Its integrated plants are Vijayanagar in Karnataka, Dolvi in Maharashtra and Salem in Tamil Nadu, and the company has stated a target of about 50 MTPA of domestic capacity by FY2030-31.

Key facts

  • Headquarters: JSW Centre, Bandra-Kurla Complex, Mumbai
  • Consolidated crude steel capacity: 35.7 MTPA (FY2024-25)
  • Crude steel production: 27.79 million tonnes in FY2024-25, a record
  • Site capacities (FY2024-25): Vijayanagar 17.5 MTPA, Dolvi 10 MTPA, Salem 1.15 MTPA
  • Stated target: about 50 MTPA domestic capacity by FY2030-31

2. Tata Steel

Tata Steel runs India’s oldest steel business and its second-largest Indian capacity. Crude steel capacity in India was 26.6 MTPA in FY2024-25, with a further 8.7 MTPA overseas, giving a group total of about 35 MTPA. Indian crude steel production hit a record 21.68 million tonnes in FY2024-25. The Indian business rests on three large sites, Jamshedpur, Kalinganagar and Meramandali, all profiled in the plants section, and the company has stated an ambition to raise Indian capacity to 40 MTPA.

Key facts

  • Registered office: Bombay House, Fort, Mumbai
  • India crude steel capacity: 26.6 MTPA (FY2024-25); group about 35 MTPA
  • India crude steel production: 21.68 million tonnes in FY2024-25, a record
  • Site capacities: Jamshedpur 11 MTPA, Kalinganagar 8 MTPA, Meramandali 5.6 MTPA
  • Stated ambition: 40 MTPA crude steel capacity in India

3. Jindal Steel

The company long known as Jindal Steel & Power shortened its name to Jindal Steel Limited in 2025, with the change effective from July 2025 following Registrar of Companies approval. Liquid steel capacity was 9.6 MTPA in FY2024-25, with an expansion programme designed to take it to 15.6 MTPA. The company reported production of 8.12 million tonnes in FY2024-25, its highest ever. Its steel plants are at Angul in Odisha and Raigarh in Chhattisgarh, with a further unit at Patratu in Jharkhand and a 9 MTPA pellet plant at Barbil in Odisha.

Key facts

  • Former name: Jindal Steel & Power Limited (renamed in 2025)
  • Registered office: O. P. Jindal Marg, Hisar, Haryana; corporate office in New Delhi
  • Liquid steel capacity: 9.6 MTPA (FY2024-25), expanding towards 15.6 MTPA
  • Production: 8.12 million tonnes in FY2024-25, a record (company presentation)
  • Steel plants: Angul and Raigarh; pellet plant at Barbil, 9 MTPA

4. Steel Authority of India (SAIL)

SAIL is India’s largest public-sector steelmaker and a Maharatna company, with the Government of India holding about 65% of its equity. Crude steel capacity is about 20 MTPA and crude steel production was 19.17 million tonnes in FY2024-25. SAIL operates five integrated steel plants — Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur and IISCO Burnpur — each profiled below, and its annual report sets out a roadmap to lift capacity towards 35 MTPA by FY2030-31.

Key facts

  • Headquarters: Ispat Bhawan, Lodhi Road, New Delhi
  • Ownership: Government of India, about 65%; Maharatna status
  • Crude steel capacity: about 20 MTPA (FY2024-25 annual report)
  • Crude steel production: 19.17 million tonnes in FY2024-25
  • Five integrated plants: Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur, IISCO Burnpur

5. Jindal Stainless

Jindal Stainless is India’s largest stainless steel manufacturer, in the company’s own words “India’s foremost and largest Swadeshi stainless steel manufacturer”. Melting capacity in India is 3.0 MTPA, split between Jajpur in Odisha (2.2 MTPA) and Hisar in Haryana (0.8 MTPA), and sales volume reached 2.37 million tonnes in FY2024-25. In March 2026 the company commissioned a 1.2 MTPA melt shop in Indonesia through a joint venture, taking group melting capacity to 4.2 MTPA including the 3.0 MTPA in India.

Key facts

  • Registered office: O. P. Jindal Marg, Hisar, Haryana; corporate office in New Delhi
  • India melt capacity: 3.0 MTPA — Jajpur 2.2 MTPA, Hisar 0.8 MTPA
  • Sales volume: 2.37 million tonnes in FY2024-25
  • Group melt capacity: 4.2 MTPA after the Indonesian melt shop commissioned in March 2026
  • Product focus: stainless steel only, unlike the carbon-steel makers above

6. Tata Steel BSL — no longer a separate company

Tata Steel BSL still appears in older top-10 lists, but it has not existed as a separate company since 2021. Under a composite scheme of amalgamation sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench, on 29 October 2021, Tata Steel BSL (formerly Bhushan Steel) was merged into Tata Steel Limited with effect from 11 November 2021.

Its one large asset, the integrated plant at Meramandali in Odisha, is therefore a Tata Steel plant today. It is profiled in the plants section as Tata Steel Meramandali, with a crude steel capacity of 5.6 MTPA.

Key facts

  • Status: amalgamated into Tata Steel Limited, effective 11 November 2021
  • Formerly: Bhushan Steel Limited
  • Plant operated: Meramandali, Dhenkanal district, Odisha
  • Meramandali crude steel capacity: 5.6 MTPA (now under Tata Steel)

7. Godawari Power and Ispat

Godawari Power and Ispat is an integrated steel and power producer based at Siltara in Raipur, Chhattisgarh. Its chain runs from captive iron-ore mining through iron-ore pellets, sponge iron and steel billets to ferro alloys and captive power, rather than large-scale crude steel. The company’s May 2025 presentation lists a 2.7 MTPA pellet plant, 0.594 MTPA of sponge iron capacity, 0.525 MTPA of steel billets and 0.4 MTPA of hot rolling capacity. It belongs in this list for the completeness of its integrated model, not for crude steel tonnage.

Key facts

  • Works and registered office: Industrial Area, Siltara, Raipur, Chhattisgarh
  • Pellet capacity: 2.7 MTPA (company presentation, May 2025)
  • Steel billets: 0.525 MTPA; sponge iron: 0.594 MTPA (May 2025)
  • Also produces: ferro alloys, H.B. wire and captive power
  • Raw material base: captive iron-ore mines

8. Electrosteel Castings

Electrosteel Castings is not a bulk steelmaker at all. It pioneered ductile iron (DI) pipes in India, setting up the first DI pipe plant in the Indian subcontinent, and describes itself as the country’s largest manufacturer of ductile iron fittings. Total production capacity is roughly 10 lakh tonnes a year across DI pipes, DI fittings and cast iron pipes, and its pipes serve water supply and sewerage networks. It appears in steel company lists because its foundries melt steel and iron at scale, but its tonnage is pipe tonnage, not crude steel.

Key facts

  • Head office: Camac Street, Kolkata; registered office at Rajgangpur, Odisha
  • DI pipe capacity: 9,00,000 tonnes per annum (company investor presentation)
  • Total capacity: about 10 lakh tonnes a year across pipes, fittings and CI pipes
  • Plants include: Khardah and Haldia (West Bengal), Srikalahasti (Andhra Pradesh), Elavur (Tamil Nadu)
  • Position: first DI pipe plant in the Indian subcontinent; largest DI fittings maker in India

9. Essar Steel India — now AM/NS India

Essar Steel India no longer operates. The company was taken through the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, and on 16 December 2019 ArcelorMittal and Nippon Steel completed their acquisition of it, creating ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India (AM/NS India), owned 60% by ArcelorMittal and 40% by Nippon Steel. The Hazira steelworks that Essar built is now AM/NS India’s flagship plant and is profiled in the plants section under its current owner. Any ranking that still lists Essar Steel as a live company is out of date.

Key facts

  • Status: acquired under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code; acquisition completed 16 December 2019
  • Successor: AM/NS India (ArcelorMittal 60%, Nippon Steel 40%)
  • Main asset transferred: the Hazira integrated plant, Gujarat
  • Hazira crude steel capacity today: 9 MTPA under AM/NS India

10. Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd. (RINL)

RINL, better known as Vizag Steel, is a Schedule-A central public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, wholly owned by the Government of India. It operates a single integrated plant, the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, with an installed capacity of 7.3 MTPA of liquid steel. In January 2025 the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a revival package of ₹11,440 crore for RINL — ₹10,300 crore as fresh equity and ₹1,140 crore of working-capital loan converted into preference capital — expressly to keep it running as a going concern.

Key facts

  • Headquarters: Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh
  • Ownership: Government of India, 100%; Ministry of Steel
  • Installed capacity: 7.3 MTPA liquid steel (PIB, January 2025)
  • Revival package: ₹11,440 crore approved in January 2025
  • Single-plant company: operates only the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant

The largest steel plants in India, one by one

Fourteen plants follow, in the order the original guide used. The table summarises them; the profiles give the detail. Capacities are crude steel unless the row says liquid steel, and each is the latest figure its operator or the government has published — several of these plants are mid-expansion, so treat the table as a dated snapshot, not a permanent ranking.

1. JSW Steel Vijayanagar Works — Toranagallu, Karnataka

Vijayanagar is the largest single-location steel plant in India, a description JSW Steel uses in its own reporting. Crude steel capacity stood at 17.5 MTPA in FY2024-25, a figure that includes 1.7 MTPA at the JSW Vijayanagar Metallics unit that was still under commissioning at the year end. A 5 MTPA expansion at that unit was commissioned and ramping up during the year, and a planned upgrade of Blast Furnace 3 is intended to take the site to 19 MTPA.

Key facts

  • Operator: JSW Steel
  • Crude steel capacity: 17.5 MTPA (FY2024-25), including 1.7 MTPA under commissioning
  • Status: India’s largest single-location steel facility (company statement)
  • Next step: Blast Furnace 3 upgrade planned to lift capacity to 19 MTPA

2. Jindal Steel Angul — Angul, Odisha

Angul is Jindal Steel’s growth engine and the plant most often misreported in rankings. Its steel melt shop capacity was 6.0 MTPA in FY2024-25, with an expansion to 12.0 MTPA under way — the 12 MTPA figure quoted in many lists is the target, not the achieved capacity. Angul also hosts what the company calls the world’s first and largest coal gasification plant for steelmaking, feeding a 1.8 MTPA direct reduced iron unit, and the chairman has stated an ambition to reach 25.2 MTPA by 2030.

Key facts

  • Operator: Jindal Steel
  • Steel melt shop capacity: 6.0 MTPA (FY2024-25), expanding to 12.0 MTPA
  • Direct reduced iron: 1.8 MTPA, using gas from the coal gasification plant
  • Company claim: world’s first and largest coal gasification plant for steelmaking
  • Stated ambition: 25.2 MTPA by 2030 (chairman’s statement, January 2025)

3. Tata Steel Jamshedpur — Jamshedpur, Jharkhand

Jamshedpur is India’s oldest integrated steel facility, described by Tata Steel as continuously operating for over a century. Steel production began here on 16 February 1912, four and a half years after the company was registered in August 1907, and the works has been rebuilt repeatedly since. Capacity today is 11 MTPA of crude steel (FY2024-25 environment statement), and Jamshedpur was the first site in India to receive ResponsibleSteel certification, later followed by Kalinganagar and Meramandali.

Key facts

  • Operator: Tata Steel
  • Crude steel capacity: 11 MTPA (FY2024-25)
  • Steel production began: 16 February 1912 (first blast furnace blown in December 1911)
  • Distinction: India’s oldest integrated steel facility; first ResponsibleSteel-certified site in India

4. JSW Steel Dolvi Works — Raigad, Maharashtra

Dolvi, on the Maharashtra coast near Mumbai, is JSW Steel’s second integrated plant. JSW acquired it in 2010 at 3.3 MTPA and has grown it by brownfield expansion since; a 5 MTPA expansion completed in FY2021-22 took capacity from 5 MTPA to the present 10 MTPA of crude steel. A further expansion, to 15 MTPA by September 2027, has been announced in the company’s FY2024-25 reporting.

Key facts

  • Operator: JSW Steel
  • Crude steel capacity: 10 MTPA
  • Growth: acquired at 3.3 MTPA in 2010; 5 MTPA expansion completed in FY2021-22
  • Announced: expansion to 15 MTPA by September 2027

5. AM/NS India Hazira — Hazira, Gujarat

Hazira is the flagship plant of AM/NS India, the joint venture that took over Essar Steel in December 2019. Crude steelmaking capacity is 9 MTPA, supported by 20 MTPA of pellet capacity, and the company calls Hazira one of the largest single-location flat steel plants in the world. An expansion of about 6 MTPA, taking Hazira to roughly 15 MTPA, was officially announced in September 2022 in two phases; the company’s long-term goal for the site is 24 MTPA.

Key facts

  • Operator: AM/NS India (ArcelorMittal 60%, Nippon Steel 40%)
  • Crude steel capacity: 9 MTPA; pellet capacity 20 MTPA
  • Earlier owner: Essar Steel, until December 2019
  • Expansion: about 6 MTPA announced in 2022, towards 15 MTPA; long-term goal 24 MTPA

6. Tata Steel Kalinganagar — Jajpur, Odisha

Kalinganagar is Tata Steel’s newest greenfield plant and the centrepiece of its recent growth. The first phase, 3 MTPA, was dedicated to Odisha in November 2015. Phase II lifted capacity to 8 MTPA: India’s largest blast furnace was commissioned at the site on 20 September 2024, and the expanded plant, built with an investment of ₹27,000 crore, was inaugurated on 22 May 2025.

Key facts

  • Operator: Tata Steel
  • Crude steel capacity: 8 MTPA after Phase II (2025)
  • Phase I: 3 MTPA, dedicated 18 November 2015
  • Phase II: India’s largest blast furnace commissioned 20 September 2024; inaugurated 22 May 2025

7. Visakhapatnam Steel Plant — Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh

The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant is RINL’s only plant and, as the Comptroller and Auditor General’s reporting records, the first shore-based integrated steel plant in India, sited on the coast to receive imported raw materials by sea. It began with 3 MTPA of capacity; the first blast furnace was dedicated in March 1990 and full-fledged operations commenced in 1992-93. Successive expansions have taken installed capacity to 7.3 MTPA of liquid steel.

Key facts

  • Operator: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd. (RINL)
  • Installed capacity: 7.3 MTPA liquid steel
  • Distinction: India’s first shore-based integrated steel plant
  • Milestones: first blast furnace dedicated 20 March 1990; full operations from 1992-93

8. Bhilai Steel Plant — Bhilai, Chhattisgarh

Bhilai, SAIL’s flagship, was established in 1955 with assistance from the former USSR and commissioned in 1959. After SAIL’s modernisation and expansion programme, the plant’s capacity stands at 7.5 MT of hot metal and 7 MT of crude steel (SAIL’s official plant particulars). Bhilai is best known as the rail plant: SAIL states it is India’s largest producer and supplier of rails for Indian Railways, rolling single-piece rails 130 metres long and welded panels of 260 metres.

Key facts

  • Operator: SAIL
  • Capacity after modernisation: 7 MT crude steel; 7.5 MT hot metal
  • Commissioned: 1959, built with assistance from the former USSR
  • Speciality: rails — India’s largest rail supplier to Indian Railways; 130 m single-piece rails

9. Tata Steel Meramandali — Dhenkanal, Odisha

Meramandali was built by Bhushan Steel and came to Tata Steel through the insolvency process: Bamnipal Steel, a Tata Steel subsidiary, acquired control on 18 May 2018 under the NCLT-approved resolution plan, and the operating company, renamed Tata Steel BSL, was merged into Tata Steel in 2021. The plant’s crude steel capacity is 5.6 MTPA, and Tata Steel’s environment statement records production of 5.19 million tonnes in FY2024-25. An expansion to 7.1 MTPA has been proposed through the environmental clearance process but is not current capacity.

Key facts

  • Operator: Tata Steel
  • Crude steel capacity: 5.6 MTPA; FY2024-25 production 5.19 million tonnes
  • History: built by Bhushan Steel; acquired by Tata Steel group in May 2018
  • Note: expansion to 7.1 MTPA proposed, not yet capacity

10. Bokaro Steel Plant — Bokaro Steel City, Jharkhand

Bokaro was built with Soviet collaboration, agreed in January 1965; its first blast furnace was commissioned on 2 October 1972 and the first 1.7 MT phase was completed in 1978. It is SAIL’s flat-products specialist, rolling hot and cold rolled coils and sheets, tin mill black plate and galvanised sheets. SAIL’s latest stated crude steel capacity for the plant is 4.65 MTPA, and an expansion to 7.25 MTPA of crude steel is under way — larger figures sometimes quoted for Bokaro (5.25 or 7.55 MTPA) are hot metal numbers, not crude steel.

Key facts

  • Operator: SAIL
  • Crude steel capacity: 4.65 MTPA (SAIL statement, 2026)
  • Built with Soviet collaboration; first blast furnace commissioned 2 October 1972
  • Products: flat products — HR and CR coils and sheets, galvanised sheets, tin mill black plate
  • Expansion: crude steel capacity planned to rise to 7.25 MTPA

11. Rourkela Steel Plant — Rourkela, Odisha

Rourkela was the first integrated steel plant in India’s public sector, set up with German collaboration at an initial 1 MTPA; its first blast furnace, Parvati, was lit in February 1959. Modernisation and expansion have taken it to 4.5 MTPA of hot metal and 4.2 MTPA of crude steel, and the modernised plant was dedicated in April 2015. Its output leans towards plates, hot rolled coils, ERW and spiral-welded pipes and cold-rolled non-oriented electrical steel.

Key facts

  • Operator: SAIL
  • Capacity after modernisation: 4.2 MTPA crude steel; 4.5 MTPA hot metal
  • Distinction: first integrated public-sector steel plant in India; German collaboration
  • First blast furnace operational: February 1959
  • Products: plates, HR coils, ERW and spiral pipes, CRNO electrical steel

12. Jindal Steel Raigarh — Raigarh, Chhattisgarh

Raigarh is Jindal Steel’s older integrated plant, rated at 3.6 MTPA in the company’s official FY2025-26 presentations. The site houses what the company documents describe as the world’s largest coal-based sponge iron (DRI) plant, and a 1 MTPA rail and universal beam mill that rolls rails up to 121 metres long, supplied as welded panels of up to 260 metres in normal and head-hardened grades. A plate-cum-coil mill produces plates up to 3,500 mm wide.

Key facts

  • Operator: Jindal Steel
  • Capacity: 3.6 MTPA integrated steel plant (official presentation, August 2025)
  • Company claim: world’s largest coal-based sponge iron plant on site
  • Rail mill: 1 MTPA; rails rolled to 121 m, welded panels to 260 m
  • Plate-cum-coil mill: plates up to 3,500 mm wide

13. IISCO Steel Plant — Burnpur, West Bengal

IISCO is one of India’s oldest iron and steel names: the enterprise was established in 1918 and first produced iron at Hirapur, later Burnpur, in 1922. IISCO was amalgamated with SAIL on 16 February 2006 and renamed IISCO Steel Plant. A modernisation and expansion lifted crude steel capacity from 0.55 MTPA to 2.5 MTPA, and the modernised plant was dedicated to the nation on 10 May 2015. A further expansion, towards 7.1 MTPA, features in SAIL’s current project reporting, but 2.5 MTPA remains the plant’s capacity today.

Key facts

  • Operator: SAIL
  • Crude steel capacity: 2.5 MTPA after modernisation
  • Origins: established 1918; iron first produced at Burnpur in 1922
  • Modernised plant dedicated: 10 May 2015
  • Caution: the 7.1 MTPA figure in project documents is a proposed expansion, not current capacity

14. Durgapur Steel Plant — Durgapur, West Bengal

Durgapur was set up with British collaboration in 1959 at 1 MTPA of crude steel. Modernisation in the 1990s took it to 1.8 MTPA, and the recently completed modernisation and expansion plan set present capacity at 2.45 MTPA of hot metal and 2.2 MTPA of crude steel (SAIL). The plant is a long-products specialist and, in SAIL’s words, the only producer of forged railway wheels and axles in the country, supplying Indian Railways from its wheel and axle plant.

Key facts

  • Operator: SAIL
  • Present capacity: 2.2 MTPA crude steel; 2.45 MTPA hot metal
  • Set up: 1959, with British collaboration, at 1 MTPA
  • Speciality: forged railway wheels and axles — the only producer in India (SAIL)

How to read these numbers

Steel statistics mix several different measures, and most misleading rankings come from confusing them. The points below explain the basis of every figure in this article.

  • Capacity is not production. Capacity is what a plant could make in a year; production is what it did make. Both are given above, each labelled.
  • Crude steel, liquid steel and saleable steel differ. Liquid steel is measured at the melt shop, crude steel after casting, and saleable steel after finishing losses. RINL’s 7.3 MTPA is liquid steel; most other figures here are crude steel.
  • Figures are dated on purpose. Most capacities are FY2024-25 values from annual reports and official statements. Where a newer official statement exists, its date is given instead.
  • Expansions change the ranking. Angul (to 12 MTPA), Dolvi (to 15 MTPA), Hazira (to about 15 MTPA) and Bokaro (to 7.25 MTPA) are all mid-expansion, so this order will not hold for long.
  • Not all tonnage is comparable. Jindal Stainless melts stainless steel, Godawari Power and Ispat is pellet- and billet-led, and Electrosteel Castings makes pipes; none of those figures should be ranked against crude steel capacity.
  • Company totals and plant totals answer different questions. JSW Steel’s 35.7 MTPA is a group figure including overseas units; Vijayanagar’s 17.5 MTPA is a single site. This article counts 10 companies and 14 plants, and keeps the two lists separate.

Frequently asked questions

Which is the largest steel plant in India?

JSW Steel’s Vijayanagar Works at Toranagallu, Karnataka, with 17.5 MTPA of crude steel capacity in FY2024-25. JSW Steel itself describes Vijayanagar as the largest single-location steel-producing facility in India. The next largest single sites are Tata Steel Jamshedpur (11 MTPA) and JSW Steel Dolvi (10 MTPA).

Which is the largest steel company in India?

By capacity, JSW Steel: 35.7 MTPA consolidated crude steel capacity in FY2024-25, of which 34.2 MTPA is in India. Tata Steel is second on Indian capacity at 26.6 MTPA, and SAIL, at about 20 MTPA, is the largest public-sector steelmaker.

How much steel does India produce?

India produced 152.18 million tonnes of crude steel in FY2024-25 (Press Information Bureau), making it the world’s second-largest producer behind China. Installed crude steel capacity reached 200.3 MTPA in 2024-25, and finished steel consumption was 152.13 million tonnes.

What happened to Essar Steel?

Essar Steel India was resolved under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. ArcelorMittal and Nippon Steel completed its acquisition on 16 December 2019 and renamed the business AM/NS India, owned 60:40 between them. Its Hazira plant continues to operate at 9 MTPA under the new owner.

Is Tata Steel BSL still a separate company?

No. Tata Steel BSL, formerly Bhushan Steel, was amalgamated into Tata Steel Limited under a scheme sanctioned by the NCLT in October 2021, effective 11 November 2021. Its Meramandali plant now operates as Tata Steel Meramandali.

What is India’s 300 MTPA steel target?

The National Steel Policy 2017 targets 300 MTPA of crude steel capacity by 2030-31, alongside 255 million tonnes of production and 158 kg per-capita finished steel consumption. Against that target, installed capacity in 2024-25 was 200.3 MTPA, so roughly another 100 MTPA is expected to be added by the end of the decade.

excerpt.rendered: India is one of the world's largest steel producers, and construction alone accounts for over half of global steel consumption. This guide profiles the top 10 steel companies in India, led by JSW Steel, amid the push toward 300 MTPA of capacity by 2030-31.
