title.rendered: Top 10 Best English Newspaper in India (Unbiased)

content.rendered:
Best English Newspaper in India: What is happening with Indian news channels? All the media is busy showcasing the same issues on bad politics. Most of these news channels negatively portray the news.

Television media is not free for anyone. The central government runs the media. If you ask me what journalism is, my definition of the term is the freedom to write or show the news as it is, without adding any bias or personal views.

But nowadays, the credibility of Indian news channels, whether they are in Hindi or English, is compromised, and their journalism is highly biased. Television media operates on the motto of driving TRP ratings.

Best English Newspaper In India

1. The Hindu

The Hindu has its most extensive circulation base in southern India and is the most widely read English daily newspaper in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Telangana, and Karnataka.

If you are interested in political events happening in our country and the outside world, The Hindu newspaper provides in-depth coverage of all these topics.

The newspaper started as a weekly in September 1878 and eventually became a daily broadsheet newspaper. The Hindu is one of the best English dailies from South India.

Certified figures revealed by the Audit Bureau of Circulations state that it has had a total circulation of 1.4 million copies since December 2009. The company employs more than 1,600 workers and had a gross income of $40 million in 2010.

Good Aspects of the Newspaper

  • The Hindu newspaper is non-biased towards any religion, section, or political party.
  • Many institutes and teachers recommend it to students for enhancing their vocabulary.
  • When compared with ‘The Washington Post’ (online), The Hindu matches its quality with international newspapers.
  • The newspaper features sections like hardcore politics and news that would interest IAS aspirants.
  • The Hindu is an ideal option if you are looking to increase your vocabulary, as it includes tough or new words not commonly spoken or read.
  • If you are switching to The Hindu, be aware that it doesn’t feature candy pics or news related to Bollywood, except for one or two articles on the last page.
  • The major advantage of The Hindu is that it has fewer advertisements and covers a lot of local news, while maintaining solid national and international coverage with must-read editorials.
  • The newspaper allows writers to criticize, oppose, or present the other side of a particular government policy or any other act.
  • It is frequently read by businessmen, political analysts, and students preparing for competitive exams.
  • The Hindu newspaper is regarded as the best for capturing what is happening around you.
  • The newspaper avoids showcasing “nonsense news,” and its approach to covering news is far better than many other English dailies.

Other Information

  • Headquarters – Chennai
  • Editor – Suresh Nambath
  • Founder – G. Subramania Iyer
  • Publisher – N. Ram

2. The Indian Express

Moving further with the list of the best English newspapers in India, the next one in the list is The New Indian Express.

The name of the newspaper has been changed to The New Indian Express. Currently, The Indian Express is distributed in 22 cities across India, primarily in Southern India.

It is one of the oldest English newspapers in India. The newspaper was founded in 1931 and is owned by the Indian Express Group.

It is one of the best and highest-circulated Indian newspapers and is owned by the Indian Express Group.

The company has its head office in New Delhi, India. It distributes several widely circulated newspapers, including The Indian Express and The Financial Express in English, Loksatta in Marathi, and Jansatta in Hindi.

Good About Newspaper

  • The Pioneer newspaper is the first to provide insurance benefits to its readers.
  • It is famous among readers for its weekly entertainment magazine, Screen, which covers the latest news from Bollywood.
  • Approximately 5 lakh copies are circulated all over India, covering relevant day-to-day happenings.
  • The newspaper covers all the major highlights from around the world.
  • The Indian Express has partnered with The Economist to provide articles from the magazine, which would otherwise be expensive.
  • The newspaper features a page titled ‘Explained’, which provides in-depth coverage of the most important issues in the country.

Users Reviews:

Indian express contains less number of Bollywood and entertainment news as compared to ToI.

The Indian Express – The newspaper has two faces of bias. In South India, its title is The New Indian Express, and readers claim the newspaper is biased towards Congress’ center-left ideology. In South India, The New Indian Express is generally biased towards the BJP’s right-wing corporate ideology.

3. Hindustan Times

Popularly referred to as HT, Hindustan Times is the Leading Indian newspaper in the English language.

The newspaper history is linked with the independence campaign of India. It was published in 1924 by Sunder Singh Lyallpuri to support India’s freedom movement against British colonials.

Sunder Singh was also the founder of India’s Akali movement. The journey of the newspaper started from New Delhi before spreading its operations to different parts of India like Ranchi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Patna, Mumbai, and Chandigarh.

It is being owned by HT media and has been circulating more than one million copies daily. The newspaper has other publications to it like the Nandan, Mint, and Kadambani.

Good About Newspaper

  • Best English Newspaper In India for the readers in the north region of the country.
  • The newspaper delivers good content and has a standard like The Hindu newspaper.
  • It contains advertisements but not more than ToI’s advertisement area.

Users Reviews:

Hindustan Times – As per the users, the newspaper is a little bit biased towards Congress’ central left ideology, even though it has broad coverage across the country.

  • Headquarter– Kasturba Gandhi marg New Delhi, India
  • Editor– Sukumar Ranganathan

4. The Statesman

The Statesman, a broadsheet English daily. It is among India’s earliest English papers.

The Statesman newspaper has its headquarters at Kolkata and started its own magazine back in 1875.

The Statesman is deemed to be among the most famous papers and is also one of the Asian News Network participants(ANN). The Asian News Network represents a team of reputed newspapers across Asia.

The Englishman (based in 1821) was united with The Statesman in 1934. The Delhi edition of The Statesman started publication in 1931.

The Statesman Weekly is a summary of knowledge and views from the Kolkata and Delhi editions. Printed on airmail paper, it is common with subscribers outside India.

This firm began its publication in Kolkata and has grown to Siliguri, Delhi, and Bhuvaneshwar.

The Statesman has a reported circulation of about 200,000 daily copies, it remains one of India’s most venerated newspapers, and foreign media widely quote its news.

Good About Newspaper

  • The newspaper is known to be one of India’s best newspapers for its writing design, which is excellent for serious viewers that never like frilling around and fake information.
  • The Statesman is deemed to be one of the most prestigious newspapers.
  • Ideal paper for viewers who prefer news presented in concise with no-frills language.

Undoubtedly, it is among the most popular newspapers in the Northeastern region of the country. Also, it is one of the few Indian newspapers that are a part of the reputed team of Asia News Network (ANN).

5. The Economic Times

The Economic Times is an English-language Indian daily newspaper. The newspaper is one of the Largest business & financial newspapers in India. Bennett, Coleman, and the company publish this newspaper.

The Economic Times is just but another subsidiary of the Times group. It is one of the most famous and Best English Newspaper In India for business news.

It is an Indian-based newspaper that has been the first option for business people in India.

The newspaper plays a major role in international businesses and the ongoings of stock markets, making it a vital option for readers to look into regularly.

For those who are keen on learning about the financial condition of Indian or global business, it’s The Economic Times who has to have the upper hand.

It is one of the top business newspapers in the world and is loved by those who are keen on learning more about the subject.

The history of the Economic Times dates back to 1961. The newspaper currently has more than 8 lakh subscribers across India.

The daily content mainly focuses on financial markets, shares, India’s economic situation, commodities, and global finance.

The Salmon crimson paper’s aid portrays the newspaper. The salmon-pink paper characterizes the Economic Times, which was being used right from the start.

The corporate head office of the company is in Mumbai. It has 11 subsidiary offices located in India, including Delhi, Lucknow, Chennai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, Nagpur, Kolkata, and Chandigarh.

In June 2009, the firm for faculty students started a news channel. The channels give information related to economic facts and fiscal news of the world. The channel is led by the current Executive Editor of The Economic Times i.e Rahul Joshi.

Good About Newspaper

  • Ideal newspapers for business news.
  • The paper main content is based on financial markets, the Indian economy, International finance shares, commodities, and international finance.
  • Most checked out English financial newspaper for the businessmen.

6. The Telegraph

The Telegraph emerges as India’s top 10 English newspapers due to its unique and mostly unbiased news coverage. The newspaper is very famous, especially in the eastern states.

The ABP Private Limited owns the newspaper, which started its publications back in 1982 from Kolkata.

A few years after its foundation, the newspaper gained enough goodwill to become the most widely circulated English daily in the eastern region published from Kolkata.

Edwin Taylor, The design director of London’s The Sunday Times, gave the newspaper the standard to control mediocrity and poor performance. The paper is printed by media group Ananda Publishers closely associated with ABP Pvt. Ltd

The news published in the paper is from distinct sections including Sports, business, education, politics, lifestyle, and entertainment, etc.

The Telegraph has five distinct editions and it is printed from Guwahati (to cater to the entire northeast), Siliguri (for North Bengal and Sikkim), Jamshedpur, and Ranchi (for Jharkhand).

Highlights

  • In 2008, with a circulation of 484,971, the Audit Bureau of Circulations certified it to be the fastest-growing daily in eastern India.
  • The ABP Group publishes it, and the newspaper competes with The Times of India. The newspaper is ranks at number eight for being the most widely read English newspaper in India as per the Indian Readership Survey (IRS) 2019.
  • The newspaper is one of the most widely circulated English newspapers in India.
  • A sharp growth is reported in the newspaper’s subscription, and the newspaper is one of the fastest-growing dialing’s in the English language.
  • The newspaper has ceased its printing of the Bhubaneshwar & Patna Editions on 14 December 2018.
  • As per the survey done in 2008, the Telegraph is the fourth most-widely read English newspaper in India (after Times of India, Hindustan Times and The Hindu) with viewers of 2.9 million.
  • In accordance with the survey done by the National Readership Survey (NRS) 2006 * the newspaper has a readership of 746,000 in Calcutta.
  • Apart from printing in English, it is also published in Bengali and English periodicals like Anandamela, Unish-Kuri, Sananda, Anandalok, Desh magazine, Businessworld, The Telegraph in Schools and Career.

Good about Newspaper

  • The Telegraph has five distinct editions
  • Well if you are asking about English word quality than, the Telegraph newspaper will be a good choice.
  • The newspaper has added a new 16-page colored section called T2, this section covers Entertainment and lifestyle.

User Reviews

Well, if you are searching for a newspaper for English word quality than, I think the Telegraph is good.

I think if you consider the quality of language then the Hindu and the Telegraph are way ahead.

7. The pioneer

Moving forward with the list of the best newspapers in India. Next listed in the list is an English daily i.e The Pioneer.

It is the second oldest English newspaper being printed in India. The newspaper gets printed from Delhi, Lucknow, Bhubaneswar, Dehradun, Kochi, Bhopal, and Chandigarh.

The Pioneer was founded in 1865 by George Allen. He has been in the tea business in northeast India.

Mr. Chandan Mitra, the owner and chief editor of this newspaper, is also a member of the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh. 

The principal newspaper concentrates on the pro-right movements that emerge from the urban middle class.

Highlights

  • In 1872, Alfred Sinnett was the the editor of the newspaper. Although he was later to be known for his interest in theosophy, he oversaw the newspaper’s transformation to one of exercising significant influence in British India.
  • In 1874, the weekly Pioneer Mail became the Pioneer Mail and India Weekly News and also featured short stories and travel writings.
  • Before 1990, this newspaper was the newspaper of Lucknow. After that, the newspaper was taken over by Thapar Group. The newspaper became a national newspaper under the tenure of L. M. Thapar which started being published from Delhi.
  • In 2010, The Pioneer started a Hindi version in Lucknow.

Good about Newspaper

  • The newspaper is always publishing pro-BJP, nationality, and right-wing ideology.

8. Daily News and Analysis

The Diligent Media Corporation owns the newspaper. The Daily News and Analysis is an Indian tabloid.

The Daily News And Analysis started on July 30, 2005, in Mumba. It is one of the best English-language daily newspapers in India.

Diligent Media Corporation, an Essel Group company, is the owner of the newspaper. Throughout information, perspectives, investigations, and interactivity, the newspaper provides readers with a composite fair picture of the city, the country, and the world.

Good about Newspaper

  • It covers the areas of the young generation’s problem and focuses on the issues raised by them.
  • The DNA is the second most-read newspaper in Mumbai. The newspaper is the preferred choice of more than 1.5 million people.
  • Apart from the print edition, the DNA newspaper is a pioneer newspaper with a responsive and dynamic website.

9. Deccan Chronicle

South India’s most widely read newspaper. Deccan Chronicle Holdings Ltd owns the newspaper.

Deccan Chronicle begins its operation back in 1938 in Andhra Pradesh. It has expanded its operations to various Tamil Nadu cities, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Kerala, and Karnataka, including Anantapur, Karimnagar, Rajahmundry, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Nellore City in Chennai, Andhra Pradesh, and Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu.

10. The Asian Age

Asian Age is the only English newspaper from India to have an international edition. India’s international newspaper published from Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, and London, UK.

The Asian Age English newspaper of India claims to have a readership of more than one million people worldwide, and it also collaborates with several English dailies of the world.

excerpt.rendered: With television news widely seen as biased and driven by TRP ratings, this guide ranks the top 10 English newspapers in India for readers who want reporting as it is — led by The Hindu, the most widely read English daily across the southern states.

Pharmaceutical Companies at Bangalore:- Do you know, Pharmaceutical Industry in India is among the Biggest pharma industries in the world. It ranks 4th in the world, pertaining to the volume of sales.

The hub of pharma companies in India is in Bangalore city. Bangalore has always been seen as a pioneer, whether it is about manufacturing pharmaceutical products or exporting them to foreign countries.

Most of the pharma companies in Bengaluru are among the largest pharma companies in India.

The setups of Pharma Companies in this city are growing very fast and today its figure has crossed 150+ Pharmaceutical companies in Bangalore.

There will be no wrong if we say it as the center of pharma companies in India.

With this article, we will go through the list of Top 10 Pharmaceutical Companies at Bangalore. Thus, you will get to know about the 10 best Pharma Companies in Bangalore.

Currently, all these companies are working on providing better healthcare services to our country. So let’s start with the topic of the Top 10 Pharma Companies in Bangalore.

Top 10 Pharmaceutical Companies at Bangalore

1. Biocon Ltd

Biocon Limited began its journey in 1978 as a joint venture with Biocon Biochemicals Ltd.

They had the vision to make India independent and self-sufficient in the manufacturing of nutrition healthcare products.

The company is one of the best pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore.

The first major achievement of this company is to be the first company in India who manufacture and export enzymes to the USA and Europe.  Apart from this, this company created the first biosimilar Insulin Glargine pen in Japan.

They are globally recognized in providing advanced therapies for chronic diseases, where medical needs are largely unmet and the cost of treatment is also high.

Papain an enzyme found in papaya which is used to prevent beer from turning vague was the first launched product.

Following are some other main interventions: –

  • 2013: -They launched a biologic drug ALZUMAb to treat psoriasis.
  • 2014: -Invented the world’s first biosimilar drug CANMAb to treat breast cancer.
  • 2015: Launched hepatitis-C in the Indian market under the brand name CIMIVIR.

More than 9,200+ people are engaged in the working slots in about 120 countries. At the present time, the reins of this company are with Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw.

He is the founder as well as the current chairman of the company.

Specification

    2. Strides Pharma

    To begin with, Strides Pharma is a Pvt Limited company that was founded in 1990 by Arun Kumar.

    The company has its share listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India.

    Strides pharma is commonly named among the top pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore.

    Over the years, it has grown tremendously in this industry. The company is backed by research and developmental activities.

    The head office of this company is in Bangalore, India. There are seven manufacturing facilities including four US FDA-approved facilities.

    The company also has an in-house R&D infrastructure in Bengaluru, India.

    Dedicated and experienced professionals engaged in their R&D department facilitating their services in India and has a strong footprint across 100 countries.

    Mainly, they focus on the manufacturing of IP-led niche finished dosage formulations.

    Products manufactured by the company

    • General Tablets,
    • Sachets,
    • Ointments,
    • Soft and Hard Gelatin Capsules
    • Liquids [Oral Liquids)
    • Topicals [Ointment & Cream] and Powders

    The company is serving an exhaustive pipeline of generics drugs. They are among the leading players in the production of soft gel capsules.

    All the products written above are supplied in countries like Italy and the US.

    Specification

    3. Beckman Coulter

    The company has completed more than 80 years of serving better healthcare solutions to society.

    Established in 1935 as National Technical Laboratories to commercialize a pH meter, invented by  Caltech professor Arnold O. Beckman.

    This Pharmacy is among the best pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore.

    The company eventually grew a lot and today it has a strong team of over 12,000 people. It has its corporate head office in California, United States.

    More than 11,000 global associates are working diligently and with a selfless spirit to make the world a healthier place. Its balance sheet of 2017 shows a turnover of $ 5.8 billion for the entire year

    In 2011, Danaher Corporation took over Beckman Coulter. The company is engaged in developing, manufacturing, and marketing products.

    Thus, they simplify, automates, and innovates complex biomedical testing. It is operating in two sections: Diagnostics and Life Sciences.

    They have a diagnostic system for complex biomedical testing. In brief, the company is committed to advance better healthcare solutions, applying the power of science and technology.

    Specification

    4. Covance Pharmaceutical

    Covance begins operations as an independent entity and a publicly Limited company. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

    The company is one of the best pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore.

    Covance is a contract research organization (CRO) offering nonclinical, preclinical, clinical, and commercialization services to pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries.

    The company is headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey. Initially, they started as Environmental Sciences Corporation.

    Later In 1997, the business merged into a publicly traded company, after being spun off by Corning which was started in 1996.

    Reins to run this company are with LabCorp (an American company) who is employing more than 50,000 people in over 60 countries.

    The company is deriving huge profits having annual revenues of over $2 billion. Looking at all these, we can call this company one of the biggest pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore. 

    They claim to have the world’s largest central laboratory network. In 2018, LabCorp the holding of Covance was rated one of the best places to work by the Human Rights Campaign.

    The company uses animals to test their drugs and other chemical inventions.

    As a contract testing facility, Covance is essentially a laboratory to conduct a test on any animal for the right price. Due to this, they had to face a lot of criticism for violating animal rights.

    As part of its clinical and non-clinical development services, They offer drug development services across all phases of development and multiple pharmaceutical areas.

    Therapeutic areas served by the company

    • Cardiovascular, diabetes,
    • Endocrinology and nephrology, 
    • Immuno-oncology,
    • Infectious diseases and inflammation, 
    • Neuroscience, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), 
    • Oncology, rare diseases, pediatrics, and the development of companion diagnostics.

    Specification

    5. Mylan Pharma

    Mylan is one of the global pharmaceutical companies in Bangalore providing healthcare services to more than 7 billion people.

    They have a distribution channel of more than 7,500 products in their portfolio.

    This company has a huge market base providing its services in over 165 countries with a dedicated team of 35,000-strong. Began with a sole motto to heal all the sorrows in a person’s life. All they do is entreat better health and healing in society.

    Mylan is a global generic and specialty pharmaceutical company. The company is headquartered in the United States of America.

    In 2007, they entered the Indian pharmaceutical market and acquired Matrix Laboratories Limited. Also, Mylan took over a generics business of Germany-based Merck KGaA.

    After these acquisitions, the company improved its international rankings.

    The company jumped from the third-largest generic and pharmaceutical company in the United States to the second-largest generic and specialty pharmaceutical company in the world.

    Founded in 1961 by Milan Puskar and Don Panoz. The company went public on the OTC market in February 1973. The manufacturing plant of the company is in Bangalore City.

    Mainly, the company is engaged in the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients (API), oral solid dose (OSD), and injectables are manufactured.

    They serve a number of markets around the world and produce a wide range of products in therapeutic areas.

    Therapeutic areas served by the company

    • Oncology, Anaphylaxis,
    • Antiretrovirals, Cardiovascular,
    • Respiratory, Dermatology, Immunology,
    • Anesthesia And Pain Management,
    • Infectious Disease, Gastroenterology,
    • Diabetology/endocrinology, And Women’s Healthcare.

    A team of more than 3000 scientists is working coordinately to provide a solution for unmet medical needs. About half of their scientific operational workforce is based in India.

    In late July 2019, Pfizer agreed to spin off and merge its off-patent medicine division, Upjohn, with Mylan.

    After this, a new company called Viatris came into existence, held as one of Mylan’s subsidiaries. Thus, the company entered into a new pharmaceutical business with sales of around $20 billion.

    Specification

    6. Himalaya

    This is a Bengaluru-based company established by M Manal in 1930. The corporate office of the company is among the top 10 pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore.

    Himalaya is a famous name providing herbal ayurvedic medicine, Nutrition, Personal, and Baby Care products.

    Almost every Indian family uses its products. I know most of you will be familiar with Neem Face Wash of Himalaya. It is one of their most popular and well-known products.

    This company has a broad market in India, besides this, it also supplies its products to 106 countries across the world.

    The research and development team of this company consists of 290 researchers.

    The team advises compositions in the making of ayurvedic and herbal products. In 1955, the company launched a Hepatic drug, named Liv.52. It was the first product in the launch.

    Himalaya Drug Company is the subsidiary of Himalaya Global Holdings Ltd. The main head office of the company is located in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India.

    The founder of this corporation was M Manal. He started the corporation with a vision to commercialize the roots and herbs products being used in natural form earlier.

    As of 2015, the company derives about 50% of its revenue from the international market.

    Specification

    7. Syngene Pharma

    Another common name in this list of top 10 Pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore is Syngene. Began its journey in the production of pharmaceuticals in 1993.

    Biocon Limited is the parent company of Syngene. The company is one of the leading contract research organizations engaged in the manufacturing of pharmaceutical products.

    They have a strong corporate governance framework whose entire focus is on client satisfaction, quality, and safety.

    Leveraging its scientific skills, the company focuses on delivering significant value to the customers.

    In order to qualify international standards, they have a World-class infrastructure spread across 1.5 million sq ft.

    They ensure a safe and sociable working environment for their workers. To safeguard the environment, they adopt environment-friendly measures to reduce waste, controlling pollution, and producing safe products.

    An ISO 9001:2008, ISO 14001:2004 certified, the company promotes extended product lines with the tag Fortune 500.

    Recent Agreement Done By company

    In 2019, they have agreed with the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), a Government of India undertaking, for installing a Center for Advanced Protein Studies (CAPS)

    Awards

    • India Pharma Award 2019 – For “Excellence in Contract Research and Manufacturing Services” 
    • Utthama Suraksha Puraskar 2019
    • CMO Leadership Awards which was Granted by Life Science Leader Magazine in New York
    • FICCI CSR Award for Environmental Sustainability
    • Safe Workplace Champion Award was given on the occasion of the 8th Manufacturing Supply Chain Summit organized in New Delhi.
    • Best Leadership Development Program for Middle Management Award

    Therapeutic areas served by the company

    • Diabetology, Oncology
    • Rheumatology
    • Infectious diseases
    • Gastroenterology
    • Nephrology and Cardiology
    • Neuropsychiatry and Immunology

    Specification

    8. MEDREICH Ltd

    Another fully integrated pharmaceutical company is Medreich. The corporate office of this company is based in Bangalore.

    The company is one of the biggest pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore.

    It was started in 1976 by Rajeev Mehta, Keith De Souza, and CP Bothra. In 2015, Japanese company Meiji Holdings acquired the company with a total consideration of $290 million.

    Meiji Group is a leading Japanese conglomerate listed on the Tokyo stock exchange. The company’s brand name has not changed post the acquisition.

    They have a dedicated team of professionals which includes 75 scientists, working sincerely in the research and development of products. The company has about 500 products in its portfolio.

    Mainly, the company is engaged in the CMO & CDMO business, Manufacturing pharma products in various dosage forms, and caters to diverse Therapeutic areas. 

    Medreich has a global presence providing its service in India, Spain, and across 55 more countries. The company has 6 manufacturing facilities in India and 1 in Spain.

    They are exclusive manufacturers for Pfizer & GSK. Medreich has advanced state-of-the-art R&D centers with proven scientific competence to develop formulations. Mainly they produce Formulations for Wyeth & Sanofi.

    With more than 3000 employees worldwide, the company is growing fast while providing quality medicines to patients.

    Medreich has the in-house ability to ensure administrative compliance in regulated markets across the globe.

    Specification

    9. Adcock Ingram Ltd

    Adcock Ingram was incorporated as a pharmacy in 1890. This is one of the biggest pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore.

    Initially started its operation under the name EJ Adcock Pharmacy in Krugersdorp, South Africa.

    The company is the only local pharma company providing full-time care by offering pharmaceutical distribution solutions.

    Adcock Ingram is a leading South African pharmaceutical conglomerate, listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

    The Company manufactures and markets pharmaceutical healthcare products. Adcock Ingram is one of the leading suppliers for the private and public sectors markets.

    The company is the second-largest manufacturer in the private pharmaceutical market. Also the second largest supplier to the public sector.

    The main area of their operation is to supply antiretroviral (ARV) medicines to the public sector. Adcock Ingram is a committed supplier of significant care products to the public sector and hospitals. 

    Recently, the corporate has undertaken a capital expansion project costing R1.5 billion. The project includes three manufacturing facilities situated in Gauteng.

    Specification

    10. SPI Pharma

    SPI is a fully owned subsidiary of the British Foods company. They are among the worldwide leaders in custom formulation solutions for pharmaceutical manufacturers.

    The company is one of the leading pharmaceutical companies in Bangalore.

    For over 75 years, they are delivering highly engineered pharmaceutical products across the world.

    Working diligently and committed towards the formulation of innovative pharmaceutical products to meet patient needs.

    The company has a full-fledged testing center in Bangalore India. SPI drug Pharma capabilities include Formulation production development and Optimization product prototypes.

    The lab is equipped with state of art formulation equipment. They work on specialty solid oral dosage forms, orally disintegrated tablets and Mini OTC.

    As a global leader, SPI Pharma serves over 55 countries with formulation innovation. The corporate office of the company is situated in Wilmington.

    Jeanne Thoma is an experienced turnaround leader was the founder of the company.

    Specification

    11. Jubilant Drug Discovery and Development Services

    Jubilant Biosys Limited, the contract research arm of Jubilant Pharmova, runs an integrated drug discovery centre in Bengaluru. From its Yeshwantpur campus it offers end-to-end discovery services, from target identification and validation through medicinal chemistry, DMPK and toxicology to candidate selection, for pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients worldwide.

    The company works as a CRDMO, a contract research, development and manufacturing organisation, and reports more than 20 years of experience in drug discovery. Its research centres are in Bengaluru, Noida and Greater Noida, with a further site at Saint-Julien in France and a manufacturing plant at Nanjangud in Karnataka.

    Key facts:

    • Bengaluru centre: No. 96, Industrial Suburb, 2nd Stage, Yeshwantpur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560022
    • Incorporated: 10 February 1998 (registered office at Noida, Uttar Pradesh)
    • Parent company: Jubilant Pharmova Limited
    • Contact: bd@jubilantbiosys.com
    • Focus: integrated drug discovery, development and GMP manufacturing services

    12. Genotypic Technology

    Genotypic Technology is a Bengaluru genomics company that has provided next-generation sequencing, microarray and bioinformatics services since 1998. It supplies genomics solutions to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and to academic researchers worldwide, and describes itself as India’s first genomics company.

    Alongside its core sequencing work, the group has built specialist subsidiaries: Dhitiomics for molecular diagnostics and QTLomics for agricultural genomics. Its services cover nucleic acid extraction, qPCR, microarray analysis and Oxford Nanopore sequencing, run from its office at R.M.V. 2nd Stage in Bengaluru.

    Key facts:

    • Address: #259, Apurva, 4th Cross, 80 Feet Road, R.M.V. 2nd Stage, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560094
    • Founded: 1998
    • Contact: genomics@genotypic.co.in; +91 80 40538300
    • Services: NGS, microarray, qPCR and bioinformatics

    13. Manan Health Care Pvt. Ltd.

    The Manan Health Care Private Limited is a Pharma Company that was established and started in 2010.

    It earns a spot on the list of the major Bangalore pharma companies after four years of trial service.

    Within its very early years of service, the company was able to make good records in the market. Consequently, it was listed as one of the most promising countries in the world.

    14. SBF Healthcare and Research Centre (SHRC)

    SBF Healthcare and Research Centre is a Bengaluru treatment centre working in cancer and arthritis care since 2006. It was founded by the late Wing Commander (Dr) V. G. Vasishta and is built around SPMF Therapy, its patented Sequentially Programmed Magnetic Field Therapy, a non-invasive treatment used for arthritis, cancer and degenerative spinal conditions.

    The centre treats osteoarthritis, degenerative disc disease and tumours, including brain tumours, and reviews results around three months after treatment. Its Bengaluru treatment centre is at Marathahalli, on the Outer Ring Road.

    Key facts:

    • Address: #25/7, Level 2, Shree Kote Ashirwad Towers, Outer Ring Road, Doddanekundi, Marathahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560037
    • Operating since: 2006
    • Founder: Late Wing Commander (Dr) V. G. Vasishta
    • Contact: info@sbfhealthcare.com; +91 99005 48375
    • Known for: SPMF (Sequentially Programmed Magnetic Field) Therapy

    15. XCyton

    XCyton Diagnostics is a Bengaluru molecular diagnostics company founded in 1993 by physician-scientist Dr B. V. Ravi Kumar. Based in the Peenya Industrial Area, it develops diagnostic products and services with the stated aim of saving lives and preventing disabilities, and works to put India on the world map of medical diagnostics.

    Its best-known product family is the Syndrome Evaluation System, which tests for several infectious causes of a clinical syndrome in a single run. XCyton products won BioSpectrum Best Bio-Product awards in 2004 (JEV-CheX) and 2008 (Syndrome Evaluation System), and a Bio-Singapore award in 2009.

    Key facts:

    • Address: #449, 10th Cross, 4th Phase, Peenya Industrial Area, Bangalore, Karnataka 560058
    • Founded: 1993, by Dr B. V. Ravi Kumar
    • Contact: info@xcyton.com; +91 80 2836 7581-85
    • Awards: BioSpectrum Best Bio-Product 2004 and 2008; Bio-Singapore Award 2009

    16. PULSATOM Healthcare

    Pulsatom Healthcare is a Bengaluru medical-device company incorporated in February 1994, with its factory and headquarters at Yeshwantpur. It specialises in point-of-care testing devices and sells through a national sales and support network and its own online store.

    Its milestone product came in 1995, when it launched India’s first indigenous blood glucose meter, using technology developed by the National Physical Laboratory and the Centre for Biochemical Technology under CSIR. It has since launched more than seven glucometer models, alongside blood pressure monitors, nebulisers and ECG monitors.

    Key facts:

    • Address: #86D2/A, 3 Main, Industrial Suburb, Yeshwantpur, Bangalore, Karnataka 560022
    • Incorporated: February 1994
    • Contact: info@pulsatom.com; 080-2357-9166
    • Milestone: India’s first indigenous glucometer, launched 1995

    17. Velbionanotech

    Velbionanotech is a Bengaluru nanotechnology research company that worked on nanochip-based drug delivery. Business Standard reported in 2004 that its researchers were designing nanochips intended to travel to a specific organ, for example to break up kidney stones or reduce the fatty deposits that cause arteriosclerosis, as a cheaper alternative to surgery.

    The company’s chairman and chief executive at the time was Joseph Asantraj, and the company was reported to be in funding talks with ICICI Venture. Little verifiable information about the company has been published since, and its former website no longer belongs to it, so its founding and staffing details could not be confirmed for this update.

    Key facts:

    • Based: Bengaluru, Karnataka
    • Focus: nanochip drug delivery research (kidney stones, arteriosclerosis)
    • Chairman and CEO, as reported in 2004: Joseph Asantraj

    18. Span Healthcare Pvt. Ltd.

    Span Healthcare Private Limited is a Bengaluru company incorporated on 20 January 2004 and based at Yeshwantpur. It is best known in transfusion medicine: industry market reports list Span among the makers of the disposable blood bags used by blood banks and hospitals.

    Registry records place its registered office in the Industrial Suburb at Yeshwantpur and link it with Diagnostica Span Private Limited, a sister company in diagnostics. Its own website is no longer live, so its current product range and staffing could not be confirmed for this update.

    Key facts:

    • Registered office: #79, Deccan Central, 3rd Floor, 40th Main MEI Road, 2nd Stage, Industrial Suburb, Yeshwantpur, Bangalore, Karnataka 560022
    • Incorporated: 20 January 2004 (CIN U02423KA2004PTC033217)
    • Contact email (registry record): ravikumar@spanhealth.com
    • Known for: disposable blood bags and transfusion-medicine products

    19. Camson Bio Technologies Ltd.

    Camson Bio Technologies Limited is a Bengaluru agricultural biotechnology company incorporated on 19 November 1993, originally as Camson Agritech. It developed biocides, biofertilisers and hybrid seeds, described itself as India’s first wholly integrated agri-biotech company, and was listed on the BSE in 2008.

    In 2015 the company demerged its seeds business into Camson Seeds Limited, and its shares were delisted from the BSE in the same year. Ministry of Corporate Affairs records now show the company as under liquidation, and its former website is offline, so it no longer trades in its earlier form.

    Key facts:

    • Registered office (per its BSE filings): C-7, 7th Floor, Corporate Block, Golden Enclave, Old Airport Road, Bangalore, Karnataka 560017
    • Incorporated: 19 November 1993 (CIN L85110KA1993PLC014944)
    • Contact (per BSE filings): info@camsonbiotechnologies.com
    • Status: under liquidation (MCA records); delisted from BSE on 26 October 2015

    Conclusion

    Wrapping up the list of top 10 Pharmaceutical Companies in Bangalore. Comment below your personal favorite pharmacy. Provide valuable feedback on the article.

    Share this article with your buddies. Tell us more to include in this list of the best Pharmaceutical Companies in Bangalore.

excerpt.rendered: Bangalore hosts 150+ pharmaceutical companies and is often called the centre of India's pharma industry. This guide profiles the top 10 pharmaceutical companies at Bangalore, led by Biocon, and what each one is known for.

Best EPC Companies in Chennai: In today’s business landscape, companies must go beyond simply selling products or services—they must focus on delivering added value. The effectiveness of any EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) company is often measured by its operating profits, market capitalization, and the number of projects successfully completed.

Return on Investment (ROI) is a key metric businesses use to evaluate how efficiently they are using capital to generate long-term profits. The best EPC companies in Chennai help you enhance your business’s long-term profitability through strategic energy and infrastructure solutions.

An EPC company partners with organizations to improve energy performance, resulting in significant cost savings. If you’re looking to identify some of the top EPC companies in Chennai, this article will guide you. We’ve compiled a curated list of the top 10 EPC firms in the city to help you make an informed decision.

Best EPC Companies in Chennai

1. Afcons Infrastructure

AFCONS Infrastructure Limited (AFCONS) is the flagship civil engineering and construction company of the 150-year-old Shapoorji Pallonji Group. Tracing its origins to 1959, the company is headquartered in Mumbai, India.

AFCONS specializes in executing large and complex infrastructure projects both in India and internationally. Over the past five years, it has received numerous awards from various countries and leading multinational clients for successfully delivering technically challenging projects.

The company offers infrastructure services across a broad range of sectors, including marine works, roads, bridges, subways, tunnels, and onshore and offshore oil and gas platforms. AFCONS has established a global footprint and is recognized among the world’s top ten companies in the shipping infrastructure sector, known for its engineering excellence, quality standards, and timely project completion.

As of 2022, AFCONS operates in 29 countries and employs over 4,600 professionals. title.rendered: Top 30 IT Staffing Companies in USA (Updated-List)

content.rendered:
Hiring technology staff in the United States usually runs through a staffing company. The firms below range from global groups with thousands of recruiters to small regional specialists, and they do not all work the same way: some supply contract staff, some run permanent searches, and a few are freelance or nearshore networks rather than conventional agencies.

This guide profiles 30 companies that appear on US IT staffing lists, checked against each company's own website and reputable industry sources in November 2026. Several names have changed since older lists were written, and those changes are flagged in each profile: what the company is called now, where it is based, and whether IT staffing is still its core business.

Quick answer

  • For large-scale contract IT staffing, the biggest specialist names are TEKsystems, Insight Global, Kforce, Apex Systems and Randstad Digital.
  • For permanent technology hires, Robert Half, CyberCoders and Mondo focus heavily on direct placement.
  • For freelance and remote talent, Toptal runs a vetted freelance network, while Hire with Near and Heinsohn Xelerator supply nearshore teams from Latin America.
  • For healthcare IT specifically, CSI Companies and Talent Groups both centre their current offer on health systems and electronic health records.
  • Not every familiar name still does IT staffing: Aerotek moved to industrial staffing in 2021, Lucas Group now sits inside Korn Ferry, and Modis trades as Akkodis.

How IT staffing companies work

Most firms in this guide use one or more of five models. The right choice depends on whether you need people quickly for a fixed period, a permanent employee, or a team managed for you.

  • Contract staffing: the agency employs or engages the worker and bills the client an hourly or daily rate for a fixed period.
  • Contract-to-hire: the worker starts on contract, with an agreed route to a permanent job if both sides agree.
  • Direct hire / permanent placement: the agency runs the search and the client employs the person from day one, usually for a one-off fee paid by the employer.
  • Managed services and project work: the firm takes responsibility for a team or a defined piece of work, rather than supplying individuals one at a time.
  • Freelance and nearshore networks: platforms and offshore-adjacent firms supply independent specialists or teams in nearby time zones, such as Latin America for US clients.

The 30 companies at a glance

Company profiles

1. Toptal

Toptal is not a conventional agency but a freelance talent network: businesses hire independent developers, designers, finance experts, product and project managers through its platform. The company says it accepts the top 3% of freelance applicants, and it has been fully remote since it was founded, with no headquarters.

Since 2023 Toptal has grown mainly by buying smaller talent platforms, including WeLoveNoCode, Growth Collective and YouTeam, and in 2026 it added Graphite and Adeva, an IT talent network. That makes it a broader group than the original freelance marketplace, but the core offer is still on-demand independent specialists rather than contract employees supplied by an agency.

  • Founded in 2010; company-stated to have served more than 25,000 clients across more than 140 countries
  • Fully remote company with no headquarters (company-stated)
  • Model: freelance network and talent marketplace, plus consulting services through acquired brands
  • Core roles: software developers, designers, finance experts, product and project managers

2. Robert Half

Robert Half is one of the largest professional staffing firms in the United States, offering contract talent and permanent placement. Technology is one of its core specialised practices, although the firm began in finance and accounting and also covers marketing and creative, legal, administrative and human resources roles.

The company shortened its legal name from Robert Half International Inc. to Robert Half Inc. in July 2023, keeping its New York Stock Exchange ticker, RHI. Its consulting arm, Protiviti, sits alongside the staffing business and handles internal audit, risk and technology consulting.

  • Headquarters: Menlo Park, California
  • Founded in 1948 (company-stated)
  • More than 300 Robert Half locations worldwide; more than 400 including Protiviti (company-stated)
  • Models: contract staffing, permanent placement, and consulting through Protiviti

3. Express Employment Professionals

Express Employment Professionals is a franchised staffing organisation: every office is locally owned and operated. It is a generalist firm covering office and administrative work, light industrial roles, skilled trades and professional positions, so IT hiring is a secondary line handled through its professional and technical recruiting rather than a dedicated technology division.

Employers use Express for temporary and contract staff, its Evaluation Hire temp-to-hire route, direct hire, and professional and executive search. For a business that needs one local supplier for both warehouse and office staff it can be convenient; for deep technology hiring, a specialist firm is usually the better comparison.

  • Headquarters: Oklahoma City, Oklahoma
  • Founded in 1983; franchising began in 1985 (company-stated)
  • More than 870 franchise locations across the US, Canada, South Africa, Australia and New Zealand (company-stated)
  • Models: temporary, contract, temp-to-hire and direct hire, plus executive search

4. Randstad Digital (formerly Randstad Technologies)

The business older lists call Randstad Technologies now trades as Randstad Digital. Randstad launched the brand in August 2023, pulling its global digital and technology capabilities into one unit inside the Dutch Randstad group, and in May 2024 it acquired Torc, an AI-powered digital talent marketplace.

Randstad Digital supplies contingent technology staff and permanent hires, runs global talent and delivery centres, and offers managed solutions across four domains: customer experience, cloud and infrastructure, data and analytics, and digital and product engineering. Engagements can be delivered onshore, nearshore or offshore.

  • Parent: Randstad, founded in 1960 and headquartered in Diemen, the Netherlands
  • Rebranded from Randstad Technologies to Randstad Digital in August 2023
  • Acquired the Torc talent marketplace in May 2024
  • Focus areas: software engineering, cloud, data, AI and cybersecurity talent

5. Adecco

Adecco is the flagship staffing brand of the Swiss Adecco Group, and its US business is a large general staffing network rather than a technology-only firm. Technology is one of the industries it recruits for, covering flexible staffing, temp-to-hire and permanent recruitment; employers also use it for outsourcing and managed service programmes.

Buyers who mainly need engineering or digital consulting from this group are usually pointed to its sister brand Akkodis, profiled separately below. Adecco's own US site states it has more than 300 locations, over 1,200 colleagues and more than 32,000 associates on assignment.

  • Group headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland; US principal office in Jacksonville, Florida, with a North American headquarters announced for Atlanta in 2021
  • Models: temporary staffing, temp-to-hire, direct hire, outsourcing and MSP programmes
  • US figures (company-stated): 300+ locations and 32,000+ associates on assignment
  • Group brands include Akkodis, LHH and Pontoon

6. TEKsystems

TEKsystems is one of the best-known IT staffing names in the United States. Part of Allegis Group and based in Hanover, Maryland, it places technology talent from individual specialists to scaled teams, and its TEKsystems Global Services arm adds full-stack technology services: strategy, design, delivery and operations.

In January 2024 TEKsystems integrated selected business units from its sister company Aston Carter, including customer support, creative and marketing, and governance, risk and compliance work. Its own boilerplate describes a team of 80,000 working with more than 6,000 customers, including 80% of the Fortune 500.

  • Headquarters: Hanover, Maryland; part of Allegis Group
  • Began in 1983 as a contract employment business (company-stated)
  • Talent areas: cloud, data, digital, DevOps and security
  • Company-stated scale: more than 6,000 customers across North America, Europe and Asia

7. Kforce

Kforce is a Tampa-based solutions firm specialising in technology staffing, with finance and accounting as its other main practice. It works through what it calls Talent Solutions, Team Solutions and Project Solutions, covering both flexible (contract) engagements and direct hire.

The firm moved into a hybrid headquarters in Midtown Tampa in 2022. In its own press releases Kforce states that each year it provides opportunities for approximately 30,000 professionals working with approximately 3,000 clients, including a significant majority of the Fortune 500.

  • Headquarters: Tampa, Florida
  • Core lines: technology staffing and finance & accounting staffing
  • Models: contract (flex) and direct hire, plus team and project solutions
  • Company-stated: approximately 30,000 professionals and 3,000 clients a year

8. Insight Global

Insight Global began as an IT staffing firm in Atlanta and is now a broad staffing and professional services company covering healthcare, accounting and finance, engineering and government work alongside technology. Its managed services division trades as Evergreen.

The company supplies temporary, temp-to-permanent and direct-hire staff, together with managed services and consulting. Company descriptions state that it has more than 70 locations across North America, Europe and Asia and staffing capability in more than 50 countries.

  • Headquarters: Atlanta, Georgia (company-stated)
  • Models: contract, contract-to-hire, direct hire, managed services and consulting
  • Sectors: IT (including cloud, AI and data), healthcare, accounting and finance, engineering, government
  • Managed services division: Evergreen

9. Aerotek

Aerotek needs a warning label on an IT staffing list: it no longer staffs technology roles. In July 2021 its parent, Allegis Group, split Aerotek's three business units into separate companies. Aerotek kept the industrial business, placing light industrial and skilled trades staff in manufacturing, logistics, construction and aviation.

The professional division became Aston Carter, covering accounting and finance, risk and compliance, operations and customer support, while the engineering and sciences division became Actalent. A business looking for the old Aerotek's professional or engineering recruiters should approach those two brands instead.

  • Headquarters: Hanover, Maryland; part of Allegis Group
  • Split in July 2021 into Aerotek (industrial), Aston Carter (professional) and Actalent (engineering and sciences)
  • Current focus: manufacturing, logistics, construction and aviation staffing
  • Company boilerplate at the split: more than 250 offices across North America

10. CyberCoders

CyberCoders is a permanent placement recruiting firm: direct hire is its stated core model, rather than contract staffing. Founded in Irvine, California in 1999 for technology recruiting, it now also recruits across construction, engineering, accounting, sales, marketing and legal.

The firm has been a division of Everforth (formerly ASGN Incorporated) since 2013 and runs its searches on a proprietary recruiting platform it calls Cyrus. Employers use it when the goal is a full-time hire, particularly for hard-to-fill technical roles.

  • Headquarters: Irvine, California
  • Founded in 1999 (company-stated); acquired by ASGN in 2013
  • Model: permanent placement / direct hire
  • Sectors: technology, construction, engineering, accounting, sales, marketing and legal

11. Apex Systems

Apex Systems describes itself as a global technology services business, combining workforce solutions with consulting in areas such as application development, data and analytics, cloud and infrastructure, and cybersecurity. It sits in the commercial segment of Everforth (formerly ASGN Incorporated), the same group as CyberCoders.

Its 2024 press material states a presence in more than 70 markets across North America, Europe and India. The offer mixes staffing with managed services and digital transformation work, so buyers should check whether an engagement is staff supply or a contracted service.

  • Headquarters: Glen Allen, Virginia
  • Parent: Everforth (formerly ASGN Incorporated)
  • Company-stated: presence in more than 70 markets
  • Services: workforce solutions, managed services, digital innovation and transformation consulting

12. Experis

Experis is ManpowerGroup's dedicated technology brand, covering IT professional resourcing, project solutions and managed services. Its stated practice areas are business transformation, cloud and infrastructure, cyber security, digital workspace and enterprise applications, and its Experis Academy trains and reskills technology staff.

In October 2021 ManpowerGroup completed its acquisition of ettain group, a US IT staffing firm strong in financial services and healthcare IT, and folded it into Experis. For buyers, Experis is the route into ManpowerGroup when the requirement is specifically technical.

  • Parent: ManpowerGroup; Experis is its technology-only brand
  • Models: contract and permanent resourcing, project services, managed services, academy training
  • ettain group joined Experis in 2021 (acquisition completed 1 October 2021)
  • Practice areas: cloud and infrastructure, cyber security, digital workspace, enterprise applications

13. Kelly Services

Kelly Services is one of the oldest names in US staffing, founded in Detroit in 1946 and now headquartered in Troy, Michigan. Technology hiring sits inside its Kelly Science, Engineering, Technology and Telecom (SETT) division, alongside science, clinical and engineering staffing.

Kelly reshaped its portfolio recently: it sold its European staffing operations to Gi Group in January 2024, then in June 2024 completed the acquisition of Motion Recruitment Partners for $425 million, which it described as the largest acquisition in its history, adding technology, telecommunications and government staffing and consulting strength.

  • Headquarters: Troy, Michigan; listed on Nasdaq (KELYA, KELYB)
  • Founded in 1946 in Detroit (company-stated)
  • Company-stated: connects 350,000+ people a year to specialty jobs, in 80 countries
  • Acquired Motion Recruitment Partners in June 2024; sold European staffing operations to Gi Group in January 2024

14. Vaco by Highspring

Vaco's parent company rebranded from Vaco Holdings to Highspring on 31 March 2025, and the staffing business now trades as Vaco by Highspring, the group's Talent Solutions platform. Highspring, a portfolio company of Olympus Partners, presents consulting, managed services and talent solutions as one offer.

Vaco's work covers three stated areas: accounting and finance, technology and digital, and human resources and operations, through contract staffing and direct hire. The company states it has more than 45 offices worldwide and seven international delivery centres.

  • Based in the Nashville area, Tennessee (Brentwood)
  • Founded in 2002 (company-stated)
  • Parent rebranded to Highspring in March 2025; owner: Olympus Partners
  • Models: contract staffing and direct hire, with consulting and managed services at group level

15. The NineHertz

The NineHertz appears on IT staffing lists, but it is primarily a software development and AI engineering company, headquartered in Jaipur, India, with US offices listed in Georgia and Ohio. Its own services are product engineering, mobile and web development, AI consulting, cloud and DevOps work, delivered as outsourced projects.

IT staff augmentation exists only as a sub-service of its software outsourcing offer, so it is best understood as a development partner that can add engineers to a project, not as a US staffing agency with a contract workforce.

  • Headquarters: Jaipur, India; US offices listed in Georgia and Ohio
  • Founded in 2013, per its current About page
  • Core business: software development, product engineering and AI services
  • Staffing position: staff augmentation is a minor add-on, not the core model

16. Hire with Near

Hire with Near is a nearshore hiring company: it recruits staff in Latin America for US employers, handling sourcing, vetting, onboarding, payroll and compliance. It was founded in 2021 out of a venture studio in Austin and Buenos Aires; its own pages give its Texas base variously as Austin and San Antonio.

Near is not an IT-only firm. It hires across finance, accounting, sales, software engineering, AI, data, design, marketing, operations and administrative support, through direct hire, staff augmentation, recruitment process outsourcing and executive search.

  • Founded in 2021 (company-stated)
  • Model: nearshore staffing and recruiting from Latin America
  • Services: direct hire, staff augmentation, RPO and executive search
  • Coverage: 20+ industries, including software engineering and data roles

17. The Judge Group

The Judge Group is a privately owned professional services firm based in Wayne, Pennsylvania, founded in 1970. Technology staffing is its historic core: its Judge Technical Services arm dates to 1986 with a focus on IT contract staffing, and the group now also covers healthcare, engineering, finance, life sciences and manufacturing.

Beyond staffing, Judge provides technology consulting and corporate learning. It acquired Copley Consulting Group in 2021 and the executive search firm Slayton Search Partners in 2022, and launched a Judge Government Services division in 2025. Its boilerplate states more than 30 locations across the US, Canada and India.

  • Headquarters: Wayne, Pennsylvania
  • Founded in 1970 (company-stated)
  • Models: contract, contract-to-hire, direct placement, managed services, consulting and training
  • Company-stated: over 30 locations; clients include over 60 of the Fortune 100

18. ManpowerGroup

ManpowerGroup is the Milwaukee-based global staffing group behind three brands: Manpower for contingent staffing and permanent recruitment, Experis for IT resourcing and services, and Talent Solutions for recruitment process outsourcing, managed service programmes and outplacement through Right Management.

Founded in Milwaukee in 1948, the group says its brands operate in more than 70 countries and territories. Its biggest recent technology move was the acquisition of ettain group in October 2021 for $925 million, which became part of Experis.

  • Headquarters: Milwaukee, Wisconsin; listed on the NYSE (MAN)
  • Founded in 1948 (company-stated)
  • Brands: Manpower, Experis and Talent Solutions
  • Acquired ettain group in 2021, now part of Experis

19. Collabera

Collabera is a Basking Ridge, New Jersey staffing firm focused on IT and professional talent, offering staff augmentation, direct placement and what it calls talent development and transformation, plus a global remote talent platform. On its own talent page it claims access to a network of more than 14 million professionals worldwide.

Its client base is concentrated in banking, financial services and insurance, healthcare, pharma and life sciences, and telecom, media, technology and energy. The group's digital engineering business was rebranded Collabera Digital in 2022 and later integrated under its sister company Ascendion, which was spun out of Collabera the same year.

  • Headquarters: Basking Ridge, New Jersey
  • Models: staff augmentation, direct placement, global remote talent
  • Company-stated: network of 14M+ professionals worldwide
  • Sister company Ascendion spun out in 2022; the US talent business still trades as Collabera

20. PrideStaff

PrideStaff is a franchised staffing organisation headquartered in Fresno, California. Its core business is commercial staffing: administrative and office work, light industrial, manufacturing, warehouse and distribution, and skilled trades, with divisions for finance (PrideStaff Financial), pharmacy (Rx relief), insurance (Insurance Relief) and executive search (G.A. Rogers & Associates).

IT staffing is a secondary line with no dedicated technology division, so PrideStaff is a realistic option for general workforce needs rather than specialist technology hiring. The company states that it operates over 85 offices in North America and began franchising in 1995.

  • Headquarters: Fresno, California
  • Franchise model; franchising began in 1995 (company-stated)
  • Company-stated (2023): over 85 offices serving more than 5,000 clients
  • Models: temporary, temp-to-hire and direct hire, plus executive search via G.A. Rogers & Associates

21. Mondo

Mondo specialises in high-end IT, technology and digital marketing talent, supplying contract, contract-to-hire and full-time staff. It has been part of Chicago-based Addison Group since December 2018 and trades as Mondo, an Addison Group company; its international offer runs through the parent group's global delivery centre.

Roles it names include full-stack developers, UI/UX designers, AI and machine learning engineers, data engineers, cloud and cybersecurity specialists, content strategists and digital marketing analysts, which makes it a common choice for product and marketing teams as well as engineering.

  • Based in New York City, New York
  • Parent: Addison Group (acquired Mondo in December 2018)
  • Models: contract, contract-to-hire and full-time placement
  • Focus: IT, technology, AI and digital marketing talent

22. Akkodis (formerly Modis)

Older lists name this business Modis. In February 2022 the Adecco Group completed its acquisition of AKKA Technologies and combined it with Modis under a new brand, Akkodis; the US legal entity changed its name from Modis, Inc. to Akkodis, Inc. later that year. Modis should not be presented as a current brand.

Akkodis is broader than staffing: its four service lines are Consulting, Solutions, Talent and Academy, spanning digital engineering, project delivery, tech talent and upskilling. It is headquartered in Switzerland within the Adecco Group, with a US principal office in Jacksonville, Florida, and its boilerplate cites 50,000 engineers and tech consultants in over 30 countries.

  • Parent: The Adecco Group; one of its three global business units
  • Brand created in 2022 from Modis plus AKKA Technologies
  • US principal office: Jacksonville, Florida
  • Company-stated: 50,000 engineers and tech consultants in over 30 countries

23. Talent Groups (formerly Queen Consulting Group)

Queen Consulting Group no longer trades under its own name. The Boston-based IT staffing firm, founded in 2015, was acquired by Talent Group (announced in January 2023), and in September 2023 Talent Group, EdgeLink and Queen Consulting Group relaunched together as one brand: Talent Groups, based in Houston, Texas.

Queen's specialism was healthcare IT, including Epic electronic health record implementations, financial services and niche technical recruiting, and healthcare IT for providers, payers and health systems remains a stated strength of Talent Groups. The combined firm offers contract staffing, contract-to-hire, direct hire and managed services.

  • Current brand: Talent Groups; Queen Consulting Group merged into it in September 2023
  • Headquarters: Houston, Texas; Queen was founded in Boston in 2015
  • Owner: Talent Groups is a portfolio company of Osceola Capital
  • Specialism: healthcare IT and EHR implementations, plus general IT staffing

24. Epitec

Epitec is a certified women-owned staffing and workforce solutions company headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, with regional hubs in Chicago, central Illinois and Dallas. Founded in 1978, it supplies IT, engineering and professional staff on contract, contract-to-hire and direct-hire terms, and also offers employer of record and statement of work engagements in the US and Canada.

In 2026 Epitec acquired the information technology, engineering and state, local and education (SLED) staffing operations of TalentBurst, including its staff, consultants and customer relationships, extending its public-sector reach.

  • Headquarters: Southfield, Michigan
  • Founded in 1978 (company-stated); certified women-owned
  • Models: contract, contract-to-hire, direct hire, employer of record and SOW
  • Acquired TalentBurst's IT, engineering and SLED staffing operations in 2026

25. CSI Companies (CSI Tech)

The CSI Companies, based in Jacksonville, Florida, has narrowed its focus since older lists were written. CSI Tech was one of four divisions it named in 2020, but its current site presents the business primarily as healthcare IT staffing, consulting and managed services, stating plainly that its core focus is healthcare IT, including Epic and Oracle Health work.

Founded in 1994 and owned by Japan's Recruit Holdings since 2010, through RGF Staffing, CSI supplies contract, contract-to-hire and direct-hire staff. It acquired the healthcare IT consultancy MedSys Group in January 2025 and states that its staff augmentation database holds over 1.8 million candidates.

  • Headquarters: Jacksonville, Florida
  • Founded in 1994 (company-stated); part of Recruit Holdings (RGF Staffing) since 2010
  • Current core focus: healthcare IT, including EHR integration and go-live support
  • Acquired MedSys Group in January 2025

26. Peyton Resource Group (PRG)

Peyton Resource Group, shortened to PRG, is a Texas staffing and recruiting firm whose own job-board copy names Dallas/Fort Worth, San Antonio and Austin among its locations. It is a general professional staffing firm rather than an IT-only agency, covering information technology alongside finance, accounting and engineering.

Its client services cover contract engagements of any length, contract-to-hire, and direct or permanent hiring, plus managed services, project and statement of work solutions, talent acquisition strategy, an RPO service it calls RAPID RPO, onboarding support and a veterans hiring programme, Operation: HeroHire.

  • Based in Texas, USA; trades as PRG (prg-usa.com)
  • Models: contract, contract-to-hire, direct hire, managed services and RPO
  • Sectors: information technology, finance, accounting and engineering
  • Company profile copy dates the firm to 2001

27. 52 Limited

52 Limited is a boutique staffing firm in Portland, Oregon, placing technology, engineering, digital and creative talent. Its own homepage lists roles from software, frontend, full stack, data and DevOps engineers to product managers, UX and product designers, data analysts and creative directors, and it names clients including Nike, Microsoft, The North Face and Wieden+Kennedy.

The firm offers contract, contract-to-hire and direct hire engagements nationwide and states that it acts as employer of record across all 50 states, an unusual reach for a locally owned agency of its size.

  • Headquarters: Portland, Oregon
  • Established in 2005 (company-stated)
  • Models: contract, contract-to-hire and direct hire; employer of record in all 50 states
  • Focus: technology and creative talent for brands, start-ups and agencies

28. Lucas Group

Lucas Group should not be listed as an independent staffing company. Korn Ferry announced its acquisition of the Atlanta-based professional search and contract staffing firm in October 2021 and completed the deal that year; by 2022 Korn Ferry reported Lucas Group fully integrated and no longer separately identifiable, inside its Professional Search and Interim business.

Founded in 1970, Lucas Group recruited across seven specialisations, of which information technology was one, alongside accounting and finance, human resources, legal, military transition, sales and marketing, and supply chain. Enquiries for its services now route through Korn Ferry.

  • Parent: Korn Ferry (acquired 2021, since integrated)
  • Founded in 1970; headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia at acquisition
  • Model: professional search and contract staffing for middle-market businesses
  • IT position: one of seven specialisations, not the core line

29. Heinsohn Xelerator (Heinsohn Business Technology)

Heinsohn Xelerator is the name used for the nearshore offer of Heinsohn Business Technology, a Colombian technology company. It is not a US staffing agency: its US staff augmentation pages state that it works in a nearshore model, supplying software development, UX/UI design, QA testing and DevOps talent mainly from Colombia and Latin America, across US time zones from coast to coast.

Staffing is one line of a wider business that also covers software development, technology consulting, project delivery and enterprise software. On its own blog the company describes Heinsohn Xelerator as having 40+ years of experience and a team of 400+ certified engineers.

  • Company: Heinsohn Business Technology, Colombia
  • Model: nearshore staff augmentation for US clients
  • Roles: software development, UX/UI design, QA testing and DevOps engineering
  • Company-stated (blog): 40+ years of experience; 400+ certified engineers

30. Han Staffing

Han Staffing, formally HAN IT Staffing, is a New Jersey-based staffing firm whose own About page says it was born in 2012. It describes itself as women-owned and women-led and a certified Minority and Women Owned Business Enterprise (MWBE).

IT staffing is a principal line — its job postings cover roles such as UI architects, lead developers and automation testers — within a general staffing business whose founders had staffed finance, retail, hospitality, healthcare and consulting clients. It is a smaller regional firm, so it suits buyers who want a diverse-owned supplier with hands-on service.

  • Based in New Jersey, USA (Iselin, per its own job postings and directories)
  • Founded in 2012 (company-stated)
  • Certified Minority & Women Owned Business Enterprise (company-stated)
  • Focus: IT staffing within a general staffing offer

What has changed since older lists were written

Several names that appear on older versions of this list, and on many other websites, no longer exist in their old form. The changes below are covered in the profiles above and are worth knowing before you contact a firm.

  • Randstad Technologies became Randstad Digital in August 2023.
  • Modis became Akkodis in 2022, after the Adecco Group combined it with AKKA Technologies.
  • Queen Consulting Group merged into the unified Talent Groups brand in September 2023.
  • Vaco's parent rebranded to Highspring in March 2025; the staffing arm is now Vaco by Highspring.
  • Lucas Group was acquired by Korn Ferry in 2021 and integrated, so it no longer operates independently.
  • Aerotek split in 2021 and now covers industrial staffing only; its professional and engineering arms became Aston Carter and Actalent.
  • CSI Companies has refocused on healthcare IT; its CSI Tech division name dates from 2020.

How to choose an IT staffing company

  • Match the model to the need: contract staff for project peaks, direct hire for permanent roles, managed services when you want outcomes rather than individuals.
  • Check the specialism, not just the size. A firm whose core business is technology will usually screen developers better than a generalist, and vice versa for mixed office and industrial hiring.
  • Ask how candidates are vetted: technical testing, reference checks, and who interviews the worker before you see a CV.
  • Confirm the current brand and ownership. Several firms on older lists have been acquired or renamed, and contracts, insurance and payroll sit with the current legal entity.
  • Agree conversion terms up front: whether a contractor can be hired permanently, after how long, and at what fee.
  • Check geographic coverage and time zones, especially for remote roles: a nearshore team in Latin America works US hours, which an offshore team may not.
  • Ask for references in your industry and check how the agency handles payroll taxes, insurance and worker classification.

Frequently asked questions

What does an IT staffing company do?

It finds, screens and supplies technology workers for client companies. Depending on the model, the agency may employ the worker itself and bill an hourly rate (contract staffing), run a search for a permanent employee (direct hire), or manage a whole team or project (managed services). The client directs the work; the agency handles recruitment, payroll and compliance for the people it supplies.

What is the difference between contract, contract-to-hire and direct hire?

With contract staffing, the worker is engaged for a set period and is usually paid by the agency. Contract-to-hire starts the same way but includes an agreed path to permanent employment. With direct hire, the client employs the person from the start and the agency is paid a placement fee. Contract routes cost more per hour but carry less long-term commitment.

Do staffing companies charge candidates?

Reputable staffing companies are paid by the employer, not by the candidate. Jobseekers should not be asked for placement fees, training fees or payment for equipment. If a firm asks a candidate for money, treat it as a warning sign and check the company independently before sharing personal documents.

Should I use a large national firm or a specialist agency?

Large firms offer scale, national coverage and managed programmes, which suits high-volume or multi-site hiring. Specialists and regional firms often know a niche or a local market better and give more senior attention to each search. Many employers use both: a national firm for volume contract roles and a specialist for scarce senior or niche skills.

What is nearshore IT staffing?

Nearshore staffing supplies workers from nearby countries in similar time zones — for US companies, typically Latin America. Firms such as Hire with Near and Heinsohn Xelerator recruit, employ or contract the staff locally and handle payroll and compliance, while the client manages the day-to-day work. The attraction is time-zone overlap and lower cost than US hiring; the trade-offs are language, culture and employment-law differences that the agency should manage.

How do I check whether a staffing company is still trading under the same name?

Look at the company's own website and recent press releases rather than directory listings, which often lag by years. Several firms in this guide changed names or owners between 2021 and 2025 — Randstad Digital, Akkodis and Talent Groups among them — and a quick check of the current brand avoids contracting with the wrong legal entity.
