Also Worth Knowing

Venues decide the shortlist. For conferences and corporate shows, the working circuit is BIEC and Palace Grounds for large formats, the Lavelle Road and MG Road hotel ballrooms in the centre, and the Whitefield and Electronic City venues along the IT corridor. For weddings, palace hotels and resort lawns towards Devanahalli and Nandi Hills, Indiranagar and Koramangala halls, and the heritage venues around the city cover most budgets. An organiser who works your venue regularly will know its load-in rules, power backup and sound limits — in Bangalore's residential neighbourhoods, sound and closing-time rules are enforced and worth asking about early.

Season matters. Wedding demand peaks from November to February and again in the summer muhurtham windows; corporate offsites cluster around quarter-ends. Book headline firms 4–6 months out for peak dates, and expect minimum-spend conditions at premium venues. Monsoon (June to September) makes lawn events risky — insist on a written rain plan, especially for venues on the city's northern edge where the rain arrives first.

Traffic is part of the run sheet. Moving artists, décor and guests between the centre, Whitefield and Electronic City can take far longer than the map suggests at peak hours. Build the buffer into the schedule, confirm the load-in window with the venue in writing, and make sure the event-day lead has a local driver or a team that knows the corridors.

Planning in another city too? Several firms here work beyond Bangalore — Percept runs national programmes through its network offices, Wizcraft works from six Indian and overseas offices, and Tamarind Global plans destination weddings across India. Compare our lists of event management companies in Delhi, event management companies in Hyderabad and the top event management companies in Mumbai, or start from the India-wide directory.

FAQs

How much does an event management company in Bangalore charge?

There is no honest standard rate card. Management fees are quoted per event after the scope is fixed, and total budgets swing with venue, guest count, catering and production. As a rule, the management fee is a small part of a budget dominated by venue and food. Get two or three itemised quotes for the same written scope and compare line by line — this article deliberately publishes no invented prices.

How far in advance should I book?

For peak wedding dates (November to February) and large conferences, 4–6 months is sensible and headline firms book out earlier. Corporate events with standard production can often be turned around in 4–8 weeks. Large-format shows at BIEC or Palace Grounds, and events needing fabrication, should be briefed as early as the date is known, because the build, not the booking, is the long pole.

Can these companies book the venue for me?

Usually yes — most firms here will shortlist, negotiate and book venues as part of the scope, and local firms often hold working relationships with venues in their own part of the city. Make sure the venue contract and its cancellation terms are in your name, whoever negotiates them.

Do I need a Bangalore-based company for a Bangalore event?

For anything with staging, décor or permissions, a team with a real Bangalore office or headquarters is a practical advantage: local vendor rates, venue familiarity and staff who can reach the site in an hour. National firms like Percept qualify because their own website lists Bengaluru among their network offices; a purely outstation firm should show you its local production partner in writing.

What should the contract cover?

The itemised scope and exclusions, the payment schedule tied to milestones, who obtains permissions and licences, the cancellation and postponement refund ladder, the rain or backup plan for outdoor formats, and the name of the event-day lead. If a company resists putting these in writing, that is your answer.

Conclusion

Bangalore rewards specialists. Pick a live-events house for a concert or a stadium property (DNA, Phase 1), a national agency for a multi-city programme (Percept, Wizcraft, Tamarind, Laqshya), a corporate-events firm for a conference or a family day (Zeal, White Massif, V Productions, Showmaker, Erigo), a wedding studio for a wedding (Tamarind, Page3, The Tales of Tradition, Kraftstar), and an activation agency when the event is really field marketing (Erigo, Eventz Unlimited, Page3). Whichever you choose, the checks are the same: written scope, similar-event references, in-house production where it counts, and cancellation terms on paper before the advance is paid.

Researched in November 2026 from the companies' official websites. Company-stated figures are attributed to their sources and change over time — confirm current details with the company before booking.

Sneakers are the one shoe India wears everywhere — to the gym, to college, to the office, on a morning walk and on a weekend trip. The choice runs from century-old American and European sportswear houses to home-grown Indian brands that sell millions of pairs a year. This guide profiles fifteen sneaker brands sold in India — who owns them, where they come from, what each one is known for, and who it suits best.

This is an editorial selection, not an official ranking. The order below is not a league table, and we have not used sales figures or market shares to arrange it. Availability varies by city: some brands have stores in every Indian metro, while others sell mainly online or through multi-brand shops. Use the profiles to match a brand to your feet — a daily runner, a gym trainer, a walking shoe or an everyday sneaker — and check what your local stores stock.

Running, Training or Everyday: What the Names Mean

The words on the box describe what the shoe is built to do. A running shoe is made for forward motion: a cushioned midsole, a breathable mesh upper and a heel-to-toe drop that helps the foot roll through each stride. A training shoe is made for side-to-side movement in the gym: a flatter, firmer sole, a stable heel and a tougher upper that survives lunges and lateral drills.

An everyday or lifestyle sneaker is made for walking and wearing all day: comfort first, with the look of a sports shoe and none of the technical demands of a race. None of these is automatically better than the others — it is a question of use. A runner needs cushioning and grip; a gym-goer needs stability; and a daily wearer needs comfort and a style that goes with jeans. Before you pay, check the shoe's intended use, the sole and the fit.

Quick Answer: The 15 Brands at a Glance

  • Nike — the world's biggest sportswear brand, founded in 1964 as Blue Ribbon Sports; Air Jordan, Air Max and the Pegasus running range.
  • Adidas — the German three-stripes brand, founded in 1949; Ultraboost, Stan Smith, Superstar and Samba.
  • Puma — the leaping-cat brand from Herzogenaurach, founded in 1948; the Suede, RS-X and Speedcat.
  • Reebok — the English brand founded in 1958; Classic Leather, Club C and the Nano training range.
  • ASICS — the Japanese running specialist, founded in 1949 in Kobe; GEL-Kayano and GEL-Nimbus.
  • Skechers — the American comfort brand, founded in 1992; GOwalk, Arch Fit and slip-in shoes.
  • Converse — the American canvas classic, founded in 1908; the Chuck Taylor All Star.
  • Fila — the Italian brand founded in 1911; the Disruptor and a long tennis heritage.
  • Under Armour — the Baltimore performance brand, founded in 1996; HOVR and Charged running shoes.
  • Campus — the Delhi value brand launched in 2005; budget sports shoes with Air Capsule cushioning.
  • Sparx — Relaxo's sports brand, launched in 2004–05; affordable running and walking shoes across India.
  • HRX — Hrithik Roshan's fitness brand, founded in 2013; training shoes and activewear.
  • Lotto — the Italian sports brand founded in 1973; tennis and football heritage, now big on value sneakers.
  • Woodland — the Indian outdoor brand launched in 1992; tough leather sneakers and adventure shoes.
  • Asian — the Delhi budget brand making shoes since 1994; running shoes for every Indian pocket.

The Brands in Detail

1. Nike

Nike is the biggest sneaker name in the world, and its story starts in Oregon. It was founded in 1964 as Blue Ribbon Sports by track athlete Phil Knight and his coach Bill Bowerman, who sold running shoes from the boot of a car. The company renamed itself Nike in 1971, after the Greek goddess of victory, and the swoosh — designed by student Carolyn Davidson — became the most recognised mark in sport.

The range is the deepest in this guide: the Pegasus for daily running, the Air Max and Air Jordan lines for style and cushioning, and the Vomero and Invincible for long-distance comfort. Nike suits almost every buyer — a first running shoe, a gym shoe or a street-style sneaker — and its stores and authorised sellers cover every Indian metro. If you want one brand that does everything, start here.

"To bring inspiration and innovation to every athlete* in the world."

— Nike's mission, Nike (nike.com, "Our Purpose"). *Nike adds: "If you have a body, you are an athlete."

  • Brand owner: Nike, Inc.
  • Founded: 1964 as Blue Ribbon Sports, Oregon; renamed Nike in 1971
  • Known for: Air Jordan, Air Max, Pegasus, Vomero, Invincible
  • Best for: running, training and everyday sneakers from one brand

Check the price of the Nike Revolution 7 on Amazon

2. Adidas

Adidas is the German giant with the three stripes, and the oldest running-shoe name in this guide after Converse and Fila. It was founded in 1949 in Herzogenaurach, Germany, by Adolf Dassler, who had been making sports shoes since the 1920s. The three stripes began as a way to hold the shoe together, and became the most copied mark in footwear. Adidas India is run from New Delhi.

The range covers every use: the Ultraboost for cushioned running, the Runfalcon and Duramo for everyday training, and the Stan Smith, Superstar and Samba for classic street style. Adidas suits runners who want proven cushioning, and style buyers who want a sneaker that has been fashionable for fifty years. The brand's own stores and its authorised sellers are easy to find across India.

  • Brand owner: adidas AG
  • Founded: 1949, Herzogenaurach, Germany
  • Known for: Ultraboost, Stan Smith, Superstar, Samba, Runfalcon
  • Best for: cushioned running shoes and classic street sneakers

Check the price of the adidas Runfalcon 5 on Amazon

3. Puma

Puma is the other half of the Dassler family story. It was founded in 1948 in Herzogenaurach by Rudolf Dassler, the elder brother of Adidas founder Adolf Dassler, after the two brothers split their family shoe business. The leaping cat logo has been the brand's mark ever since, and Puma has dressed footballers, sprinters and pop stars for more than seventy-five years.

The range runs from the Suede — the 1968 classic that became a streetwear icon — to the RS-X and the Speedcat, plus the Velocity Nitro and Softride running shoes that lead its India range. Puma suits buyers who want sporty style with a slightly lower price than Nike or Adidas, and its stores are a common sight in Indian malls. For a first branded sneaker, Puma is often the easiest step in.

  • Brand owner: Puma SE
  • Founded: 1948, Herzogenaurach, Germany
  • Known for: Suede, RS-X, Speedcat, Velocity Nitro, Softride
  • Best for: sporty everyday sneakers and value running shoes

Check the price of the Puma Flyer Runner on Amazon

4. Reebok

Reebok is the English brand with the longest running-shoe bloodline in this guide. It was founded in 1958 in Bolton, England, by brothers Joe and Jeff Foster, whose grandfather J. W. Foster had been making running spikes since 1895. The name comes from the rhebok, a small African antelope. In 2022, Authentic Brands Group bought Reebok from Adidas, and the brand is now run from Boston, Massachusetts.

The range centres on the classics: the Classic Leather and the Club C, both white leather sneakers that have been in fashion for four decades, and the Nano range for gym training. Reebok suits buyers who want a clean, retro look at a fair price, and gym-goers who want a stable, flat training shoe. Its India stores and online sellers keep the classics in stock.

  • Brand owner: Authentic Brands Group (since 2022)
  • Founded: 1958, Bolton, England
  • Known for: Classic Leather, Club C, Nano training shoes
  • Best for: retro leather sneakers and gym training shoes

5. ASICS

ASICS is the runner's brand in this guide. It was founded in 1949 in Kobe, Japan, by Kihachiro Onitsuka, who started by making basketball shoes in his living room. The name ASICS comes from the Latin phrase "Anima Sana In Corpore Sano" — a sound mind in a sound body — and the brand has built its whole identity around running science ever since.

The range is led by the GEL-Kayano and GEL-Nimbus for long-distance running, the GEL-Cumulus for daily miles, and the Japan S and Onitsuka Tiger lines for retro style. ASICS suits serious runners first: the shoes are built around GEL cushioning and a precise fit, and they are the first choice of many Indian marathoners. If you run regularly, try ASICS before you buy anything else.

  • Brand owner: ASICS Corporation
  • Founded: 1949, Kobe, Japan
  • Known for: GEL-Kayano, GEL-Nimbus, GEL-Cumulus, Onitsuka Tiger
  • Best for: serious running and long-distance comfort

6. Skechers

Skechers is the comfort brand of this guide. It was founded in 1992 in Manhattan Beach, California, by Robert Greenberg, who had earlier co-founded the LA Gear brand. Skechers grew by making shoes that feel good the moment you put them on — soft insoles, light soles and wide fits — and it is now one of the largest footwear brands in the world.

The range is built around walking and everyday comfort: the GOwalk line for daily walking, Arch Fit for supported feet, D'Lites for chunky street style, and the slip-in designs that need no bending down to put on. Skechers suits walkers, standing workers and anyone who spends long hours on their feet — and buyers who want comfort without a sports-shoe look. Its India stores are in most big malls.

  • Brand owner: Skechers USA, Inc.
  • Founded: 1992, Manhattan Beach, California
  • Known for: GOwalk, Arch Fit, D'Lites, slip-in shoes
  • Best for: walking, standing all day and all-day comfort

Check the price of the Skechers GOwalk Flex on Amazon

7. Converse

Converse is the oldest sneaker brand in this guide, and the simplest. It was founded in 1908 in Malden, Massachusetts, by Marquis Mills Converse, who made winter footwear before turning to basketball shoes. In 1917 the company launched the All Star, and in 1923 it added the signature of basketball player Chuck Taylor — creating the Chuck Taylor All Star, the best-selling basketball shoe in history.

The range is still built on that one shoe: the Chuck Taylor All Star in high-top and low-top canvas, alongside the One Star and the Run Star for a chunkier modern look. Converse suits buyers who want a timeless canvas sneaker that goes with everything, from jeans to dresses. Nike has owned Converse since 2003, and the shoes are sold across India in its stores and online.

  • Brand owner: Converse (Nike, Inc. since 2003)
  • Founded: 1908, Malden, Massachusetts
  • Known for: Chuck Taylor All Star, One Star, Run Star
  • Best for: timeless canvas sneakers for everyday wear

8. Fila

Fila is the Italian brand with a tennis soul. It was founded in 1911 in Biella, Italy, as a maker of underwear and knitwear, and moved into sportswear in the 1970s — dressing tennis star Björn Borg and becoming the look of the tennis court. The brand is now owned by Fila Holdings of South Korea, which bought it in 2007 and rebuilt it as a global sportswear name.

The range mixes retro and modern: the Disruptor, the chunky sneaker that led the 2010s trend, and the Ray Tracer and Memory Workshift for everyday wear. Fila suits buyers who like bold, retro Italian styling at a mid-range price, and its shoes are widely sold in Indian multi-brand stores and online. For a statement sneaker that is not Nike or Adidas, Fila is a strong pick.

  • Brand owner: Fila Holdings Corp. (South Korea)
  • Founded: 1911, Biella, Italy
  • Known for: Disruptor, Ray Tracer, tennis heritage
  • Best for: bold retro sneakers and tennis style

9. Under Armour

Under Armour is the performance brand that started in a laundry basket. It was founded in 1996 in Baltimore, Maryland, by Kevin Plank, a former American football player who was tired of sweat-soaked cotton shirts. His first product was a tight, sweat-wicking HeatGear shirt, sewn in his grandmother's basement, and the brand grew from that one idea into a global sports company.

The footwear range is led by the HOVR running shoes, the Charged training shoes and the Curry Brand basketball line, built with basketball star Stephen Curry. Under Armour suits gym-goers and runners who want technical, no-nonsense performance gear, and its shoes are known for a snug, athletic fit. Its India stores are in the big metros, with online sales alongside.

  • Brand owner: Under Armour, Inc.
  • Founded: 1996, Baltimore, Maryland
  • Known for: HOVR, Charged, Curry Brand, HeatGear
  • Best for: gym training and performance running

10. Campus

Campus is the Indian brand that sells more sports shoes in India than the global giants — by pairs, not by value. It was launched in 2005 in Delhi by Hari Krishan Agarwal, who had already built the Action shoe brand in the 1980s. The idea was simple: a proper sports shoe at a price an Indian family could afford. Campus Activewear listed on the stock exchanges in May 2022, and the company is now run by his son, Nikhil Aggarwal.

The range is broad and affordable: the Air Capsule running shoes, the First and Canva everyday trainers, and the North Plus walking shoes, sold in more than 300 exclusive stores and thousands of multi-brand shops. Campus suits first-time sneaker buyers, students and families who want a comfortable, good-looking shoe without the global-brand price. It is the value pick of this guide.

  • Brand owner: Campus Activewear Ltd.
  • Launched: 2005, Delhi
  • Known for: Air Capsule running shoes, First, Canva, North Plus
  • Best for: affordable everyday sneakers for the whole family

Check the price of the Campus Atlantis running shoes on Amazon

11. Sparx

Sparx is the sports-shoe arm of Relaxo, India's largest footwear maker. Relaxo Footwears was founded in 1976 in Delhi by brothers Mukand Lal Dua and Ramesh Kumar Dua, who began with rubber slippers and built a footwear empire. The Sparx brand was launched in 2004–05, when Relaxo decided to take on the global sports brands with an Indian-priced running shoe.

The range is the SM series of mesh running shoes — the SM 500, SM 675 and their successors — plus sandals and athleisure styles, sold in Relaxo's own stores and in shoe shops in almost every Indian town. Sparx suits buyers who want a light, breathable running shoe for daily use at a genuinely low price. It is the cheapest branded sneaker in this guide, and the one most often bought as a first pair.

  • Brand owner: Relaxo Footwears Ltd.
  • Launched: 2004–05, Delhi (Relaxo founded 1976)
  • Known for: SM series mesh running shoes, sandals, athleisure
  • Best for: low-cost daily running and walking shoes

Check the price of the Sparx SM 675 running shoes on Amazon

12. HRX

HRX is India's first home-grown fitness brand, and it comes from the movies. It was founded in 2013 by actor Hrithik Roshan with Afsar Zaidi of Exceed Entertainment, built around Roshan's own fitness philosophy of becoming the best version of yourself. The brand launched exclusively on Myntra in November 2013, and Myntra took a majority stake in 2016.

The range covers activewear and footwear: training shoes, running shoes and athleisure for men and women, designed for gym workouts and everyday fitness. HRX suits young buyers who want a sporty, celebrity-backed Indian brand at a mid-range price, and it is one of the most-searched Indian fitness brands online. Its shoes are sold mainly through Myntra and Flipkart, with brand stores in some cities.

  • Brand owner: HRX (Hrithik Roshan / Exceed Entertainment; Myntra holds a majority stake)
  • Founded: 2013, India
  • Known for: training shoes, running shoes, activewear
  • Best for: gym workouts and everyday fitness style

13. Lotto

Lotto is the Italian sports brand with the cleverest logo in this guide. It was founded in 1973 in Montebelluna, Italy, by the Caberlotto family, who had been making football boots for decades. The brand began with tennis shoes — worn by Wimbledon champion John Newcombe — and its double-field logo is a tennis court and a football pitch laid over each other.

The range covers football boots, tennis shoes and everyday sneakers, and in India the brand sells value sports shoes through its own site and online marketplaces. Lotto suits buyers who want a genuine European sports brand at an Indian price, and footballers who want boots with real heritage. For a sneaker with a story behind it, Lotto is the quiet pick of this guide.

  • Brand owner: Lotto Sport Italia S.p.A.
  • Founded: 1973, Montebelluna, Italy
  • Known for: tennis shoes, football boots, everyday sneakers
  • Best for: value sports shoes with Italian heritage

14. Woodland

Woodland is the tough outdoor brand with Indian roots. It was launched in India in 1992 by the Aero Group, a Delhi leather-shoe family business run by Avtar Singh and his son Harkirat Singh, who had been exporting boots to Canada and Russia. The first product was a rugged, hand-stitched leather boot, and the first stores opened in Delhi's Connaught Place and South Extension.

The range is built for the outdoors: leather boots, trekking shoes, adventure sneakers and apparel, sold through more than 600 exclusive brand outlets across India. Woodland suits buyers who want a shoe that survives rough use — a monsoon trek, a bike ride, a construction site — and who like a rugged, outdoorsy look. It is the hardest-wearing brand in this guide.

  • Brand owner: Aero Group (Woodland)
  • Launched: 1992, India (Aero Group, Delhi)
  • Known for: leather boots, trekking shoes, adventure sneakers
  • Best for: outdoor use and tough, long-lasting shoes

15. Asian

Asian is the Delhi budget brand that became a household name on Amazon India. The Asian Group of Industries began making shoes in 1994 in New Delhi, selling affordable casual, sports and school shoes to Indian families. In 2023 the brand signed cricket legend MS Dhoni as its ambassador, and its running shoes became some of the most-bought sneakers on Indian e-commerce.

The range is value running and sports shoes — mesh uppers, light soles and bright colours — sold online and in 13 brand stores across Delhi-NCR, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat. Asian suits buyers who want a new pair of running shoes at the lowest possible price, and students and first-time buyers who need a decent shoe for daily use. It is the budget pick of this guide.

  • Brand owner: Asian Footwears (Asian Group of Industries)
  • Founded: 1994, New Delhi
  • Known for: budget running shoes, sports shoes, school shoes
  • Best for: first running shoes on a tight budget

How to Choose a Sneaker Brand

Start with the use, not the brand. A running shoe, a gym shoe and a daily sneaker are built differently, and the wrong one will hurt. Decide what you will do in the shoes most days — run, train, walk or simply wear them — and shortlist brands that make that kind of shoe well.

Get the fit right before the look. Sneaker sizes vary between brands: a UK 8 in Nike can feel different from a UK 8 in Campus or Asian. Try the shoe on in a store where you can, walk around in it, and leave a thumb's width at the toe. For running, most runners go half a size up from their daily shoe.

Match the sole to the surface. A soft, cushioned sole suits roads and long walks; a flat, firm sole suits the gym; a grippy, lugged sole suits trails and wet roads. Woodland's tough soles suit rough ground, while Skechers' soft soles suit all-day standing — the right sole matters more than the brand name.

Set a budget and stick to it. A good sneaker exists at every price in this guide, from Asian and Sparx at the low end to Nike and ASICS at the top. A higher price usually buys better cushioning and longer life, but a well-chosen budget shoe that fits beats an expensive shoe that does not. Check the current price on Amazon or in a store before you buy.

Check the seller before you buy online. Branded sneakers are widely copied, so buy from the brand's own store, its official website or an authorised seller. On Amazon India, check that the listing names the brand as the manufacturer and the seller as authorised — the listings linked in this guide do.

FAQs

Which is the best sneaker brand in India?

There is no single answer — it depends on your feet, your use and your budget. Nike is the safest all-rounder; Adidas leads on cushioned running and classic style; ASICS leads for serious runners; Skechers leads on walking comfort; and Campus, Sparx and Asian lead on value. This guide is an editorial selection to help you choose, not an official ranking.

Which brand is best for running?

For regular running, start with Nike, Adidas or ASICS: the Pegasus, Ultraboost and GEL-Kayano ranges are built for daily miles, and all three have wide ranges in Indian stores. For occasional runs on a budget, Campus and Sparx make light mesh running shoes that are good enough for short daily runs.

Which Indian sneaker brands are good on a budget?

Campus, Sparx and Asian are the three Indian value picks in this guide. Campus offers the widest range and the most stores; Sparx is the cheapest branded running shoe in most Indian towns; and Asian is the online value leader, with MS Dhoni as its ambassador. All three make comfortable daily shoes at a fraction of the global brands' prices.

Are sneakers sold on Amazon India genuine?

They can be, if you buy carefully. Choose listings where the brand is named as the manufacturer and the seller is the brand itself or an authorised seller — the six Amazon listings linked in this guide meet that test. Avoid listings with no brand name, stock photos only, or prices far below every other seller.

How do I pick the right sneaker size?

Indian shoe sizes follow the UK system, but the fit varies by brand. Measure your feet in the evening, when they are slightly swollen, and compare with the brand's size chart. Leave a thumb's width at the toe, and go half a size up for running shoes. If you are between sizes, try both in a store before ordering online.

Why does this guide not list prices?

Sneaker prices vary by city, size, colour, retailer and season, and change too often for a guide to stay accurate. We link to Amazon India for the brands sold there so you can see the current price before buying.

Conclusion

India's sneaker market rewards both loyalty and curiosity. Keep a dependable everyday brand in mind for the shoes you wear daily, back the Indian makers — Campus, Sparx, HRX, Woodland and Asian — when you want a good shoe at an Indian price, and leave room for the global classics when the occasion calls for them. Whichever brand you choose, try it on, walk in it, and check the seller before you pay.

Research note: Brand backgrounds in this guide were checked against the brands' official websites, company histories and reputable profiles in November 2026. Ranges and product names are as the brands themselves describe them; availability varies by city. If you spot an error, please contact VisitBest so we can correct it.

title.rendered: Top 20 Event Management Companies in Chennai (2026)

content.rendered:
Quick answer first, then the detailed list — 20 event management companies with a verified Chennai presence, for weddings, corporate events, conferences, exhibitions, concerts and product launches, each with its Chennai base or office and its specialisation, and what to check before you book. Where a company publishes its official logo, we show it; the rest are described, never illustrated with a substitute mark.

Chennai runs three event economies at once. Along Old Mahabalipuram Road and the Sriperumbudur–Oragadam industrial belt it is corporate India — auto and electronics plant inaugurations, dealer meets, developer conferences and some of the country's busiest factory family days, fed by the city's manufacturing base and its IT corridor. Across the city it is celebration India — weddings at palace hotels and resort lawns towards Mahabalipuram and the East Coast Road, sangeets and receptions in Adyar, Besant Nagar and Anna Nagar, and large-format concerts and film audio launches that belong to Kollywood. And at the Chennai Trade Centre in Nandambakkam it is exhibition India — trade fairs and expos that draw buyers from across South India. The best event management companies in Chennai usually specialise in one of these worlds, and this list tells you which is which.

Every company below has a real Chennai presence — a headquarters, a genuine office or substantial documented work in the city — verified against its official website in November 2026. Experience figures are the companies' own published statements, attributed as such; we have not invented fees, phone numbers, ratings or review counts. Prices in this industry are quoted per event after a scope discussion, so any company that gives you a firm rate without seeing your brief should be treated with caution.

Quick Answer: Which Chennai Event Company Should You Pick?

For national corporate and experiential programmes that include Chennai, start with Wizcraft, Percept Limited, Tamarind Global or Showtime Events (India). For corporate conferences, family days and annual meets, look at Helios Event Productions, Maze Events and Experiences, OM Events Chennai, Epix Entertainment, Elite Eventz and Curate Events. For exhibitions, trade fairs and stall fabrication, use Zak Trade Fairs & Exhibitions, JAAS Creations, Aramm Events or Showspace Events. For weddings, the shortlist splits by style: Tamarind Global and Oh Yes Events for large-format and destination celebrations, Spize Weddings & Events and Destiny Tales for design-led and South Indian weddings. For in-house production — staging, sound, lighting and LED — look at JAAS Creations, MadMaze Studios, Aramm Events and Renaissance Event Management. For product launches and brand activations, use Wizcraft, Showspace Events, Maze Events and Experiences or Epix Entertainment.

How to Choose an Event Management Company in Chennai

Chennai has hundreds of organisers, and the difference between a smooth event and a stressful one is usually paperwork, not taste. Before you pay any advance:

  • Get the scope in writing. An itemised quote that separates venue, catering, décor, sound, lighting, artists, photography and management fee. Vague lump sums are where budgets leak.
  • Ask what is produced in-house. Firms with their own staging, fabrication, AV and décor teams (several on this list have them) recover faster when something changes on the day.
  • Check references for a similar event. A company brilliant at sangeets may be new to 2,000-delegate conferences. Ask for two clients with events like yours and actually call them.
  • Confirm permissions and licences. Concerts, outdoor events and liquor service in Chennai need police, excise and venue permissions; your contract should name who obtains them.
  • Pin the cancellation and postponement terms. Weather, artist dropout and venue issues happen. The refund ladder and date-shift policy belong in the agreement, not in a WhatsApp chat.
  • Fix the payment schedule. Tie payments to milestones (booking, production start, event day, closure) and list what is excluded — GST, venue charges, generator fuel and overtime are the usual surprises.
  • Name the event-day commander. One person with authority to spend and decide on the day, with a phone number that is answered.
  • Allow for Chennai's distances and heat. Moving artists, décor and guests between the centre, OMR and Sriperumbudur can take far longer than the map suggests — build the buffer into the run sheet, not into the show. For outdoor formats, insist on a written rain plan for the north-east monsoon (October to December) and shade and hydration for summer afternoons.

Also Worth Knowing

Venues decide the shortlist. For conferences and trade fairs, the working circuit is the Chennai Trade Centre in Nandambakkam for large formats, the Anna Salai and OMR hotel ballrooms in the centre and along the IT corridor, and the Sriperumbudur and Oragadam venues near the industrial belt. For weddings, palace hotels and resort lawns towards Mahabalipuram and the East Coast Road, Adyar and Besant Nagar halls, and the heritage venues around Mylapore cover most budgets. An organiser who works your venue regularly will know its load-in rules, power backup and sound limits — in Chennai's residential neighbourhoods, sound and closing-time rules are enforced and worth asking about early.

Season matters. Wedding demand peaks from November to February and again in the summer muhurtham windows; corporate offsites cluster around quarter-ends. Book headline firms 4–6 months out for peak dates, and expect minimum-spend conditions at premium venues. The north-east monsoon (October to December) makes lawn events risky — insist on a written rain plan, especially for venues on the city's coastal edge where the rain arrives first. December is also the music season, when the city's sabhas are booked solid and artist availability tightens.

Distances are part of the run sheet. Moving artists, décor and guests between the centre, OMR and Sriperumbudur can take far longer than the map suggests at peak hours. Build the buffer into the schedule, confirm the load-in window with the venue in writing, and make sure the event-day lead has a local driver or a team that knows the corridors.

Planning in another city too? Several firms here work beyond Chennai — Percept runs national programmes through its network offices, Wizcraft works from six Indian and overseas offices, and Tamarind Global plans destination weddings across India. Compare our lists of event management companies in Delhi, event management companies in Hyderabad and the top event management companies in Mumbai, or start from the India-wide directory.

FAQs

How much does an event management company in Chennai charge?

There is no honest standard rate card. Management fees are quoted per event after the scope is fixed, and total budgets swing with venue, guest count, catering and production. As a rule, the management fee is a small part of a budget dominated by venue and food. Get two or three itemised quotes for the same written scope and compare line by line — this article deliberately publishes no invented prices.

How far in advance should I book?

For peak wedding dates (November to February) and large conferences, 4–6 months is sensible and headline firms book out earlier. Corporate events with standard production can often be turned around in 4–8 weeks. Large-format shows at the Chennai Trade Centre, and events needing fabrication, should be briefed as early as the date is known, because the build, not the booking, is the long pole.

Can these companies book the venue for me?

Usually yes — most firms here will shortlist, negotiate and book venues as part of the scope, and local firms often hold working relationships with venues in their own part of the city. Make sure the venue contract and its cancellation terms are in your name, whoever negotiates them.

Do I need a Chennai-based company for a Chennai event?

For anything with staging, décor or permissions, a team with a real Chennai office or headquarters is a practical advantage: local vendor rates, venue familiarity and staff who can reach the site in an hour. National firms like Percept qualify because their own website lists Chennai among their network offices; a purely outstation firm should show you its local production partner in writing.

What should the contract cover?

The itemised scope and exclusions, the payment schedule tied to milestones, who obtains permissions and licences, the cancellation and postponement refund ladder, the rain or backup plan for outdoor formats, and the name of the event-day lead. If a company resists putting these in writing, that is your answer.

Conclusion

Chennai rewards specialists. Pick a national agency for a multi-city programme (Percept, Wizcraft, Tamarind, Showtime for ceremonies), a Chennai-headquartered corporate-events firm for a conference or a family day (Helios, Maze, OM Events, Epix, Elite, Curate), an exhibition specialist for a trade fair or a stall (Zak, JAAS, Aramm, Showspace), a wedding studio for a wedding (Tamarind, Oh Yes, Spize, Destiny Tales), and a production house when staging and fabrication are the brief (JAAS, MadMaze, Aramm, Renaissance). Whichever you choose, the checks are the same: written scope, similar-event references, in-house production where it counts, and cancellation terms on paper before the advance is paid.

Researched in November 2026 from the companies' official websites. Company-stated figures are attributed to their sources and change over time — confirm current details with the company before booking.

title.rendered: Top 20 Event Management Companies in Kolkata (2026)

content.rendered:
Quick answer first, then the detailed list — 20 event management companies with a verified Kolkata presence, for weddings, corporate events, conferences, exhibitions, concerts and product launches, each with its Kolkata base or office and its specialisation, and what to check before you book. Where a company publishes its official logo, we show it; the rest are described, never illustrated with a substitute mark.

Kolkata runs three event economies at once. In Sector V and New Town it is corporate India — IT company annual days, dealer meets, product launches and conferences, fed by the city's IT corridor and its manufacturing base around Howrah. Across the city it is celebration India — Bengali weddings with their own rituals (Aiburo Bhaat, Gaye Holud, Saat Paak, Shubho Drishti, Bou Bhat) at palace hotels, clubs and resort lawns towards Rajarhat and the East Coast, sangeets and receptions in Salt Lake, Ballygunge and Alipore, and large-format concerts at Netaji Indoor Stadium and Nazrul Mancha. And every autumn it is festival India — Durga Puja pandals, corporate Puja events and the season's social calendar, when the city's best planners are booked months ahead. The best event management companies in Kolkata usually specialise in one of these worlds, and this list tells you which is which.

Every company below has a real Kolkata presence — a headquarters, a genuine office or substantial documented work in the city — verified against its official website in November 2026. Experience figures are the companies' own published statements, attributed as such; we have not invented fees, phone numbers, ratings or review counts. Prices in this industry are quoted per event after a scope discussion, so any company that gives you a firm rate without seeing your brief should be treated with caution.

Quick Answer: Which Kolkata Event Company Should You Pick?

For national corporate and experiential programmes that include Kolkata, start with Percept Limited, Tamarind Global or DNA Entertainment Networks. For concerts, live entertainment and large-format shows, look at DNA Entertainment Networks, Showhouse Event Management, JMD Events & Experiences and MOKSH Events. For corporate conferences, exhibitions and in-house production, use Solutions Events, The Eventful Company, One8 Event, Purple Crown Events, Eventus Event Management Co., Green Wings Events or Event Mantra Kolkata. For weddings, the shortlist splits by style: Tamarind Global and RKM Weddings for luxury and destination celebrations, Wedding Sutra, Sumangalam Weddings and Swamangalam for Bengali weddings, Wowmantic Events and Bamboocraft Events for design-led weddings and social events. For college festivals, campus events and nightlife formats, look at The Event Enchanters and JMD Events & Experiences.

How to Choose an Event Management Company in Kolkata

Kolkata has hundreds of organisers, and the difference between a smooth event and a stressful one is usually paperwork, not taste. Before you pay any advance:

  • Get the scope in writing. An itemised quote that separates venue, catering, décor, sound, lighting, artists, photography and management fee. Vague lump sums are where budgets leak.
  • Ask what is produced in-house. Firms with their own staging, fabrication, AV and décor teams (several on this list have them) recover faster when something changes on the day.
  • Check references for a similar event. A company brilliant at Bengali weddings may be new to 2,000-delegate conferences. Ask for two clients with events like yours and actually call them.
  • Confirm permissions and licences. Concerts, outdoor events and liquor service in Kolkata need police, fire and venue permissions; your contract should name who obtains them.
  • Pin the cancellation and postponement terms. Weather, artist dropout and venue issues happen. The refund ladder and date-shift policy belong in the agreement, not in a WhatsApp chat.
  • Fix the payment schedule. Tie payments to milestones (booking, production start, event day, closure) and list what is excluded — GST, venue charges, generator fuel and overtime are the usual surprises.
  • Name the event-day commander. One person with authority to spend and decide on the day, with a phone number that is answered.
  • Allow for Kolkata's distances and the monsoon. Moving artists, décor and guests between the centre, Salt Lake, New Town and the south can take far longer than the map suggests — build the buffer into the run sheet, not into the show. For outdoor formats, insist on a written rain plan for the monsoon (June to September) and shade and hydration for summer afternoons. Durga Puja season (September–October) books out early: for a Puja-season date, brief your planner at least four to six months ahead.

FAQs

How much does an event management company in Kolkata charge?

There is no standard rate. Companies on this list quote per event after a scope discussion — venue, guest count, décor, sound and lighting, artists, photography and the management fee are priced separately. Get an itemised quote in writing, ask what is excluded (GST, venue charges, generator fuel, overtime), and compare at least three quotes for the same written scope.

How far ahead should I book?

For weddings, four to six months is the usual advice, and longer for peak season (November to February) and for Durga Puja season (September–October), when the city's best planners are booked months ahead. Corporate events and birthdays can usually be arranged in three to six weeks. If your date is close, call anyway — several firms on this list keep a small buffer for urgent bookings.

Can these companies book the venue for me?

Usually yes — most firms here will shortlist, negotiate and book venues as part of the scope, and local firms often hold working relationships with venues in their own part of the city. Make sure the venue contract and its cancellation terms are in your name, whoever negotiates them.

Do I need a Kolkata-based company for a Kolkata event?

For anything with staging, décor or permissions, a team with a real Kolkata office or headquarters is a practical advantage: local vendor rates, venue familiarity and staff who can reach the site in an hour. National firms like Percept qualify because their own corporate profile lists Kolkata among their network offices; a purely outstation firm should show you its local production partner in writing.

What should the contract cover?

The itemised scope and exclusions, the payment schedule tied to milestones, who obtains permissions and licences, the cancellation and postponement refund ladder, the rain or backup plan for outdoor formats, and the name of the event-day lead. If a company resists putting these in writing, that is your answer.

Conclusion

Kolkata rewards specialists. Pick a national agency for a multi-city programme (Percept, Tamarind, DNA for live shows), a Kolkata-headquartered production house for a conference or an exhibition (Solutions, Showhouse, JMD for live formats), a corporate-events firm for a conference, an AGM or a launch (The Eventful Company, One8, Purple Crown, Eventus, Green Wings, Event Mantra), a wedding studio for a wedding (Tamarind, RKM and Sumangalam for luxury and destination, Wedding Sutra and Swamangalam for Bengali weddings, Wowmantic and Bamboocraft for design-led and traditional formats), and a campus-events firm for a college festival (The Event Enchanters, JMD). Whichever you choose, the checks are the same: written scope, similar-event references, in-house production where it counts, and cancellation terms on paper before the advance is paid.

Researched in November 2026 from the companies' official websites. Company-stated figures are attributed to their sources and change over time — confirm current details with the company before booking.

India buys its clothes from a mix of century-old global names and home-grown brands that started in a single shop or a family workshop. The choice runs from the denim that built American workwear to the kurtas that dressed a generation of Indian women, and from super-premium suiting to value shirts that sell in every small town. This guide profiles fifteen clothing brands sold in India — who owns them, where they come from, what each one is known for, and who it suits best.

This is an editorial selection, not an official ranking. The order below is not a league table, and we have not used sales figures or market shares to arrange it. Availability varies by city: some brands have stores in every Indian metro, while others sell mainly online or through multi-brand shops. Use the profiles to match a brand to your wardrobe — office formals, weekend denim, ethnic wear or everyday basics — and check what your local stores stock.

Formal, Casual or Ethnic: What the Categories Mean

Formal wear is clothing built for the office and for occasions: crisp cotton shirts, trousers, suits and blazers, usually in solid colours or quiet checks. The brands in this guide that lead on formals — Van Heusen, Louis Philippe, Allen Solly and Raymond — grew up dressing Indian offices, and their shirts are cut for a tie and a jacket. If you wear formals five days a week, fit and fabric matter more than fashion.

Casual wear is what India wears most days: jeans, T-shirts, polo shirts and casual shirts. Levi's, Flying Machine, Killer, Mufti, Pepe Jeans and Jack & Jones live here, and the difference between them is mostly about denim — the wash, the fit and the weight of the cloth. A good pair of jeans should feel comfortable on the first wear and get better with age, not fall apart after ten washes.

Ethnic and fusion wear is India's own category: kurtas, salwar suits, anarkalis and the fusion styles that mix Indian cuts with western fits. FabIndia, Biba and W lead here, and they suit buyers who want ready-to-wear ethnic clothing without a tailor. The right ethnic brand depends on the occasion — daily wear, office wear or a wedding — and on whether you prefer handloom fabrics or easy-care blends.

Quick Answer: The 15 Brands at a Glance

  • Levi's — the original jeans brand, founded in 1853 in San Francisco; the 501, the 511 Slim and the trucker jacket.
  • Peter England — the Irish-born shirt brand, founded in 1889, in India since 1997; the honest shirt for office and everyday wear.
  • Van Heusen — the American shirt name, dating to 1881, in India since 1990; formal shirts, Power Dressing and suits.
  • Allen Solly — roots in 1744 England, in India since 1993; the brand that brought Friday Dressing to Indian offices.
  • Louis Philippe — launched in India in 1989; super-premium shirts, trousers and suits under The Upper Crest.
  • Raymond — the Indian suiting house, founded in 1925; fine fabrics and The Complete Man.
  • FabIndia — founded in 1960 in New Delhi; handloom kurtas, ethnic wear and home textiles.

The Brands in Detail

1. Levi's

Levi's is the oldest clothing brand in this guide, and the one that invented the blue jean. It was founded in 1853 in San Francisco by Levi Strauss, a Bavarian immigrant who sold dry goods to gold-rush miners. In 1873, Strauss and tailor Jacob Davis patented the riveted work trouser, and the 501 — first made in 1890 — became the template every other jean has followed since.

The range in India is led by the 501 Original and the 511 Slim, plus the 512, the 505 and the trucker jacket that has been a wardrobe staple for decades. Levi's suits buyers who want jeans that last: the denim is heavy, the fits are consistent, and the brand's stores and authorised sellers cover every Indian metro. If you want one pair of jeans to wear for years, start here.

  • Brand owner: Levi Strauss & Co.
  • Founded: 1853, San Francisco; riveted jeans patented 1873
  • Known for: 501 Original, 511 Slim, trucker jackets
  • Best for: durable denim and classic jeans fits

2. Peter England

Peter England is the shirt brand that dressed a generation of young Indian professionals. It was founded in 1889 in Londonderry, Ireland, where it supplied khaki trousers to British soldiers during the Boer War. More than a century later, in 1997, Madura Garments launched the brand in India in the mid-price shirt segment — the first brand to do so at that price.

The brand grew fast: in 2000, the Aditya Birla Group acquired the worldwide rights to Peter England, and it became one of India's largest menswear brands. The range covers formal shirts, casual shirts, trousers, suits and blazers, all pitched at honest, mid-range prices. Peter England suits office-goers who want a reliable shirt that looks smart without a premium price tag.

  • Brand owner: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail (Madura Fashion & Lifestyle)
  • Founded: 1889, Londonderry, Ireland; in India since 1997
  • Known for: formal and casual shirts, trousers, suits
  • Best for: dependable office shirts at mid-range prices

3. Van Heusen

Van Heusen is the shirt brand that taught India the idea of power dressing. The Van Heusen name dates back to 1881 in the United States, where it became known for dress shirts with soft, foldable collars. In India, the brand has been sold by Madura since 1990, and it now sits in the premium tier of the Aditya Birla portfolio, above Peter England and alongside Allen Solly.

The range is built around formal shirts — crisp cottons, fine checks and stripes — plus suits, blazers and trousers for the boardroom. Van Heusen suits professionals who want a polished, authoritative look: the shirts are cut for a tie, the fabrics hold a crease, and the brand's own stores are a fixture of Indian malls. For a first serious office wardrobe, Van Heusen is a safe place to start.

  • Founded: 1881, United States; in India since 1990

4. Allen Solly

Allen Solly is the brand that loosened up the Indian office. Its roots go back to 1744, when William Hollins & Co began making clothes in Nottingham, England. Madura Garments acquired the brand in 1993 and launched it in India, where Allen Solly became famous for one idea: Friday Dressing — the relaxed, smart-casual look that let office workers dress down at the end of the week.

The range now covers casual shirts, polo shirts, T-shirts, chinos and jackets, alongside formal shirts for the rest of the week. Allen Solly suits buyers who want colour and ease in their work wardrobe: bright checks, soft fabrics and fits that are comfortable rather than stiff. If your office allows smart-casual dressing, Allen Solly is the brand built for it.

  • Brand owner: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail (Madura Fashion & Lifestyle)
  • Founded: 1744, England; in India since 1993
  • Known for: Friday Dressing, casual shirts, chinos
  • Best for: smart-casual office wear with colour

5. Louis Philippe

Louis Philippe is the most premium of the four Madura menswear brands, and the one with the most royal name. It was launched in India in 1989 by Madura Garments, named after Louis Philippe, King of France from 1830 to 1848. The brand created the super-premium segment in Indian menswear, positioning itself as The Upper Crest — the top of the range, with the promise of nothing but the best.

The range began with shirts and grew into trousers, suits, jackets, T-shirts and accessories, including the Gods and Kings collection launched in 2003. Louis Philippe suits buyers who want the finest formal wear in this guide: immaculate tailoring, premium fabrics and a fit that flatters. It is the brand to choose when the occasion — a wedding, a board meeting, a big presentation — calls for the best shirt you own.

  • Brand owner: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail (Madura Fashion & Lifestyle)
  • Founded: 1989, India; named after King Louis Philippe of France
  • Known for: premium shirts, suits, Gods and Kings collection
  • Best for: super-premium formal wear and special occasions

6. Raymond

Raymond is the Indian name in suiting. It was founded in 1925 as the Raymond Woollen Mill in Thane, near Mumbai, by the Singhania family, and it grew into India's largest maker of suiting fabric. For decades, an Indian man's first suit was cut from Raymond cloth at his local tailor — the brand's fabric, sold by the metre, was the default choice for weddings and office wear alike.

The range now covers ready-to-wear suits, shirts, trousers and blazers alongside the famous suiting and shirting fabrics, sold through Raymond's own stores and thousands of tailors. Raymond suits buyers who want a well-tailored suit at an Indian price, and grooms and professionals who trust a century-old name. Its long-running campaign line says it plainly, and the line has become part of Indian culture.

"The Complete Man"

7. FabIndia

FabIndia is the craft brand of this guide. It was founded in 1960 in New Delhi by John Bissell, an American who fell in love with Indian handloom textiles and set out to connect village weavers with city buyers. The idea was simple and radical for its time: sell hand-woven, hand-printed clothing made by rural artisans, and pay the makers fairly. More than six decades later, the brand still works that way.

The range covers kurtas, salwar suits, sarees, shirts and jackets for men and women, plus home furnishings, all in natural fabrics like cotton, silk and wool. FabIndia suits buyers who want breathable, handloom clothing with a story: the fabrics are soft, the prints are traditional, and no two hand-woven pieces are exactly alike. For summer kurtas and everyday ethnic wear, it is the natural choice.

  • Brand owner: Fabindia Ltd.
  • Founded: 1960, New Delhi, by John Bissell
  • Known for: handloom kurtas, ethnic wear, home textiles
  • Best for: breathable handloom clothing and everyday ethnic wear

8. Biba

Biba is the brand that made ready-to-wear salwar suits respectable. It was founded in 1988 in New Delhi by Meena Bindra, who started designing salwar-kameez sets from her home with an 8,000-rupee bank loan. At the time, Indian women mostly relied on tailors; Biba was among the first national brands to sell finished ethnic wear off the rack, and it pioneered the salwar-kurta revolution across the country.

The range covers kurtis, salwar suits, anarkalis, palazzos and mix-and-match sets, plus a girls' line and the value brand Rangriti. Biba also pioneered Bollywood merchandising in India, recreating costumes from films like Devdas. Biba suits buyers who want ethnic wear for every occasion — daily wear, office wear and festivals — at prices that work for a family budget.

  • Founded: 1988, New Delhi, by Meena Bindra

9. W (W for Woman)

W is the fusion brand of this guide — Indian silhouettes with a modern, western ease. It was launched in 2002 by TCNS Clothing, opening its first store in Delhi, and it pioneered the mix-and-match idea in Indian retail: buy a kurta, a bottom and a dupatta separately, and put together your own outfit. The brand's red-and-yellow W mark is now one of the most recognised logos in Indian womenswear.

The range covers kurtas, kurta sets, palazzos, skirts and dresses in easy fabrics like rayon and cotton blends, aimed at the modern Indian woman who wants ethnic wear for the office as well as for festivals. W suits buyers who like to mix pieces rather than buy fixed sets, and who want contemporary cuts without giving up Indian style. 10. U.S. Polo Assn.

U.S. Polo Assn. is the authentic brand of the sport of polo. It is the official brand of the United States Polo Association, the governing body for polo in the United States since 1890, and its double-horsemen logo is one of the most copied marks in Indian menswear. In India, the brand is licensed to Arvind Fashions, which runs its stores and online sales.

The range is led by the polo shirt — pique cotton, tipped collar, embroidered horsemen — plus T-shirts, casual shirts, jeans and jackets in a classic American sporty style. U.S. Polo Assn. suits buyers who want a clean, preppy look that works for college, weekends and casual Fridays: the polo shirt goes with jeans, chinos and shorts alike. 11. Flying Machine

Flying Machine is India's first home-grown denim brand, and a piece of Indian fashion history. It was launched in 1980 by Arvind Mills of Ahmedabad, at a time when the only jeans in India were smuggled imports. The brand became a cult favourite among young Indians through the 1980s, and its launch marked Arvind's entry into branded apparel — and the arrival of denim culture on Indian streets.

The range covers jeans, T-shirts, shirts and jackets in youthful, Italian-influenced styles; the brand was relaunched in a new avatar in 2007 with Italian designer Chicco. Flying Machine suits young buyers who want genuine denim heritage at an Indian price: the jeans are well-cut, the washes are modern, and the brand's stores are a common sight in Indian malls. For a first pair of branded jeans, it remains the classic Indian choice.

  • Brand owner: Arvind Ltd. (Arvind Lifestyle Brands)
  • Launched: 1980, Ahmedabad; India's first denim brand
  • Known for: jeans, denim jackets, youth casual wear
  • Best for: young buyers and first branded jeans

12. Killer

Killer is the rebellious denim brand of this guide. It was launched in 1989 by Kewal Kiran Clothing Ltd (KKCL) of Mumbai, set up by brothers Kewalchand, Hemant, Dilip and Vikas Jain, who had built a garment business from their father's Dadar workshop. The name was chosen deliberately: Killer stands for the killer instinct the brothers said a winner needs. The brand became one of India's largest-selling denim labels.

The range covers jeans, cargos, joggers, T-shirts, shirts and jackets for young men and women, and Killer claims a string of Indian firsts — including the first low-rise jeans in the country, launched in 2002. Killer suits buyers who want bold, edgy denim with attitude: strong washes, slim fits and street style at a mid-range price. If your style leans loud, Killer is the brand for it.

  • Brand owner: Kewal Kiran Clothing Ltd. (KKCL)
  • Launched: 1989, Mumbai
  • Known for: denim jeans, low-rise jeans, youth street style
  • Best for: bold, edgy denim for young buyers

13. Mufti

Mufti is the Indian casual brand built from a borrowed ten thousand rupees. It was founded in 1998 in Mumbai by Kamal Khushlani, who had started making shirts in 1992 under the name Mr & Mr, borrowing 10,000 rupees from his aunt and delivering clothes to retailers on his bike. The word mufti means casual dress, as opposed to a uniform — and the brand was built for men who chose individuality over conformity.

The range covers casual shirts, jeans, T-shirts, trousers and jackets, and Mufti was the first Indian brand to introduce stretch jeans for men. The brand is owned by Credo Brands Marketing Ltd and now has more than 400 exclusive stores across India. Mufti suits buyers who want comfortable, well-made casual wear with a modern Indian attitude, at a mid-premium price.

  • Brand owner: Credo Brands Marketing Ltd.
  • Founded: 1998, Mumbai, by Kamal Khushlani
  • Known for: casual shirts, stretch jeans, smart-casual menswear
  • Best for: comfortable casual wear with an Indian attitude

14. Pepe Jeans

Pepe Jeans is the London denim brand with Indian roots. It was founded in 1973 on Portobello Road in London by Nitin Shah and his brothers, who sold jeans from a market stall before building one of Europe's best-known denim labels. The handwritten Pepe Jeans script — still the brand's logo today — became a fixture of British street style in the 1970s and 1980s, and the brand has dressed generations of young Europeans since.

The range in India covers jeans, T-shirts, shirts, jackets and dresses in a British casual style, sold through Pepe Jeans India (pepejeans.in) and multi-brand stores. Pepe Jeans suits buyers who want European denim with a slightly dressier edge than the American brands: the fits are slim, the washes are refined, and the styling works as well in a cafe as on a college campus.

  • Brand owner: Pepe Jeans Group (All We Wear Group)
  • Founded: 1973, London, by Nitin Shah
  • Known for: denim jeans, British street style, the script logo
  • Best for: refined European denim and smart-casual looks

15. Jack & Jones

Jack & Jones is the Danish denim brand that grew from a single idea: jeans for young men, done properly. It was founded in 1990 in Brande, Denmark, by the Bestseller group, and it began as a denim-only label before expanding into T-shirts, shirts, jackets and accessories. The brand's clean, modern styling — simple cuts, muted colours, honest fabrics — has made it a staple of Indian malls and online fashion.

The range in India covers jeans in several fits, oversized and slim T-shirts, casual shirts and winter wear, sold through Bestseller India's own stores and online. Jack & Jones suits buyers who want fuss-free, modern menswear: the clothes are well-made, the styling is understated, and the prices sit in the mid-range. For a wardrobe refresh that does not shout, it is a reliable pick.

  • Brand owner: Bestseller
  • Founded: 1990, Brande, Denmark
  • Known for: denim jeans, T-shirts, modern menswear
  • Best for: clean, modern everyday menswear

How to Choose a Clothing Brand

Start with the occasion, not the brand. Office formals, weekend denim and festive ethnic wear are different jobs, and no single brand does all three best. Decide what you will wear most days — a shirt and trousers, jeans and a T-shirt, or a kurta — and shortlist the brands that lead in that category. A great jeans brand can still make a poor formal shirt.

Get the fit right before the label. Indian sizes vary between brands: a medium in Peter England can feel different from a medium in Jack & Jones, and a 32 waist in Levi's is not the same as a 32 in Killer. Try the garment on where you can, check the shoulder seam and the sleeve length, and remember that cotton shrinks slightly after the first wash.

Match the fabric to the weather. Cotton breathes in Indian summers, which is why the formal shirts and kurtas in this guide are mostly cotton or cotton blends. Handloom cotton from FabIndia is the coolest option in peak summer, while heavier denim suits winter and travel. Check the fabric label before you buy — a polyester shirt will feel very different from a cotton one in May.

Set a budget and stick to it. A good wardrobe exists at every price in this guide, from Biba and W at the value end of ethnic wear to Louis Philippe and Raymond at the premium end of formals. A higher price usually buys better fabric and longer life, but a well-chosen mid-range shirt that fits beats an expensive shirt that does not. Check the current price on Amazon or in a store before you buy.

Check the seller before you buy online. Branded clothing is widely copied, so buy from the brand's own store, its official website or an authorised seller. On Amazon India, check that the listing names the brand as the manufacturer and the seller as authorised — the listings linked in this guide do.

FAQs

Which is the best clothing brand in India?

There is no single answer — it depends on what you wear, where you wear it and what you can spend. Levi's leads on denim heritage; Louis Philippe leads on premium formals; Raymond leads on suiting; Biba and W lead on ethnic wear for women; and Peter England leads on value office shirts. This guide is an editorial selection to help you choose, not an official ranking.

Which brand is best for formal office wear?

For daily office wear, start with Peter England for value, Van Heusen for a polished look, Allen Solly for smart-casual offices and Louis Philippe for the most premium finish. All four belong to the same Aditya Birla portfolio and are tiered by price, so you can move up the range as your budget allows. Raymond is the pick when you need a suit rather than a shirt.

Which Indian clothing brands are good on a budget?

Peter England, Flying Machine, Killer and Mufti are the value picks in this guide, and Biba and W lead on affordable ethnic wear. Peter England offers the widest office range at mid-range prices; Flying Machine and Killer are the cheapest branded jeans in most Indian towns; and Biba's kurtis are the value leader in ready-to-wear ethnic clothing.

Which brand is best for jeans?

For heritage and durability, Levi's 501 and 511 are the benchmark. For Indian value, Flying Machine and Killer make well-cut jeans at lower prices, and Pepe Jeans and Jack & Jones offer European fits. Try the fit before the brand: a 511 Slim from Levi's feels very different from a slim fit from Killer, and the right pair is the one that fits your body.

Are clothes sold on Amazon India genuine?

They can be, if you buy carefully. Choose listings where the brand is named as the manufacturer and the seller is the brand itself or an authorised seller — the six Amazon listings linked in this guide meet that test. Avoid listings with no brand name, stock photos only, or prices far below every other seller.

Why does this guide not list prices?

Clothing prices vary by city, size, colour, retailer and season, and change too often for a guide to stay accurate. We link to Amazon India for the brands sold there so you can see the current price before buying.

Conclusion

India's clothing market rewards both loyalty and curiosity. Keep a dependable formal brand in mind for the shirts you wear to work, back the Indian makers — Raymond, FabIndia, Biba, Flying Machine, Killer and Mufti — when you want quality at an Indian price, and leave room for the global classics when the occasion calls for them. Whichever brand you choose, try it on, check the fabric, and check the seller before you pay.

India washes its hair with a remarkable mix of brands: century-old global names, salon-born professional labels, and home-grown Ayurvedic and digital-first brands. The choice runs from the anti-dandruff leader to the herbal shampoo your grandmother would recognise, and from a Paris salon formula to a Bengaluru start-up's apple cider vinegar bottle. This guide profiles fifteen shampoo brands sold in India — who owns them, where they come from, what each one is known for, and who it suits best.

This is an editorial selection, not an official ranking. The order below is not a league table, and we have not used sales figures or market shares to arrange it. Availability varies by city: some brands sell in every Indian kirana store, while others sell mainly online or through salons. Use the profiles to match a shampoo to your hair — dandruff, damage, hair fall, frizz or everyday washing — and check what your local stores stock.

Anti-Dandruff, Damage Repair or Herbal: What the Categories Mean

Anti-dandruff shampoos are built around an active ingredient that controls the flaking and itching of the scalp. Head & Shoulders leads here — its zinc pyrithione formula has been the category's benchmark since 1961 — and TRESemmé, Dove and Himalaya all make dandruff-care variants. If flakes are your main problem, start with this group and use the shampoo regularly rather than occasionally.

Damage-repair shampoos are made for hair that has been coloured, heat-styled or weakened by hard water and pollution. Pantene, Dove, L'Oréal Paris, TRESemmé, Garnier and Matrix live here, with keratin, argan oil and pro-vitamin formulas that aim to smooth, strengthen and add shine. The difference between them is mostly about the formula and the finish — some leave hair sleek, others leave it light and bouncy.

Herbal and Ayurvedic shampoos are India's own category: bhringraj, amla, reetha, onion and apple cider vinegar, sold by Himalaya, Biotique, Indulekha, Khadi Natural, Mamaearth and WOW Skin Science. They suit buyers who want plant-based ingredients and gentle, everyday formulas. The right herbal brand depends on your concern — hair fall, dandruff, dryness or dullness — and on whether you prefer a traditional Ayurvedic blend or a modern, fragrance-led formula.

Quick Answer: The 15 Brands at a Glance

  • Head & Shoulders — the anti-dandruff leader, launched in 1961 by Procter & Gamble; zinc pyrithione and the Cool Menthol range.

  • Dove — the Unilever care brand, launched in 1957; Intense Repair and Hair Fall Rescue shampoos.

  • Himalaya — the Indian herbal wellness company, founded in 1930 in Bengaluru; Anti-Hair Fall shampoo with bhringaraja.
  • Biotique — the Ayurvedic beauty brand, founded in 1992 by Vinita Jain; Bio Bhringraj and Bio Kelp shampoos.
  • Mamaearth — the toxin-free Indian brand, founded in 2016 by Ghazal and Varun Alagh; Onion shampoo for hair fall.
  • WOW Skin Science — the Bengaluru D2C brand, founded in 2014; Apple Cider Vinegar shampoo.
  • Indulekha — the Kerala Ayurvedic brand, launched in 2009, now with Hindustan Unilever; Bringha shampoo for hair fall.

The Brands in Detail

1. Head & Shoulders

Head & Shoulders is the world's best-known anti-dandruff shampoo, and the oldest specialist in this guide. It was introduced in the United States in 1961 by Procter & Gamble, after a decade of research led by chemical engineer John Parran Jr. into the dandruff-causing fungus. The active ingredient his team settled on — zinc pyrithione — is still the heart of the formula today.

The range in India is led by the Cool Menthol and Smooth & Silky variants, plus 2-in-1 shampoo-and-conditioner bottles and sachets sold in every small shop. Head & Shoulders suits anyone whose main hair problem is dandruff or an itchy scalp: use it regularly, leave it on the scalp for a minute or two, and the flakes stay away. It is the default first bottle for dandruff in Indian homes.

  • Launched: 1961, United States; zinc pyrithione formula
  • Known for: anti-dandruff care, Cool Menthol, Smooth & Silky

2. Pantene

Pantene is the Pro-V brand — and one of the oldest names in this guide. It was created in Switzerland in 1945 by Hoffmann-La Roche, which named it after panthenol, the pro-vitamin at the centre of its formula. Procter & Gamble bought the brand in 1985 and relaunched it around the world as Pantene Pro-V, the 2-in-1 shampoo and conditioner that became its signature.

The range in India is led by Total Damage Care, Hair Fall Control and the newer Miracle Rescue and Hair Science lines. Pantene suits buyers who want a reliable, everyday shampoo for damaged or falling hair: the formulas are gentle, the bottles are widely available, and the brand's Indian ambassadors have made it a household name. For damaged hair on a normal budget, it is the safe starting point.

  • Brand owner: Procter & Gamble (since 1985)
  • Founded: 1945, Switzerland; named after panthenol
  • Known for: Pro-V formula, Total Damage Care, Hair Fall Control
  • Best for: everyday care for damaged hair

3. Dove

Dove began as a bar, not a shampoo. Unilever launched it in the United States in 1957 as a beauty bar containing one-quarter moisturising cream, with the promise that it would not dry the skin the way soap did. The brand came to India in 1995 and grew into hair care in the years that followed, carrying the same gentle, moisturising idea into shampoo.

The range in India is led by Intense Repair, with keratin actives for dry and damaged hair, and Hair Fall Rescue for weak hair. Dove suits buyers with dry, frizzy or damaged hair who want a mild, everyday shampoo: the formulas are creamy, the fragrance is soft, and the brand is sold in every Indian town. For hair that feels rough after washing, Dove is the gentle fix.

  • Launched: 1957, United States; in India since 1995
  • Known for: one-quarter moisturising cream, Intense Repair, Hair Fall Rescue
  • Best for: dry, frizzy and damaged hair

4. L'Oréal Paris

L'Oréal Paris is the oldest beauty company in this guide, and the one that invented the modern shampoo. It was founded in Paris in 1909 by chemist Eugène Schueller, who began by selling a safe hair dye to local hairdressers. In 1934, Schueller launched Dop, the first soap-free shampoo — until then, women washed their hair with black soap boiled in water.

The range in India is led by Elvive Total Repair 5, Dream Lengths and the Extraordinary Clay and Hyaluron Moisture lines. L'Oréal Paris suits buyers who want salon science at a supermarket price: the formulas are research-led, the range covers every hair concern, and the brand's famous line says what it stands for.

— L'Oréal Paris tagline (lorealparis.co.in).

5. TRESemmé

TRESemmé began in the salon, not the supermarket. It was first made in 1947 by the Godefroy Manufacturing Company in New York, developed with stylist Edna L. Emmé — the name is a play on the French for "well-loved" and her surname. The line was sold only to professional salons for decades, before Alberto-Culver bought it in 1968 and Unilever acquired it in 2010.

The range in India is led by Keratin Smooth, with keratin and argan oil for straighter, shinier hair, and Hair Fall Defense. TRESemmé suits buyers who want a salon finish at home: the shampoos are made for frizz control and smooth styling, and the brand's professional heritage shows in the formulas. For frizzy hair that needs taming, it is the salon pick of this guide.

  • Known for: Keratin Smooth, Hair Fall Defense, salon heritage

6. Herbal Essences

Herbal Essences is the botanical romantic of this guide. Clairol launched it in 1971 as a single shampoo — Clairol Herbal Essence — in a clear bottle with a cartoon nature girl on the label, and it became the scent of the seventies. Procter & Gamble bought the brand from Clairol in 2001 and rebuilt it as Herbal Essences, a full range of botanical shampoos and conditioners.

The range in India is led by the bio:renew collections — Argan Oil, Coconut Milk, Aloe and the rose-scented lines — all built around plant-based ingredients and strong, memorable fragrance. Herbal Essences suits buyers who choose a shampoo by scent and feel: the formulas are light, the bottles are bright, and the fragrance lasts. For a sensory, everyday wash, it is the most cheerful brand here.

7. Himalaya

Himalaya is the Indian herbal pioneer of this guide. It was founded in 1930 by M. Manal, who had watched villagers in Burma calm restless elephants with the root of the Rauwolfia serpentina plant and set out to test the herb scientifically. The company grew from that first drug, Serpina, into India's best-known herbal wellness house, headquartered in Bengaluru.

The range in India is led by the Anti-Hair Fall shampoo with bhringaraja and palasha, plus Protein shampoo and the gentle baby shampoo. Himalaya suits buyers who trust Ayurveda and want a mild, herbal wash: the formulas are gentle enough for daily use, the ingredients are named on the pack, and the brand is sold in pharmacies as well as supermarkets. For hair fall with a herbal approach, start here.

  • Brand owner: Himalaya Wellness Company
  • Founded: 1930, by M. Manal; HQ Bengaluru
  • Known for: Anti-Hair Fall shampoo, Protein shampoo, herbal wellness
  • Best for: gentle herbal care and hair fall

8. Biotique

Biotique is the brand that took Ayurveda to the world before selling it at home. It was founded in 1992 by Vinita Jain, who had studied Ayurvedic texts in her family's tea estates in Assam and Darjeeling and then researched biotechnology in Switzerland. She built Biotique by blending the 5,000-year-old science of Ayurveda with modern biotechnology, and sold first in Switzerland before coming home to India in 1994.

The range in India is led by Bio Bhringraj therapeutic shampoo for hair fall, Bio Kelp protein shampoo and the Bio Walnut Bark and Bio Papaya lines. Biotique suits buyers who want Ayurvedic ingredients in a modern, dermatologist-tested formula: the shampoos are botanical, the fragrances are herbal, and the brand's Swiss research story is part of its identity. For Ayurveda with laboratory backing, Biotique is the pick.

  • Brand owner: Bio Veda Action Research (Biotique)
  • Founded: 1992, by Vinita Jain; HQ Noida
  • Known for: Bio Bhringraj, Bio Kelp, Advanced Ayurveda

9. Mamaearth

Mamaearth is the youngest Indian brand in this guide, and the one that grew fastest. It was founded in 2016 by husband and wife Ghazal and Varun Alagh, who could not find toxin-free baby products for their newborn son and decided to make them. The brand began with baby care, moved into skin and hair care, and became the flagship of Honasa Consumer, which listed on the Indian stock exchanges in 2023.

The range in India is led by the Onion shampoo — onion oil with plant keratin for hair fall — plus the Rosemary, Rice Water and Argan variants. Mamaearth suits buyers who want toxin-free, natural-ingredient shampoos and who shop online: the brand is digital-first, the ingredient lists are printed plainly, and the Onion shampoo is one of India's most-bought hair products. For hair fall with a modern natural formula, it is the online favourite.

  • Founded: 2016, by Ghazal and Varun Alagh; HQ Gurugram

WOW Skin Science is the Bengaluru D2C brand that made apple cider vinegar a shampoo ingredient in India. 11. Indulekha

Indulekha is the Kerala Ayurvedic brand that grew from a regional oil into a national name. It was first launched in 2009 by the Kerala-based Mosons Group as a premium Ayurvedic hair oil, and its Bringha Oil — a proprietary Ayurvedic medicine for hair fall, made with bhringraj and other herbs — carved out a loyal following across the south. Hindustan Unilever acquired the brand in 2016 and took it across India.

The range in India is led by the Bringha Hair Cleanser shampoo, the companion to the famous Bringha Oil, plus the newer scalp serums for hair growth and dandruff. Indulekha suits buyers who want a genuinely Ayurvedic, doctor-recommended approach to hair fall: the products are registered as proprietary Ayurvedic medicines, not ordinary cosmetics, and the brand's Kerala roots are part of its story. For hair fall with Ayurvedic credentials, Indulekha is the specialist.
